short_description: Chemokine-receptor; recruits naive T cells and DCs to T zone
summary_description: CCL21 binds CCR7, a Gi-coupled GPCR triggering chemotactic migration via actin remodeling. CCL21 is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells (FRCs) and lymphatic/HEV endothelium in the T-cell zone; CCR7 is expressed on naive T cells, central memory T cells, and mature DCs, guiding their homing into the paracortex and afferent lymphatics. This is a canonical, well-supported lymphoid homing axis.

short_description: Chemokine-receptor; guides T cells/DCs into T-cell zone
summary_description: CCL19 engages CCR7, a Gi-protein-coupled receptor that activates PI3K/Rac signaling to drive directed cell migration. CCL19 is secreted by FRCs (and some DCs) within the T-cell zone stroma, while CCR7 marks naive/central memory T cells and mature DCs. Together with CCL21 it organizes T-zone architecture and DC/T-cell co-localization for antigen presentation; canonical and well-established.

short_description: CD23–CD21 binding; B-cell/FDC activation and IgE regulation in follicles
summary_description: Membrane and soluble FCER2 (CD23) bind CR2 (CD21) directly, an established protein–protein interaction that co-stimulates B cells and regulates IgE production. Both are highly expressed by follicular dendritic cells and naive/mantle-zone follicular B cells, so this pair marks the B-follicle/FDC network. Spatial co-localisation is strong because both genes are concentrated in follicles; the signal is not directional ligand-to-receptor signalling in the usual sense.

short_description: Chemokine-receptor; organizes B cells and Tfh into follicles
summary_description: CXCL13 binds CXCR5, a Gi-coupled chemokine receptor driving migration toward B-cell follicles. CXCL13 is produced by follicular dendritic cells (FDCs) and some follicular stromal cells, while CXCR5 is expressed on B cells, follicular T helper (Tfh) cells, and some innate lymphoid cells. This canonical axis establishes and maintains B-cell follicles and germinal centres in lymphoid tissue.

short_description: Likely spurious; ECM protein paired with BCR signalling subunit
summary_description: Fibronectin (FN1) is an extracellular matrix glycoprotein that engages integrins, not CD79A, which is an intracellular/transmembrane signalling component of the B-cell receptor (BCR) complex with no known extracellular ligand-binding function for FN1. FN1 is made by stromal/reticular cells; CD79A is restricted to B lineage cells. This pairing is very likely a database/co-expression artefact rather than a genuine signalling interaction.

short_description: Non-canonical; intracellular intermediate filament vimentin linked to CD44
summary_description: Vimentin (VIM) is primarily a cytoplasmic intermediate filament protein, though extracellular/surface vimentin has been reported to interact with CD44 in some contexts (e.g., leukocyte adhesion, wound healing). CD44 is broadly expressed on T cells, B cells, macrophages, and stromal cells, mediating hyaluronan binding and adhesion. This interaction is weakly supported/non-canonical and may partly reflect inferred co-expression rather than a well-validated extracellular signalling axis in lymphoid tissue.

short_description: Chemokine-scavenger receptor; CCL14 decoy binding, non-signalling
summary_description: CCL14 binds ACKR1 (DARC), an atypical chemokine receptor that lacks canonical G-protein signalling and instead scavenges/transports chemokines across endothelium. ACKR1 is expressed on HEV and venular endothelial cells and erythrocytes; CCL14 is produced constitutively by various stromal/endothelial sources. This is explicitly a decoy/scavenging interaction, not a direct signalling axis, shaping local chemokine gradients rather than directly activating immune cells.

short_description: Chemokine-decoy receptor; scavenges CCL2, shapes gradients, non-signalling
summary_description: CCL2 (MCP-1) binds ACKR1 (DARC), a non-signalling atypical chemokine receptor on venular/HEV endothelium and erythrocytes that scavenges chemokines to modulate extracellular gradients rather than transducing intracellular signals. CCL2 itself is secreted by macrophages/stromal cells to recruit monocytes via CCR2. This CCL2-ACKR1 pairing is a decoy/scavenging interaction, not a direct activating signal.

short_description: Non-canonical; TIMP1 binds CD63 tetraspanin, modulates adhesion/survival
summary_description: TIMP1 (tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinase-1) can bind CD63, a tetraspanin, on the cell surface to activate integrin-associated signalling promoting cell survival/adhesion independent of MMP inhibition. CD63 is broadly expressed on macrophages, DCs, platelets, and endothelium; TIMP1 is secreted by stromal cells and macrophages during tissue remodeling. This is a less canonical, secondary signalling function for TIMP1 beyond its classical protease-inhibitory role.

short_description: Chemokine-receptor; recruits monocytes/macrophages to inflamed tissue
summary_description: CCL2 (MCP-1) binds CCR2, a Gi-coupled chemokine receptor driving monocyte/macrophage chemotaxis. CCL2 is produced by macrophages, stromal cells, and endothelium, while CCR2 is expressed on monocytes, some DC subsets, and inflammatory macrophages, supporting myeloid cell recruitment into lymphoid tissue, particularly during inflammation. This is a canonical, well-established monocyte-recruitment axis.

short_description: Chemokine-receptor; recruits Th17/DCs/B cells to mucosal-associated lymphoid tissue
summary_description: CCL20 binds CCR6, a Gi-coupled receptor mediating chemotaxis of Th17 cells, immature DCs, and B cells. CCL20 is produced by epithelial cells and some stromal/follicular cells (notably in tonsil subepithelial dome), while CCR6 marks Th17, regulatory T cells, and memory B cells, supporting mucosal immune surveillance and follicle-associated epithelium trafficking. This is a canonical, well-supported axis particularly relevant in tonsil.

short_description: Artefact; intracellular kinase LCK paired with CD8 co-receptor
summary_description: LCK is a cytoplasmic Src-family tyrosine kinase associated with the intracellular tails of CD4/CD8 and TCR-CD3, not a secreted or surface ligand capable of engaging CD8A/CD8B extracellularly. CD8 is expressed on cytotoxic T cells recognizing MHC-I. This pairing is a clear database/co-expression artefact reflecting intracellular signalling association, not a genuine ligand-receptor interaction.

short_description: Matricellular protein-syndecan; adhesion/TGF-β activation signalling
summary_description: Thrombospondin-1 (THBS1) binds syndecan-1 (SDC1/CD138), a heparan sulfate proteoglycan, mediating cell adhesion and activation of latent TGF-β, influencing cell growth and matrix interactions. THBS1 is secreted by platelets, macrophages, and stromal cells; SDC1 is highly expressed on plasma cells and some epithelial/stromal cells in lymphoid tissue, supporting plasma cell niche interactions, e.g., in medullary cords. This is a plausible, moderately supported interaction.

short_description: Non-canonical; CD90 engaging integrin CD11c/CD18 for adhesion
summary_description: THY1 (CD90), a GPI-anchored surface glycoprotein, can serve as a counter-ligand for the integrin ITGAX_ITGB2 (CD11c/CD18, complement receptor 4), mediating leukocyte adhesion rather than classical chemokine-like signalling. THY1 is expressed on stromal fibroblasts/FRCs and some endothelium; ITGAX_ITGB2 is on DCs, macrophages, and some NK cells, supporting adhesion to stroma. This is a weakly characterized, non-canonical interaction in lymphoid tissue.

short_description: Non-canonical; lymphotoxin-beta paired with CD40 instead of LTBR
summary_description: LTB (lymphotoxin-beta, part of the LTα1β2 heterotrimer) canonically signals through LTBR, not CD40; CD40 is instead the receptor for CD40LG (CD154). LTB is produced by lymphoid tissue inducer cells and B/T cells organizing secondary lymphoid structures (FDC networks, HEV maintenance), while CD40 is expressed on B cells, DCs, and macrophages for costimulatory signalling. This LTB-CD40 pairing is non-canonical/likely a database misassignment given LTB's true receptor is LTBR.

short_description: Complement fragment–adrenergic receptor; likely database artefact pairing
summary_description: C3 (complement component 3, cleaved to C3a/C3b) normally signals via complement receptors (C3AR1, CR1/2, ITGAM/ITGAX-ITGB2) and opsonizes targets for phagocytosis and B-cell co-stimulation on FDCs/macrophages. ADRA2A is a Gi-coupled adrenergic receptor on neurons/stromal/smooth muscle cells with no known complement ligand specificity, so this pairing is non-canonical and likely a database artefact arising from promiscuous ligand-receptor resource annotation rather than a genuine complement signalling axis.

short_description: MHC class I–CD8 co-receptor; CTL antigen recognition
summary_description: HLA-C (MHC-I) presents peptide to the TCR while CD8A acts as a co-receptor binding the MHC-I alpha3 domain, stabilizing the immune synapse and enhancing CD8+ T-cell signalling. HLA-C is expressed broadly on nucleated cells (including stromal/dendritic cells in lymphoid tissue) while CD8A marks cytotoxic T cells in T-cell zones and surveying germinal centres, supporting canonical antigen surveillance/cytotoxic priming.

short_description: Chemokine-receptor mismatch; CCL21 is a CCR7 ligand, not CXCR3
summary_description: CCL21 is a homeostatic chemokine that canonically signals through CCR7, driving naive T cells and mature DCs into T-cell zones via HEVs and lymphatics; it is not a validated CXCR3 ligand. CXCR3 instead binds CXCL9/10/11 on activated T cells/NK cells. This pairing is non-canonical/weakly supported and likely reflects a database cross-annotation rather than true receptor usage.

short_description: PAI-1–uPAR interaction; regulates proteolysis, adhesion, and cell migration
summary_description: SERPINE1 (PAI-1) binds PLAUR (uPAR) to inhibit uPA-mediated plasminogen activation and modulate uPAR-integrin-dependent adhesion/migration signalling. In lymphoid tissue, PAI-1 is produced by stromal/endothelial cells and macrophages, while PLAUR is expressed on myeloid cells, activated lymphocytes and stromal fibroblasts, contributing to tissue remodeling, wound healing-type responses and leukocyte trafficking rather than classical immune signalling.

short_description: Complement-opsonin/receptor; promotes efferocytosis and macrophage adhesion
summary_description: C1QA, part of the C1q complement complex, binds CD93 (C1qRp), a C-type lectin receptor promoting phagocytosis, adhesion and clearance of apoptotic cells/debris. In lymphoid tissue, C1QA is produced mainly by resident/subcapsular macrophages and DCs, while CD93 is expressed on macrophages, monocytes and endothelial cells (including HEV), supporting tissue remodeling, efferocytosis and vascular adhesion rather than classical lymphocyte signalling.

short_description: E-selectin–CD44 adhesion; supports leukocyte rolling and endothelial capture
summary_description: SELE (E-selectin), induced on activated endothelium, binds glycosylated CD44 (and other sialyl-Lewis-bearing ligands) to mediate leukocyte rolling and initial capture under flow. SELE is expressed by activated HEV/venular endothelial cells while CD44 is broadly expressed on T/B cells, monocytes and macrophages, supporting lymphocyte/myeloid recruitment into lymphoid tissue, particularly during inflammation.

short_description: MHC class I–TCR/CD3 complex; supports T-cell receptor signalling
summary_description: HLA-B presents peptide antigen to the TCR, and CD3D is a signalling subunit of the CD3 complex physically associated with the TCR, transducing activation signals rather than directly binding MHC itself. HLA-B is expressed on nucleated cells throughout lymphoid tissue; CD3D marks T cells in T-cell zones. The direct ligand-receptor link is indirect/approximate since CD3D itself does not bind MHC.

short_description: Chemokine–decoy receptor; ACKR1 scavenges CXCL2, no signalling
summary_description: CXCL2 is a neutrophil-chemoattractant CXC chemokine that normally signals through CXCR2; ACKR1 (DARC) is an atypical decoy/scavenger receptor that binds many chemokines without triggering G-protein signalling, instead regulating chemokine bioavailability and transcytosis. ACKR1 is expressed on venular/HEV endothelium and erythrocytes, so this interaction represents chemokine scavenging/presentation rather than a canonical signalling axis.

short_description: Matricellular protein–integrin; CCN1 binds ITGA5B1 to drive adhesion
summary_description: CCN1 (CYR61) is a matricellular protein that engages integrin ITGA5 (as part of ITGA5_ITGB1) to promote cell adhesion, migration and stromal remodeling signalling. In lymphoid tissue CCN1 is produced by stromal fibroblasts/FRCs and endothelial cells, while ITGA5-bearing integrins are expressed on stromal cells, fibroblasts and some leukocytes, supporting extracellular matrix organization and stromal niche maintenance.

short_description: Non-classical MHC I–CD8 co-receptor; atypical/weak canonical engagement
summary_description: HLA-F is a non-classical, often open-conformer MHC class I molecule with less well-characterized CD8 engagement compared to classical HLA-A/B/C; some reports show HLA-F interacts with ILT/KIR receptors rather than strongly with CD8A. HLA-F is expressed on activated/stressed cells including some lymphoid stromal and immune cells, and CD8A marks cytotoxic T cells, but this specific pairing is weakly supported relative to classical HLA-CD8 interactions.

short_description: Complement C1q–LRP1; mediates clearance and immunoregulation via phagocytes
summary_description: C1QB, a subunit of complement C1q, binds LRP1 (CD91) on phagocytes to promote efferocytosis/clearance of apoptotic cells and immune complexes, along with anti-inflammatory signalling. C1q is produced mainly by macrophages/DCs in lymphoid tissue, while LRP1 is expressed on macrophages, DCs and stromal cells, supporting tissue homeostasis and clearance functions in germinal centres and medullary regions.

short_description: MHC class I–CD8 co-receptor; canonical CTL antigen presentation axis
summary_description: HLA-A presents peptide antigens to the TCR while CD8A binds the MHC-I alpha3 domain as a co-receptor, stabilizing synapse formation and enhancing CD8+ T-cell activation signalling. HLA-A is broadly expressed on nucleated cells (stromal, dendritic, lymphoid) throughout lymphoid tissue, and CD8A marks cytotoxic T cells in T-cell zones, representing a canonical, well-supported interaction.

short_description: Chemokine–adrenergic receptor mismatch; likely database artefact, not canonical
summary_description: CCL20 is the sole ligand for CCR6, recruiting Th17 cells, B cells and immature DCs to mucosal and subepithelial lymphoid tissue; it has no established interaction with ADRA2A, a Gi-coupled adrenergic GPCR on neuronal/stromal/smooth muscle cells. This pairing is non-canonical and most likely reflects a database artefact rather than genuine chemokine receptor usage.

short_description: Non-classical MHC I–CD8; primarily an NK/CD94-NKG2 ligand
summary_description: HLA-E is a non-classical MHC class I molecule whose principal, well-characterized receptors are the NK cell CD94-NKG2A/C heterodimers rather than CD8A, though weak CD8 co-receptor engagement is possible given shared alpha3 domain architecture. HLA-E is expressed on stressed/activated cells across lymphoid tissue; CD8A marks cytotoxic T cells, but this pairing is secondary/weakly supported compared to its NK receptor role.

short_description: von Willebrand factor–Stabilin-2; scavenger receptor-mediated endothelial clearance
summary_description: VWF, a glycoprotein secreted by endothelial cells involved in platelet adhesion/hemostasis, is cleared via STAB2 (Stabilin-2), a scavenger receptor that mediates endocytic clearance of ligands rather than classical signalling. STAB2 is expressed on sinusoidal/lymphatic endothelial cells in lymphoid organs, so this interaction reflects endothelial scavenging/homeostatic clearance rather than an immune signalling pathway.

short_description: Sialyltransferase-lectin; modulates BCR signaling threshold in B cells
summary_description: ST6GAL1 sialylates surface glycoproteins (adding α2,6-linked sialic acid), generating ligands recognized by CD22 (Siglec-2), an inhibitory co-receptor that dampens BCR signaling. ST6GAL1 is broadly expressed (hepatocytes, secreted into serum, also B cells), while CD22 is B-cell restricted, important in follicular/GC B cell tolerance. Interaction is somewhat non-canonical as ST6GAL1 is an enzyme rather than a classical surface ligand, and CD22 engagement typically depends on sialylated glycan products rather than direct protein-protein binding, so this pairing may reflect a database inference from glycan-mediated recognition rather than direct ligand-receptor docking.

short_description: Glycoprotein-lectin; dampens immune activation via inhibitory signaling
summary_description: CD52 is a small GPI-anchored sialoglycoprotein that engages SIGLEC10, an inhibitory sialic-acid-binding receptor, delivering suppressive signals to lymphocytes and myeloid cells. CD52 is expressed broadly on T and B lymphocytes and monocytes; SIGLEC10 is found on B cells, NK cells, eosinophils, and some macrophages, contributing to peripheral tolerance and limiting excessive activation in lymphoid tissue. This is a biologically plausible but less well-characterized interaction relative to classical Siglec ligands.

short_description: Matricellular protein-scavenger receptor; anti-angiogenic, phagocytic signaling
summary_description: Thrombospondin-1 (THBS1) binds CD36, a scavenger receptor, triggering anti-angiogenic signaling and promoting apoptosis of endothelial cells, as well as facilitating phagocytic clearance of apoptotic cells/oxidized lipids. THBS1 is produced by platelets, macrophages, stromal/endothelial cells; CD36 is expressed on macrophages, dendritic cells, and endothelium, relevant to tissue remodeling and clearance in lymphoid stroma and germinal centers (tingible body macrophages).

short_description: Complement opsonin-integrin; mediates phagocytosis via complement receptor 4
summary_description: Complement C3 (cleaved to iC3b) is recognized by ITGAX (CD11c), which pairs with ITGB2 to form Complement Receptor 4 (CR4), mediating opsonophagocytosis. C3 is produced by hepatocytes and local macrophages/FDCs; ITGAX is a marker of dendritic cells and macrophages, important for antigen capture on FDCs in germinal centers and myeloid phagocytosis. Note: database may list ITGAX alone though functional receptor is the ITGAX_ITGB2 heterodimer.

short_description: Complement regulator-scavenger receptor; likely weak/non-canonical pairing
summary_description: CD59 is a GPI-anchored complement regulatory protein that inhibits membrane attack complex formation by binding C9/C8, not a known ligand for STAB1 (Stabilin-1), a scavenger receptor on macrophages/lymphatic endothelium involved in clearance of modified LDL and apoptotic cells. This pairing is weakly supported and likely reflects a database/co-expression artefact rather than a validated direct interaction; CD59's canonical role is complement regulation, not STAB1 engagement.

short_description: Selectin ligand-selectin; mediates leukocyte rolling at HEVs
summary_description: SELPLG (PSGL-1) is a sialomucin ligand recognized by L-selectin (SELL/CD62L), mediating leukocyte tethering and rolling, important for lymphocyte homing. SELPLG is expressed on leukocytes (T, B cells, myeloid cells) while SELL is expressed on naive/central memory T and B lymphocytes and is critical for binding to PNAd on high endothelial venules (HEVs), enabling lymphocyte entry into lymph nodes/tonsils.

short_description: Matrix glycoprotein-integrin; supports stromal adhesion and remodeling
summary_description: Tenascin-C (TNC) binds the α9β1 integrin complex (ITGA9_ITGB1), promoting cell adhesion, migration, and extracellular matrix remodeling, and can modulate lymphocyte trafficking signals. TNC is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells (FRCs) and stromal cells in T-zone/transitional areas; ITGA9_ITGB1 is expressed on some lymphatic endothelium, neutrophils, and stromal/epithelial cells, contributing to lymphoid stromal architecture and tissue remodeling.

short_description: Growth factor-RTK; drives dendritic cell development/homeostasis
summary_description: FLT3 ligand (FLT3LG) binds the receptor tyrosine kinase FLT3, activating downstream PI3K/MAPK/STAT5 signaling that drives proliferation and differentiation of dendritic cell progenitors and some lymphoid progenitors. FLT3LG is produced by stromal cells and activated T cells; FLT3 is expressed on conventional and plasmacytoid DC precursors and early hematopoietic progenitors, critical for DC homeostasis in lymphoid organs.

short_description: TLR-accessory complex; modulates innate/B-cell TLR-like signaling
summary_description: LY86 (MD-1) forms a complex with CD180 (RP105), a TLR4-family accessory receptor that modulates B cell and dendritic cell responses to LPS, generally acting as a negative regulator of TLR4 signaling. LY86/CD180 are co-expressed on B cells and dendritic cells/macrophages, contributing to regulation of innate activation thresholds in lymphoid follicles and marginal zones.

short_description: Costimulatory adhesion pair; strengthens immune synapse T-NK interactions
summary_description: CD48 (SLAM family) engages CD2 on T/NK cells, providing adhesion and costimulatory signals that stabilize the immunological synapse and enhance cytotoxic and helper T cell activation. CD48 is broadly expressed on hematopoietic cells (B cells, DCs, macrophages) while CD2 is on T and NK cells, important for lymphocyte-APC interactions in T zones and at sites of antigen presentation.

short_description: Collagen-adhesion receptor; supports stromal scaffolding and lymphocyte migration
summary_description: Collagen I (COL1A1) can engage CD44, a broadly expressed adhesion/matrix receptor, supporting cell adhesion, migration and retention within fibrous stroma, though CD44's primary high-affinity ligand is hyaluronan rather than collagen. COL1A1 is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells/stromal fibroblasts; CD44 is expressed on nearly all leukocytes, mediating migration through T-zone/medullary stroma. This collagen-CD44 link is less canonical than CD44-hyaluronan binding.

short_description: Matricellular ligand-endocytic receptor; clearance and signaling modulation
summary_description: Thrombospondin-1 binds LRP1 (a multifunctional endocytic/signaling receptor), mediating internalization of THBS1 complexes and modulating TGF-β activation, cell adhesion, and apoptosis pathways. THBS1 is secreted by platelets, macrophages and stromal cells; LRP1 is broadly expressed on macrophages, fibroblasts, and endothelial cells, contributing to tissue remodeling and clearance processes within lymphoid stroma.

short_description: Chemokine-receptor; non-canonical, CXCL14 not a validated CXCR4 agonist
summary_description: CXCR4 is the canonical receptor for CXCL12 (SDF-1), driving B/T cell homing and retention in lymphoid follicles/bone marrow niches; CXCL14 is an atypical chemokine without a well-established cognate GPCR, and its direct activation of CXCR4 is not well supported experimentally. This pairing is likely a weakly supported or database-inferred interaction rather than a validated signaling axis; CXCL14 is expressed by stromal/epithelial cells while CXCR4 is on B/T lymphocytes and plasmablasts.

short_description: Complement protein-interferon-induced protein; non-canonical/unlikely direct interaction
summary_description: C3 is a complement opsonin acting via classical complement receptors (CR1-4, C3aR); IFITM1 is an interferon-induced transmembrane protein primarily restricting viral entry and modulating membrane fluidity, not a recognized complement receptor. This pairing lacks established direct biochemical interaction and is likely a database artefact from co-expression in activated macrophages/lymphocytes rather than a genuine ligand-receptor signaling pair.

short_description: MHC-I-coreceptor; supports CD8 T-cell antigen recognition
summary_description: HLA-C, a classical MHC class I molecule, presents peptide antigen to the TCR while CD8 (as the CD8A/CD8B heterodimer) co-engages the MHC-I α3 domain, stabilizing the TCR-peptide-MHC complex and enhancing CD8+ T cell activation. HLA-C is expressed on nearly all nucleated cells (including FDCs, stromal cells); CD8B is restricted to cytotoxic T cells, central to antigen surveillance in T-cell zones and at sites of antigen presentation.

short_description: Adipokine/cytokine-integrin; NAMPT signals via α5β1 integrin
summary_description: NAMPT (visfatin/PBEF) acts as an extracellular cytokine-like ligand binding the α5β1 (ITGA5_ITGB1) fibronectin receptor, triggering integrin-mediated adhesion and pro-inflammatory signalling. In lymphoid tissue NAMPT is secreted by stromal cells, macrophages and activated leukocytes, while ITGA5_ITGB1 is broadly expressed on endothelium, fibroblastic reticular cells and immune cells, supporting leukocyte adhesion/migration and inflammatory crosstalk. This interaction is relatively non-canonical/less well characterized compared to classical integrin-ECM pairs and partly rests on NAMPT's secondary moonlighting role.

short_description: Chemokine-receptor; retains/recruits B/T cells, plasma cells, HSCs
summary_description: CXCL12 (SDF-1) is a homeostatic CXC chemokine that binds the GPCR CXCR4, activating Gi-protein signalling for chemotaxis, retention and survival. In secondary lymphoid organs CXCL12 is produced by stromal/reticular cells (e.g., perivascular and medullary fibroblasts, FDC-associated stroma) and endothelium, while CXCR4 is expressed on B cells, T cells, plasma cells and dendritic cells, guiding B-cell follicle/medullary positioning, plasma cell retention and germinal centre dynamics. This is a canonical, well-established axis.

short_description: Transglutaminase-integrin; non-enzymatic adhesion/co-receptor signalling via β1
summary_description: Tissue transglutaminase 2 (TGM2) can act extracellularly as a non-enzymatic adhesion co-receptor for β1 integrins, promoting cell-ECM adhesion and outside-in integrin signalling (often together with fibronectin). TGM2 is secreted by stromal fibroblasts, endothelium and macrophages, while ITGB1 is widely expressed on leukocytes and stromal cells, supporting adhesion/migration within reticular networks. This pairing is less canonical than classical integrin-ligand interactions and partly reflects TGM2's moonlighting extracellular function rather than a dedicated signalling axis.

short_description: Adhesion molecule-integrin; ICAM1 binds CD11c/CD18 for leukocyte adhesion
summary_description: ICAM1 is an Ig-superfamily adhesion ligand for the β2 integrin ITGAX_ITGB2 (CD11c/CD18, complement receptor 4), mediating firm adhesion and transendothelial migration. ICAM1 is expressed on activated endothelium (HEV), fibroblastic reticular cells and antigen-presenting cells, while ITGAX_ITGB2 is restricted to myeloid cells and dendritic cells, supporting DC-T cell interactions and leukocyte trafficking into lymphoid tissue. This is a well-supported canonical adhesion pathway.

short_description: PSGL-1-integrin; leukocyte rolling/adhesion via P-selectin ligand and β2
summary_description: SELPLG (PSGL-1) is the canonical ligand for P/E-selectin, but it can also engage β2 integrins (ITGB2, needing partner α-chain like LFA-1/Mac-1) supporting firm adhesion after initial rolling. SELPLG is expressed on leukocytes (T cells, monocytes, neutrophils) and ITGB2 similarly on leukocytes, relevant at HEV for lymphocyte homing. The listed pairing with isolated ITGB2 (lacking an alpha partner) is a simplified/non-canonical representation of a multi-step adhesion cascade and likely reflects database incompleteness.

short_description: Chemokine-adrenergic receptor; likely database artefact, non-canonical pairing
summary_description: CXCL1 is a CXC chemokine that normally signals through CXCR2, not through the adrenergic receptor ADRA2A, which binds catecholamines (norepinephrine/epinephrine) on sympathetic neuron targets. There is no established direct ligand-receptor biology between CXCL1 and ADRA2A. This pairing is very likely a database artefact/promiscuous computational prediction rather than a genuine signalling axis in lymphoid tissue.

short_description: Collagen/endostatin-integrin; ECM adhesion via α5 (needs β1 partner)
summary_description: COL18A1 (source of endostatin) is a basement-membrane collagen that can engage α5β1 integrin for cell-ECM adhesion and anti-angiogenic signalling; here only ITGA5 is listed, omitting the obligate ITGB1 partner. COL18A1 is produced by vascular/lymphatic basement membranes and stromal cells, while ITGA5-bearing cells include endothelium and fibroblastic reticular cells, relevant to vascular integrity in HEV/lymphatic sinuses. Listing ITGA5 alone is a simplified/incomplete receptor representation typical of database curation.

short_description: MHC-I-coreceptor; pMHC-I presentation to CD8 T cells
summary_description: HLA-A, a classical MHC class I molecule, presents peptide to the TCR while CD8 (as the CD8αβ heterodimer, of which CD8B is one chain) acts as a coreceptor stabilizing TCR-pMHC-I engagement and recruiting LCK for signalling. HLA-A is expressed broadly on nucleated cells including stromal and dendritic cells in lymphoid tissue, while CD8B is restricted to CD8+ T cells in T-cell zones. Listing CD8B alone (without CD8A) is a simplified representation of the CD8αβ coreceptor.

short_description: Cytokine-chemokine receptor; non-canonical, TGFB1 does not directly ligate CXCR4
summary_description: TGFB1 is a TGF-β superfamily cytokine signalling through TGFBR1/2 serine-threonine kinase receptors, not through the GPCR CXCR4, whose canonical ligand is CXCL12. TGFB1 is produced by regulatory T cells, stromal fibroblasts and macrophages, while CXCR4 is expressed on B/T cells and plasma cells; any functional link is likely indirect (TGFB1 can modulate CXCR4 expression) rather than direct receptor engagement. This pairing should be treated as non-canonical/likely a database artefact.

short_description: Non-classical MHC-I-coreceptor; weak/atypical CD8 engagement
summary_description: HLA-F is a non-classical, often intracellular/open-conformer MHC class I molecule with atypical surface expression and uncertain peptide-presentation role, distinct from classical HLA-A/B/C that robustly engage CD8 coreceptor. Any interaction with CD8B (one chain of the CD8αβ coreceptor) would be weak and non-canonical compared to classical pMHC-I-CD8 engagement. HLA-F is expressed on activated/stressed cells and some NK-interacting contexts; this pairing is weakly supported and likely reflects database inference rather than established lymphoid biology.

short_description: Basement-membrane collagen-CD93; vascular adhesion/clearance receptor on endothelium
summary_description: COL4A1 is a major basement-membrane collagen component, and CD93 (C1qRp) is a receptor implicated in cell adhesion, efferocytosis and angiogenesis that can bind extracellular matrix components including collagen. COL4A1 is produced by endothelial/stromal basement membranes, while CD93 is expressed on endothelial cells, myeloid cells and some stem cells, supporting vascular integrity and leukocyte-endothelial interactions at HEV. This is a moderately supported, less classical interaction relative to integrin-collagen axes.

short_description: Progranulin-lectin receptor; weak/atypical GRN-CLEC4M (DC-SIGNR) engagement
summary_description: Granulin (GRN/progranulin) is a secreted growth factor typically signalling via sortilin/TNFR pathways, while CLEC4M (DC-SIGNR/L-SIGN) is a C-type lectin receptor mainly recognizing glycosylated pathogen/self antigens for endocytosis. A direct GRN-CLEC4M interaction is not well characterized mechanistically. CLEC4M is expressed on sinusoidal/lymphatic endothelium and some macrophages while GRN is broadly secreted by myeloid cells and stroma; this pairing is weakly supported and likely a database-predicted rather than validated axis.

short_description: Fibrillar collagen-CD93; ECM adhesion/clearance receptor, less canonical
summary_description: COL1A1 is a major fibrillar collagen of connective tissue/stroma, and CD93 is implicated in adhesion to extracellular matrix and apoptotic cell clearance, with some reported collagen-binding activity. COL1A1 is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells and stromal fibroblasts, while CD93 is expressed on endothelium and myeloid cells, potentially supporting stromal-vascular adhesion. This interaction is less canonical than dedicated collagen receptors (e.g., integrins, DDRs) and should be considered moderately supported.

short_description: Complement C1q–Siglec-3; inhibitory myeloid sensing of C1q (moderate support)
summary_description: C1q, a secreted ABC heterotrimer (C1QA/B/C), has been reported to engage CD33 (Siglec-3) together with LAIR-1, which dampens myeloid activation. C1q is produced mainly by macrophages (subcapsular/medullary sinus) and DCs; CD33 is on monocytes and macrophages. The pairing is less canonical than C1q–CR1/CD93/LRP1, and the signal probably reflects macrophage-rich sinus regions.

short_description: Chemokine-scavenger/decoy receptor; ACKR1 (DARC) scavenges CXCL1, no signalling
summary_description: CXCL1 is an ELR+ CXC chemokine that normally signals through CXCR2 for neutrophil recruitment, while ACKR1 (DARC) is an atypical/decoy chemokine receptor that binds and scavenges chemokines without triggering G-protein signalling, instead regulating chemokine bioavailability and transcytosis. ACKR1 is expressed on venular/HEV endothelium and erythrocytes, where it shapes local chemokine gradients rather than directly activating leukocytes. This is a genuine but non-signalling scavenger interaction, not a canonical activating receptor pairing.

short_description: Complement-Siglec; macrophage-derived C1q dampens myeloid activation
summary_description: C1QA is a complement C1q subunit that can engage CD33 (Siglec-3), an inhibitory sialic-acid-binding immunoreceptor, modulating myeloid cell activation and phagocytic/clearance responses. In lymphoid tissue, C1q is produced by macrophages/DCs (e.g. in medullary sinuses, subcapsular sinus) while CD33 is expressed on myeloid cells (macrophages, monocytes), supporting a macrophage-macrophage or macrophage-self regulatory axis. This is a less canonical pairing relative to classical complement receptors (C1QA normally signals via CR1/CD93/calreticulin), so support is moderate and may reflect database inference from co-expression rather than validated direct binding.

short_description: ECM glycoprotein-integrin; fibroblast matrix signals to stromal/leukocyte adhesion
summary_description: Tenascin-C (TNC) binds integrin alpha5 (as part of ITGA5_ITGB1), activating FAK/Rho signalling that modulates cell adhesion, migration and ECM remodeling. TNC is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells (FRC) and activated stroma in lymphoid tissue, while ITGA5 is expressed on stromal cells, endothelium and migrating leukocytes, supporting T-zone/FRC network organization and cell trafficking. This is a reasonably well-supported ECM-integrin interaction relevant to stromal remodeling during immune responses.

short_description: Don't-eat-me signal; CD24 engages SIGLEC10 to inhibit phagocytosis
summary_description: CD24 is a GPI-anchored sialoglycoprotein that binds the inhibitory receptor SIGLEC10 on myeloid cells, delivering a 'don't eat me' signal that suppresses macrophage phagocytosis and inflammatory activation. CD24 is broadly expressed on B cells, DCs and epithelial/stromal cells in lymphoid organs, while SIGLEC10 is expressed on macrophages (e.g. tingible body macrophages in germinal centres, sinus macrophages). This is a well-characterized immune checkpoint-like interaction relevant to clearance of apoptotic cells in GC and sinuses.

short_description: Notch ligand-receptor; stromal/endothelial signal supporting vascular and T-cell niches
summary_description: JAG1 on a signal-sending cell engages NOTCH3 on a neighboring cell, triggering gamma-secretase-mediated release of the Notch intracellular domain and transcriptional regulation of target genes controlling cell fate and differentiation. In lymphoid tissue, JAG1 is expressed by endothelial cells and stromal/FRC populations, while NOTCH3 marks perivascular mural cells (pericytes/smooth muscle) and some stromal subsets around HEVs, supporting vascular niche maintenance and T-zone stromal organization. This is a canonical, well-supported juxtacrine signalling pair.

short_description: Chemokine-integrin crosstalk; CXCL12 may transactivate integrin adhesion, non-canonical
summary_description: CXCL12 (SDF-1) is the canonical ligand for CXCR4/ACKR3, but can indirectly promote integrin alpha5beta1-mediated adhesion via inside-out signalling rather than direct binding to ITGA5. CXCL12 is produced by stromal/reticular cells and HEVs, while ITGA5 is expressed on stromal cells and trafficking leukocytes; biologically this reflects chemokine-induced integrin activation during lymphocyte homing rather than a direct ligand-receptor interaction. This pairing is non-canonical/likely a database inference artefact rather than direct binding.

short_description: Collagen-CD44; ECM adhesion receptor supports stromal and leukocyte attachment
summary_description: Collagen I alpha2 chain (COL1A2) can bind CD44, a broadly expressed adhesion/hyaluronan receptor, contributing to cell-ECM adhesion and migratory signalling. COL1A2 is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells and stromal fibroblasts in lymphoid tissue, while CD44 is expressed on nearly all leukocytes (T, B cells, macrophages) and stromal cells, supporting lymphocyte retention/migration within the FRC network and extracellular matrix interactions. This is a moderately supported matrix-adhesion receptor interaction, though CD44's primary high-affinity ligand is hyaluronan rather than fibrillar collagen.

short_description: Matricellular protein-integrin; CCN1 engages leukocyte beta2 integrin for adhesion
summary_description: CCN1 (CYR61), a matricellular protein, can bind integrin beta2 (as part of complexes like ITGAL_ITGB2/LFA-1 or ITGAM_ITGB2/Mac-1), promoting leukocyte adhesion and inflammatory signalling. CCN1 is expressed by stromal/endothelial cells and activated fibroblasts, while ITGB2 integrins are restricted to leukocytes (T cells, macrophages, neutrophils), supporting adhesion to inflamed stroma/endothelium in lymphoid tissue. This interaction is plausible but less extensively validated than classical ITGB2 ligands (ICAM family).

short_description: Tenascin-C-syndecan; ECM glycoprotein engages heparan sulfate proteoglycan on plasma cells
summary_description: Tenascin-C binds syndecan-1 (SDC1/CD138) via heparan sulfate chains, modulating cell adhesion, migration and growth factor presentation. TNC is produced by FRCs/activated stroma, while SDC1 is prominently expressed on plasma cells and some stromal/epithelial cells, relevant to plasma cell niches in medullary cords and bone marrow-like microenvironments. This is a biologically plausible ECM-proteoglycan interaction supporting plasma cell retention in stromal niches.

short_description: Non-canonical MHC-Ib/CD8 pairing; HLA-E normally signals via NKG2A/CD94
summary_description: HLA-E is a non-classical MHC class Ib molecule whose principal receptors are the NKG2A/CD94 and NKG2C/CD94 heterodimers on NK and CD8 T cells, not CD8B directly; CD8B pairs with CD8A to form the CD8 coreceptor that binds classical MHC-I alongside TCR. HLA-E is expressed broadly (stressed epithelial/endothelial/stromal cells), while CD8B marks CD8 T cells; this pairing is non-canonical and likely reflects a database/co-expression artefact rather than a validated direct ligand-receptor interaction.

short_description: Thrombospondin-osteoprotegerin; non-canonical, THBS1 usually binds CD36/CD47/integrins
summary_description: Thrombospondin-1 (THBS1) classically signals through CD36, CD47 and integrins rather than TNFRSF11B (osteoprotegerin, a decoy receptor for RANKL), so this pairing is atypical. THBS1 is produced by platelets, macrophages and stromal cells, while TNFRSF11B/OPG is expressed by stromal/follicular dendritic-like cells and acts mainly as a soluble decoy sequestering RANKL rather than a conventional signalling receptor for THBS1. This interaction is weakly supported and likely a database-predicted rather than mechanistically validated pair.

short_description: Chemokine protease interaction; DPP4 truncates CXCL9, mostly enzymatic not receptor
summary_description: CXCL9 (MIG) is a CXCR3 ligand that can be N-terminally cleaved by DPP4 (CD26), a cell-surface peptidase, altering its chemotactic activity rather than DPP4 acting as a bona fide signalling receptor. CXCL9 is produced by stromal cells, macrophages and DCs in T zones during Th1 responses, while DPP4 is expressed on activated T cells and endothelium; this reflects a protease-substrate relationship rather than classical ligand-receptor signalling, so the designation as 'receptor' is non-canonical.

short_description: Chemokine-decoy receptor; CXCL12 scavenging by ACKR3 shapes gradients
summary_description: CXCL12 binds ACKR3 (CXCR7), an atypical/scavenger chemokine receptor that lacks classical G-protein signalling and instead internalizes and degrades CXCL12 to sculpt chemokine gradients, indirectly modulating CXCR4-dependent lymphocyte positioning. CXCL12 is produced by stromal/reticular cells and HEVs, while ACKR3 is expressed on lymphatic/blood endothelium and some stromal cells. This is a well-documented decoy receptor interaction, not canonical GPCR signalling.

short_description: Transglutaminase-integrin; TGM2 engages integrin alpha9 to support cell adhesion
summary_description: Transglutaminase 2 (TGM2) can act as a non-enzymatic co-receptor/ligand for integrin alpha9beta1, promoting cell adhesion and outside-in signalling independent of its crosslinking activity. TGM2 is expressed by stromal/endothelial and fibroblastic cells and deposited in ECM, while ITGA9 is found on lymphatic endothelium and some leukocytes, supporting lymphatic vessel interactions and matrix adhesion in lymphoid stroma. This is a moderately supported, less classical integrin-binding partner compared to ITGA9's main ligands (VCAM1, osteopontin, tenascin-C).

short_description: Chemokine-adrenergic receptor mismatch; likely database artefact, not a real pair
summary_description: CCL19 is the canonical chemokine ligand for CCR7, guiding naive T cells and DCs into T-zone via CCR7; ADRA2A is an alpha2-adrenergic GPCR for catecholamines (norepinephrine/epinephrine) and is not a chemokine receptor. CCL19 is produced by FRCs/HEVs, while ADRA2A is expressed on various stromal/neuronal-associated cells; this pairing lacks known direct binding and is almost certainly a database/co-expression artefact rather than a genuine ligand-receptor interaction.

short_description: Protease inhibitor-scavenger receptor; SERPING1 clearance via LRP1 endocytosis
summary_description: SERPING1 (C1 inhibitor) can be bound and internalized by LRP1, a multifunctional endocytic scavenger receptor, mediating clearance of protease-inhibitor complexes and regulating complement/contact pathway activity rather than triggering classical signal transduction. SERPING1 is produced by hepatocytes and some macrophages/stromal cells, while LRP1 is broadly expressed on macrophages, stromal fibroblasts and endothelium in lymphoid tissue, supporting homeostatic clearance functions. This is a legitimate but primarily scavenging/endocytic interaction rather than canonical signalling ligand-receptor engagement.

short_description: MHC-I–coreceptor; presents antigen, activates CD8+ T cells
summary_description: HLA-B (MHC class I) presents endogenous peptides to the TCR while CD8A on CD8+ T cells binds the MHC-I alpha3 domain, stabilizing the TCR-pMHC interaction and promoting cytotoxic T cell activation. HLA-B is expressed broadly by nucleated cells including stromal and immune cells in lymphoid tissue; CD8A is restricted to CD8+ T cells and some NK/dendritic subsets, mediating antigen surveillance in T zones and germinal centres.

short_description: Likely artefact: intracellular phosphatase misannotated as ligand for FCRL4
summary_description: PTPN6 (SHP-1) is a cytoplasmic protein tyrosine phosphatase involved in intracellular inhibitory signalling downstream of ITIM-bearing receptors, not a secreted or membrane ligand; it cannot engage FCRL4 extracellularly. FCRL4 is an inhibitory Fc receptor-like molecule expressed on memory/marginal zone-like B cells in mucosal and tonsillar tissue. This pairing is a database artefact arising from co-expression or pathway annotation rather than a genuine ligand-receptor interaction.

short_description: Collagen IV–CD93; supports vascular basement membrane adhesion
summary_description: COL4A2 (collagen IV, basement membrane component) binds CD93, a C-type lectin-domain receptor that promotes cell adhesion and clearance functions, with downstream effects on endothelial cell adhesion and angiogenesis. COL4A2 is produced by endothelial cells and pericytes in HEVs and lymphoid vasculature, while CD93 is expressed on endothelial cells and myeloid cells, supporting vascular integrity and leukocyte-endothelial interactions in perivascular niches.

short_description: Protease-inhibitor scavenger ligand–LRP1; mediates endocytic clearance
summary_description: Alpha-2-macroglobulin (A2M) traps proteases and is recognized by LRP1, a multifunctional endocytic scavenger receptor, triggering receptor-mediated internalization and degradation rather than classical signalling. A2M is secreted by macrophages, hepatocytes-like stromal cells and FRCs, while LRP1 is broadly expressed on macrophages, fibroblastic reticular cells, and endothelium, contributing to extracellular matrix remodeling and protease homeostasis in lymphoid stroma.

short_description: Alarmin (DAMP)–scavenger receptor; innate activation, lipid/pattern sensing
summary_description: S100A9 is a calcium-binding alarmin (often as S100A8/A9 heterodimer) that signals via pattern-recognition/scavenger receptors including CD36 to promote innate immune activation and lipid uptake. S100A9 is released by neutrophils and activated monocytes/macrophages, while CD36 is expressed on macrophages, dendritic cells and some endothelium, contributing to inflammatory and scavenging responses in lymphoid tissue; this pairing is less canonical than S100A9-TLR4/RAGE and weakly supported.

short_description: Collagen I–integrin α9β1; fibroblast/matrix adhesion signalling
summary_description: COL1A1 (fibrillar collagen I) engages the integrin heterodimer ITGA9_ITGB1, activating integrin outside-in signalling that promotes cell adhesion, migration and matrix organization. COL1A1 is secreted by fibroblastic reticular cells (FRCs) and stromal fibroblasts forming the conduit network, while ITGA9_ITGB1 is expressed on various leukocytes and stromal cells, supporting structural scaffolding and cell trafficking within T-zone reticular networks.

short_description: von Willebrand factor–LRP1; endothelial clearance and hemostasis link
summary_description: VWF is a large multimeric glycoprotein secreted by endothelial cells that mediates platelet adhesion; LRP1 acts as a clearance receptor that endocytoses VWF to regulate its plasma levels, rather than initiating classical signalling cascades. VWF is produced by HEV/vascular endothelial cells, while LRP1 is expressed on endothelium, macrophages and stromal cells, contributing to vascular homeostasis in lymphoid organ vasculature.

short_description: Lumican (SLRP)–integrin β1; stromal matrix-cell adhesion
summary_description: Lumican (LUM), a small leucine-rich proteoglycan of the ECM, interacts with integrin beta1 subunit-containing heterodimers to modulate cell adhesion, migration and matrix organization signalling. LUM is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells and stromal fibroblasts, while ITGB1 is broadly expressed on leukocytes and stromal cells, supporting structural organization of the reticular conduit network in T-cell zones.

short_description: Collagen I–integrin α5 subunit; partial integrin, weak evidence
summary_description: COL1A1 is the classical ligand for fibronectin-binding integrin alpha5beta1, but ITGA5 alone (without beta1 partner specified) is an incomplete receptor annotation, making this pairing weakly supported as listed. Biologically, COL1A1 from FRCs/stromal fibroblasts would signal through ITGA5_ITGB1 heterodimers on stromal and immune cells to support adhesion and conduit scaffolding in lymphoid T-zones; the single-subunit annotation likely reflects a database simplification.

short_description: ICAM2–LFA-1; endothelial-leukocyte adhesion and transmigration
summary_description: ICAM2 binds integrin LFA-1 (ITGAL_ITGB2), mediating firm adhesion and supporting leukocyte transendothelial migration and immune synapse formation via outside-in integrin signalling. ICAM2 is constitutively expressed on endothelial cells (including HEVs) and some lymphocytes, while LFA-1 is expressed on all leukocytes, playing a key role in lymphocyte homing through HEVs into lymph node parenchyma.

short_description: Urokinase-uPAR; proteolysis, cell migration and tissue remodeling
summary_description: PLAU (urokinase plasminogen activator) binds its GPI-anchored receptor PLAUR (uPAR), activating plasminogen to plasmin and triggering pericellular proteolysis, cell migration and ECM remodeling signalling. PLAU is secreted by macrophages, endothelial cells and stromal fibroblasts, while PLAUR is expressed on myeloid cells, endothelium and some fibroblasts, contributing to tissue remodeling and leukocyte migration within lymphoid stroma during immune responses.

short_description: CCN2/CTGF–LRP1; matricellular signalling and endocytic clearance
summary_description: CCN2 (CTGF), a matricellular protein, binds LRP1 which can act both as a clearance/endocytic receptor and co-receptor modulating growth factor signalling (e.g., TGF-beta pathway) affecting fibrosis and matrix remodeling. CCN2 is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells and activated stromal fibroblasts, while LRP1 is expressed on stromal cells, macrophages and endothelium, implicated in stromal remodeling within lymphoid tissue fibrosis/repair contexts.

short_description: Collagen III–integrin α1β1; fibroblast adhesion and matrix sensing
summary_description: COL3A1 (collagen III) engages integrin alpha1beta1, activating collagen-binding integrin signalling that regulates cell adhesion, proliferation and matrix remodeling. COL3A1 is secreted by fibroblastic reticular cells and stromal fibroblasts forming reticular fibers, while ITGA1_ITGB1 is expressed on stromal cells, some T cells and NK cells, supporting structural integrity and retention within T-cell zone conduits.

short_description: Galectin-9–CD44; immune regulation and Treg/Tim-3 modulation
summary_description: Galectin-9 (LGALS9) binds carbohydrate moieties on CD44, modulating T cell adhesion, Treg stability, and in concert with Tim-3 can dampen effector T cell responses. LGALS9 is expressed by stromal cells, macrophages, and dendritic cells, while CD44 is broadly expressed on lymphocytes, macrophages, and stromal cells, contributing to immune regulation and lymphocyte retention in germinal centres and T zones.

short_description: Adrenomedullin–ACKR3 scavenger receptor; decoy/non-signalling clearance
summary_description: Adrenomedullin (ADM) is a vasoactive peptide that can bind ACKR3 (CXCR7), an atypical scavenger receptor that internalizes ligand without classical G-protein signalling, primarily serving a decoy/clearance function (ACKR3 is best characterized for CXCL12/CXCL11 scavenging). ADM is produced by endothelial and stromal cells; ACKR3 is expressed on endothelium and some stromal/lymphatic cells. This interaction is non-canonical and likely reflects a weakly supported or decoy-receptor database entry rather than a primary signalling axis.

short_description: Adhesion ligand-integrin; endothelial VWF binds leukocyte/platelet ITGB1 integrins
summary_description: VWF is an endothelial/platelet adhesion glycoprotein that engages beta1 integrins (ITGB1 pairs with various alpha subunits) to mediate cell adhesion and signalling; functional receptor specificity usually requires the alpha partner, so ITGB1 alone is ambiguous. In lymphoid tissue VWF is produced by HEV/blood vessel endothelium, while ITGB1 is broadly expressed on leukocytes, stromal cells and platelets, supporting adhesion at vascular sites. This pairing is weakly specific since ITGB1 requires an alpha subunit for a true functional integrin receptor.

short_description: Chemokine-receptor mismatch; CXCL12 normally signals via CXCR4, not CXCR3
summary_description: CXCL12 is a homeostatic chemokine whose canonical receptor is CXCR4 (and ACKR3); CXCR3 is instead the receptor for CXCL9/10/11, so this pairing is non-canonical and likely a database/correlation artefact. CXCL12 is made by stromal/reticular cells and HEV to retain progenitors and lymphocytes, while CXCR3 is expressed on activated/effector T cells and NK cells recruited to inflamed or GC-adjacent areas. Treat this interaction with caution as it lacks strong direct ligand-receptor binding evidence.

short_description: Chemokine-receptor mismatch; CCL19 normally signals via CCR7, not CXCR3
summary_description: CCL19 is the canonical ligand for CCR7, not CXCR3 (receptor for CXCL9-11), making this a non-canonical/likely spurious pairing from spatial co-expression rather than direct binding. CCL19 is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells (FRC) in the T-cell zone to guide CCR7+ naive T cells and DCs; CXCR3 marks activated/effector T and NK cells. This result should be flagged as a probable database/co-localization artefact.

short_description: Collagen-integrin; fibrillar collagen binds ITGA1_ITGB1 for stromal adhesion
summary_description: COL1A1 (collagen I) is an ECM structural protein that binds the ITGA1_ITGB1 (alpha1beta1) integrin, triggering adhesion and outside-in signalling important for cell-matrix interactions and tissue remodeling. In lymphoid organs, collagen I is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells/stromal fibroblasts forming the conduit network, while ITGA1_ITGB1 is expressed on stromal cells, some memory T cells, and pericytes engaging this scaffold. This is a canonical, well-supported ECM-integrin interaction typical of stromal/reticular network biology.

short_description: Adhesion molecule-integrin; ICAM3 engages LFA-1 (ITGAL/ITGB2) for immune synapse
summary_description: ICAM3 (CD50) is a constitutively expressed adhesion molecule that binds ITGAL (CD11a), the alpha chain of LFA-1 (ITGAL_ITGB2), promoting leukocyte adhesion and immunological synapse formation; the beta2 partner is required for full receptor function. ICAM3 is broadly expressed on leukocytes and APCs (DCs, B cells), while ITGAL is expressed on T cells, NK cells and other leukocytes, supporting T cell-APC conjugation in T zones and GC. This is a canonical adhesion interaction, though reported here without its obligate ITGB2 partner.

short_description: Matricellular ligand-integrin subunit; thrombospondin-1 binds alpha4 integrins (with beta1/7)
summary_description: THBS1 (thrombospondin-1) is a matricellular glycoprotein that can bind ITGA4-containing integrins (alpha4beta1/alpha4beta7), modulating leukocyte adhesion, migration and immune regulation; ITGA4 alone lacks a beta partner here, so specificity is incomplete. THBS1 is secreted by activated platelets, macrophages and stromal cells, while ITGA4 is expressed on lymphocytes and monocytes trafficking through HEV and perivascular regions. Functionally plausible but weakly specified without the beta-chain partner.

short_description: Semaphorin-plexin; SEMA4A/PLXNB2 regulates DC-T cell interactions and Th differentiation
summary_description: SEMA4A is a semaphorin ligand that binds plexin-B2 (PLXNB2), activating RhoGTPase signalling involved in cell migration, DC-T cell interaction, and Th1/Th17 differentiation. In lymphoid tissue SEMA4A is expressed on dendritic cells and activated T cells, while PLXNB2 is expressed on T cells, B cells and stromal/epithelial-like cells, supporting immune cell crosstalk in T zones and germinal centers. This is a well-supported, canonical semaphorin-plexin signalling axis.

short_description: ECM glycoprotein-integrin; tenascin-C binding to alpha7 integrin is atypical/weak
summary_description: Tenascin-C (TNC) is an ECM glycoprotein typically signalling through integrins like alpha9beta1, alphavbeta3/6 or alpha8beta1; ITGA7 (alpha7, normally pairing with beta1 in muscle) is not a well-established TNC receptor, making this a weak/non-canonical pairing. TNC is produced by stromal fibroblasts/FRC during remodeling or inflammation, while ITGA7 is more characteristic of muscle and some stromal cells, not a typical lymphoid immune receptor. Likely a low-confidence computational prediction rather than a validated interaction.

short_description: ECM glycoprotein-integrin; tenascin-C engages alpha8beta1 integrin on stromal cells
summary_description: TNC (tenascin-C) binds the ITGA8_ITGB1 (alpha8beta1) integrin, a recognized tenascin receptor mediating cell-matrix adhesion and modulation of cell migration during tissue remodeling. TNC is expressed by fibroblastic reticular cells/stromal fibroblasts especially under remodeling or inflammatory conditions, while ITGA8_ITGB1 is expressed on stromal/mesenchymal and some smooth muscle-like cells in perivascular niches. This is a biologically plausible, moderately well-supported ECM-integrin interaction in stromal remodeling contexts.

short_description: Endothelial annexin-Robo; ANXA2/ROBO4 stabilizes vascular/HEV endothelial junctions
summary_description: ANXA2 (annexin A2) is a membrane-associated protein that can interact with ROBO4, an endothelial-specific receptor that stabilizes vasculature by antagonizing VEGF-induced permeability and promoting junctional integrity. Both are expressed predominantly by vascular/HEV endothelial cells in lymphoid organs, consistent with a role in maintaining HEV barrier integrity during lymphocyte transmigration. This is a plausible but less extensively validated non-chemokine endothelial signalling axis, more established in angiogenesis research than lymphoid immunology.

short_description: Matricellular ligand-integrin subunit; thrombospondin-1/alpha6 integrin, partner beta chain unspecified
summary_description: THBS1 can engage alpha6-containing integrins (typically alpha6beta1 or alpha6beta4) to modulate cell adhesion and migration, though ITGA6 alone omits the required beta partner, weakening specificity. THBS1 is secreted by platelets, macrophages, and stromal cells, while ITGA6 is expressed on basal epithelial cells, some leukocyte subsets and endothelium, with lesser-defined roles in secondary lymphoid organ biology. Interaction is plausible but underspecified/weakly supported without the beta chain.

short_description: Collagen (endostatin precursor)-integrin; COL18A1 binds alpha1beta1 for adhesion/anti-angiogenesis
summary_description: COL18A1 (collagen XVIII, precursor of endostatin) can interact with ITGA1_ITGB1 (alpha1beta1) integrin, influencing endothelial cell adhesion and angiogenesis regulation. COL18A1 is produced by vascular basement membranes and stromal/endothelial cells, while ITGA1_ITGB1 is expressed on endothelial and stromal cells, relevant to vascular remodeling and HEV basement membrane interactions in lymphoid tissue. This is a biologically reasonable though less thoroughly characterized ECM-integrin interaction compared to COL1A1.

short_description: Galectin-CD47; LGALS9/CD47 is non-canonical, CD47's established ligand is SIRPA/TSP1
summary_description: LGALS9 (galectin-9) is a well-known ligand for TIM-3 and other receptors regulating T cell exhaustion/tolerance; CD47 is canonically engaged by SIRPA ("don't eat me" signal) and thrombospondin-1, not galectin-9, so this pairing is non-canonical or weakly supported. LGALS9 is expressed by macrophages, DCs, and stromal cells, while CD47 is broadly expressed on hematopoietic and stromal cells for phagocytosis regulation. Likely reflects co-expression rather than a validated direct binding interaction.

short_description: Endothelial multimerin-CD93; MMRN2/CD93 supports vascular/HEV endothelial adhesion and angiogenesis
summary_description: MMRN2 (multimerin-2) is an endothelial-restricted ECM glycoprotein that binds CD93 (also known as C1qR1), modulating endothelial cell adhesion, migration, and angiogenesis. Both ligand and receptor are predominantly expressed by vascular/HEV endothelial cells in lymphoid organs, consistent with a role in vascular stabilization and leukocyte-endothelial interactions during lymphocyte trafficking. This is a reasonably well-supported endothelial-specific interaction, though more established in general vascular biology than lymphoid-specific contexts.

short_description: TAM ligand-receptor tyrosine kinase; GAS6/AXL dampens inflammation, clears apoptotic cells
summary_description: GAS6 is a vitamin K-dependent ligand that activates the receptor tyrosine kinase AXL, promoting efferocytosis of apoptotic cells, dampening inflammatory signalling, and supporting tissue homeostasis. GAS6 is produced by macrophages, DCs and stromal cells, while AXL is expressed on macrophages, DCs, and some stromal/endothelial cells, relevant to clearance of apoptotic lymphocytes in germinal centers and resolution of inflammation. This is a canonical, well-established TAM receptor signalling axis.

short_description: MHC class I-CD8 coreceptor; antigen presentation to CD8 T cells
summary_description: HLA-B presents peptide antigen to the TCR/CD8 complex on CD8+ T cells, with CD8B (part of CD8 heterodimer) stabilizing TCR-MHC-I engagement and triggering cytotoxic T cell activation/signalling. HLA-B is broadly expressed on nucleated stromal and immune cells; CD8B is restricted to CD8+ T cells, relevant in T-cell zone and GC CD8 surveillance. Canonical interaction, well supported.

short_description: ECM collagen-CD44; stromal adhesion and matrix remodeling signal
summary_description: Collagen VI alpha3 chain binds CD44, promoting cell-matrix adhesion and potentially modulating migration/survival signalling via CD44 clustering. COL6A3 is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells (FRC) and stromal fibroblasts, while CD44 is broadly expressed on lymphocytes, macrophages, and stromal cells, supporting leukocyte trafficking through the reticular network. Interaction is plausible but moderately supported, mainly inferred from ECM-receptor databases.

short_description: Progranulin-TNFR1; anti-inflammatory modulation, blocks TNF signalling
summary_description: Granulin (GRN/progranulin) binds TNFRSF1A (TNFR1), competing with TNF-alpha and dampening NF-kB-driven inflammatory signalling rather than activating classical death-domain apoptosis pathways. GRN is secreted by macrophages, neutrophils, and some stromal cells; TNFRSF1A is broadly expressed on stromal and immune cells including FRCs. Biologically plausible immunomodulatory axis, though less canonical than TNF-TNFR1 signalling itself.

short_description: FACIT collagen-CD44; fibroblastic reticular network adhesion cue
summary_description: Collagen XIV (FACIT-type) interacts with CD44 to mediate stromal matrix organization and cell adhesion, influencing leukocyte retention within collagen-rich reticular fibers. COL14A1 is expressed by FRCs/perivascular fibroblasts in T zone, while CD44 is expressed on lymphocytes and stromal cells, supporting structural scaffolding of lymphoid compartments. Database-level ECM-receptor pairing, modestly supported functionally.

short_description: Fibulin-integrin beta1; ECM adhesion in stromal remodeling
summary_description: Fibulin-1 (FBLN1) binds integrin beta1-containing heterodimers, promoting cell-ECM adhesion and modulating fibroblast/leukocyte adhesion signalling via FAK pathways. FBLN1 is secreted by stromal fibroblasts/FRCs in capsule and trabecular regions; ITGB1 is broadly expressed on stromal, endothelial and immune cells, contributing to tissue architecture and cell positioning. Reasonably supported ECM-integrin interaction.

short_description: Slit-Robo guidance; vascular endothelial stabilization and angiogenesis control
summary_description: SLIT3 engages the endothelial-specific receptor ROBO4 to stabilize vasculature by antagonizing VEGF-induced permeability and regulating angiogenic sprouting. SLIT3 is expressed by stromal/endothelial cells, while ROBO4 is restricted to vascular/high endothelial venule (HEV) endothelium, relevant to maintaining HEV integrity for lymphocyte entry. Canonical vascular guidance pair, well supported.

short_description: Matrix metalloproteinase-CD44; ECM remodeling and migration signal
summary_description: MMP9 binds to CD44 on the cell surface, localizing proteolytic activity for ECM degradation and facilitating cell migration, also enabling release of matrix-bound growth factors. MMP9 is produced by macrophages, neutrophils, and activated stromal cells; CD44 is expressed broadly on leukocytes and stromal cells, important during tissue remodeling and immune cell trafficking, e.g., in germinal centre and medullary regions. Well-documented functional interaction.

short_description: CTGF-integrin alpha5; fibroblast adhesion and fibrotic signalling
summary_description: CCN2 (CTGF) binds ITGA5 (as part of alpha5beta1 integrin), promoting fibroblast adhesion, migration and profibrotic signalling via FAK/ERK pathways. CCN2 is secreted by activated FRCs/fibroblasts, and ITGA5 is expressed on stromal and some immune cells, contributing to stromal remodeling, particularly during tissue repair or chronic inflammation in lymphoid stroma. Moderately supported stromal interaction.

short_description: Galectin-9-CD45; immunoregulatory glycan-lectin signalling, modulates T cells
summary_description: Galectin-9 (LGALS9) binds glycosylated CD45 (PTPRC), modulating TCR signalling thresholds and promoting T-cell regulation/apoptosis (distinct from its better-known TIM-3 ligand role). LGALS9 is expressed by macrophages, DCs, and stromal cells; PTPRC (CD45) is pan-leukocyte, relevant broadly across lymphoid compartments. This LGALS9-PTPRC pairing is less canonical than LGALS9-HAVCR2(TIM-3) and may reflect broader glycan-binding promiscuity captured by databases.

short_description: TIMP3-CD44; MMP inhibition coupled to matrix receptor
summary_description: TIMP3 is a matrix-bound metalloproteinase inhibitor that can associate with CD44 at the cell surface, linking MMP inhibition to CD44-mediated adhesion/signalling and regulating ECM turnover. TIMP3 is produced by stromal fibroblasts/FRCs; CD44 is widely expressed on leukocytes and stromal cells, relevant to controlling tissue remodeling balance in lymphoid stroma. Interaction is plausible but weakly characterized functionally, largely database-derived.

short_description: TIMP2-integrin beta1; MMP regulation and adhesion-linked signalling
summary_description: TIMP2 binds integrin beta1 (independent of its MMP-inhibitory domain) to modulate cell adhesion, proliferation, and anti-angiogenic signalling via MAP kinase pathways. TIMP2 is secreted by stromal fibroblasts/endothelial cells; ITGB1 is broadly expressed on stromal, endothelial, and immune cells, relevant to vascular and stromal homeostasis in lymphoid tissue. Known non-protease-dependent integrin interaction, moderately well supported.

short_description: CD14-integrin beta1; monocyte/macrophage adhesion and innate signalling
summary_description: CD14, typically a GPI-anchored co-receptor for LPS/TLR4 signalling, can engage integrin beta1 to support monocyte/macrophage adhesion and migration signalling in inflamed tissue. CD14 is expressed by monocytes/macrophages and some DCs; ITGB1 is broadly expressed on stromal and immune cells, relevant to macrophage positioning in medullary cords/sinuses. Non-canonical pairing relative to CD14's primary TLR4 co-receptor role; likely secondary/weakly supported adhesion interaction.

short_description: RANKL-osteoprotegerin; decoy receptor blocks RANK signalling, LTi/FDC development
summary_description: TNFSF11 (RANKL) normally signals through RANK (TNFRSF11A) to drive lymphoid tissue organogenesis, but TNFRSF11B (osteoprotegerin, OPG) acts as a soluble decoy receptor that sequesters RANKL and blocks this signalling. RANKL is expressed by stromal organizer cells/LTi-interacting cells, FDCs, and lymphoid tissue inducer cells; OPG is secreted by stromal cells/osteoblast-like cells as a regulatory decoy, important in modulating FDC network development and bone-lymphoid crosstalk. This is a decoy-receptor interaction, not a signalling-competent pair.

short_description: CXCL12-integrin beta1 crosstalk; chemokine-enhanced adhesion, HEV/stromal niche
summary_description: CXCL12 (SDF-1) primarily signals through CXCR4 but can transactivate/potentiate integrin beta1-mediated adhesion (inside-out signalling) to enhance leukocyte arrest on stroma/endothelium. CXCL12 is produced by FRCs, FDCs, and perivascular/HEV stromal cells; ITGB1 is expressed on lymphocytes and stromal cells, relevant to T/B cell homing and retention in lymphoid niches. This is a secondary chemokine-integrin crosstalk interaction rather than CXCL12's canonical receptor (CXCR4), so weakly direct.

short_description: Collagen I-VEGFR3; atypical ECM-lymphatic receptor link, likely artefact
summary_description: Collagen I (COL1A1) is a canonical ECM structural protein with no established direct ligand activity for FLT4 (VEGFR3), which normally binds VEGF-C/D to drive lymphangiogenesis. COL1A1 is made by fibroblasts/FRCs; FLT4 is restricted to lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs) in lymphoid sinuses. This pairing is non-canonical and most likely reflects a database/co-expression artefact rather than a genuine signalling ligand-receptor interaction.

short_description: ECM proteoglycan-syndecan; basement membrane/ECM anchoring and signaling
summary_description: HSPG2 (perlecan) is a large basement-membrane heparan sulfate proteoglycan binding syndecan-1 core protein, modulating cell adhesion, growth factor presentation and ECM organization. In lymphoid tissue, perlecan derives from stromal/vascular basement membranes (HEV, fibroblastic reticular cells) while SDC1 marks plasma cells, epithelial cells and some stroma, supporting niche adhesion. Interaction is structural/ECM rather than a classical signaling axis.

short_description: Angiopoietin-like-syndecan; lipid/ECM modulation, weakly characterized in lymphoid tissue
summary_description: ANGPTLA4 is a secreted adipokine-like factor regulating lipid metabolism and angiogenesis, reported to bind syndecan family members including SDC3 to modulate cell adhesion and vascular permeability. ANGPTL4 is produced by stroma/adipocytes/endothelium under hypoxic or metabolic stress, while SDC3 is expressed on macrophages/neural-associated cells; evidence for this pair in lymph node/tonsil/spleen is limited and likely reflects a generic ECM-proteoglycan interaction rather than a lymphoid-specific axis.

short_description: Integrin subunit-adhesion receptor; non-canonical, likely database artefact
summary_description: ITGB2 (CD18) normally pairs with alpha subunits (e.g., LFA-1, Mac-1) to bind ICAMs; CD226 (DNAM-1) is an adhesion/costimulatory receptor on NK/T cells binding CD155/CD112, not ITGB2. This pairing is non-canonical and likely reflects a database artefact from promiscuous integrin-subunit annotation rather than a validated ligand-receptor signaling event in lymphoid tissue.

short_description: Basement-membrane proteoglycan-integrin; ECM adhesion and mechanosignaling
summary_description: Perlecan (HSPG2) engages integrin beta1-containing heterodimers to mediate cell-ECM adhesion, basement membrane integrity and mechanotransduction. In lymphoid organs, perlecan is produced by vascular/stromal basement membranes (HEV, FRC networks) while ITGB1 is broadly expressed on leukocytes, stromal and endothelial cells, supporting retention and migration within reticular/vascular niches.

short_description: Chemokine-receptor; recruits Th1/effector T cells and NK cells
summary_description: CXCL9 (MIG) is an IFN-gamma-induced chemokine signaling through GPCR CXCR3 to drive chemotaxis and integrin activation. Produced by macrophages, DCs and stromal cells in T-zone/interfollicular regions, it recruits CXCR3+ effector/memory T cells, Th1 cells and NK cells, important for T-cell zone positioning and inflammatory responses in lymph node/tonsil/spleen.

short_description: Inhibitory co-receptor paired with BCR subunit; non-canonical pairing
summary_description: BTLA is an inhibitory immunoreceptor on T/B cells that normally signals via HVEM (TNFRSF14), not CD79A, which is the Ig-alpha signaling subunit of the B-cell receptor complex. This pairing is non-canonical/likely a database artefact arising from co-expression on B cells rather than a genuine ligand-receptor interaction.

short_description: Chemokine linked to adrenergic receptor; database artefact, not a real receptor
summary_description: CXCL13 is the canonical ligand for CXCR5, driving B-cell and Tfh follicular organization and germinal centre formation (produced by FDCs/follicular stroma). ADRA2A is an adrenergic GPCR for catecholamines, not a chemokine receptor; this pairing is a database/algorithmic artefact reflecting promiscuous GPCR matching, not a genuine signaling interaction.

short_description: Fibrillar-associated collagen-integrin; stromal ECM adhesion
summary_description: COL14A1 (FACIT collagen) binds integrin alpha1beta1 (collagen receptor) to mediate fibroblast/stromal adhesion to collagen fibrils and regulate matrix organization. In lymphoid tissue this reflects reticular fibroblast/FRC network-collagen interactions supporting conduit and capsule structure, with ITGA1_ITGB1 expressed on stromal cells, some T cells and endothelium.

short_description: Angiopoietin-like-syndecan; lipid/vascular modulation, weak lymphoid relevance
summary_description: ANGPTL4 can bind syndecan-1 to modulate lipoprotein lipase activity, vascular permeability and cell adhesion, mainly characterized in adipose/endothelial biology. SDC1 marks plasma cells and some epithelium/stroma in lymphoid organs; direct evidence for this axis as a dedicated lymphoid signaling pathway is weak and likely reflects generic ECM/proteoglycan binding captured by spatial correlation.

short_description: Amyloid precursor-LRP1; scavenger receptor endocytosis/signaling, weak lymphoid role
summary_description: APP binds LRP1, a multifunctional endocytic/scavenger receptor mediating ligand clearance and intracellular signaling (classically studied in neurons). Both are broadly expressed including on macrophages, stromal cells and endothelium in lymphoid tissue; this interaction is not immunologically canonical and likely reflects a general scavenger-receptor/ligand correlation rather than lymphoid-specific signaling.

short_description: Complement inhibitor-selectin; non-canonical, likely spurious pairing
summary_description: SERPING1 (C1-inhibitor) is a soluble serine protease inhibitor regulating complement/kinin cascades, not a known ligand for P-selectin (SELP), which binds PSGL-1 on leukocytes to mediate rolling adhesion on activated endothelium/platelets. This pairing lacks established biology and is likely a database/co-expression artefact rather than a genuine receptor interaction.

short_description: Matrix proteoglycan-integrin; stromal ECM adhesion and immune modulation
summary_description: Versican (VCAN) is a large ECM chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan that can engage integrin beta1 complexes to influence cell adhesion, proliferation and inflammatory signaling. Produced by fibroblastic reticular cells/stroma in T-zone and capsule regions, it interacts with ITGB1 on leukocytes and stromal cells, contributing to reticular network and immune cell retention/migration cues.

short_description: Alarmin (DAMP)-scavenger receptor; myeloid activation signaling
summary_description: S100A8 (part of calprotectin) is a damage-associated alarmin released by neutrophils/monocytes that can engage scavenger receptor CD36 (alongside TLR4/RAGE) to promote myeloid activation, foam-cell-like lipid handling and inflammatory signaling. Both are expressed on macrophages/myeloid cells in lymphoid tissue, relevant to innate immune activation and inflammation rather than lymphocyte trafficking.

short_description: Fibronectin-complement receptor; non-canonical, likely artefactual link
summary_description: Fibronectin (FN1) is an ECM glycoprotein binding integrins/syndecans, not C5a (the natural ligand of C5AR1, a GPCR on myeloid cells mediating complement-driven chemotaxis/inflammation). This pairing is non-canonical and likely reflects a spatial co-expression artefact rather than a direct ligand-receptor signaling event.

short_description: Angiopoietin-integrin; vascular remodeling and endothelial-pericyte signaling
summary_description: ANGPT2 (Angiopoietin-2), normally a Tie2 ligand, can also engage integrin alpha5beta1 to modulate endothelial cell adhesion, vascular destabilization and remodeling, particularly in inflamed/high endothelial venule contexts. Produced by endothelial cells (HEV) and acting on ITGA5_ITGB1-expressing endothelium/pericytes, this reflects vascular remodeling rather than classical lymphocyte signaling.

short_description: Complement-receptor; opsonin binding drives immune complex trapping on FDCs
summary_description: C3 (cleaved to C3b/iC3b) binds CR1 (CD35), promoting immune complex clearance and complement regulation. In lymphoid tissue, C3 is produced by macrophages/stromal cells and complement fragments decorate antigen; CR1 is expressed on follicular dendritic cells (FDC), B cells and erythrocytes, where it retains immune complexes in the germinal centre for antigen presentation to B cells.

short_description: Growth factor-coreceptor; promotes angiogenesis and lymphatic/HEV vascular remodeling
summary_description: VEGFA binds the co-receptor NRP1, enhancing VEGFR2 signalling to drive endothelial proliferation, migration and vascular permeability. In lymphoid organs VEGFA is produced by stromal/myeloid cells while NRP1 is expressed on blood/lymphatic endothelium (HEV, lymphatics) and some DCs, supporting angiogenesis and vascular remodeling needed for lymphocyte trafficking.

short_description: Chemokine-proteoglycan; matrix immobilization of CCL5 for haptotactic presentation
summary_description: CCL5 (RANTES) is a chemokine that normally signals through CCR1/CCR3/CCR5; binding to syndecan-1 (SDC1) is a glycosaminoglycan-mediated immobilization/presentation interaction rather than classical GPCR signalling. CCL5 is secreted by T cells/macrophages/stroma, while SDC1 is expressed on plasma cells, epithelium and some stromal cells, helping localize chemokine gradients on matrix/plasma cell surfaces for leukocyte recruitment.
