This pairing is a non-canonical, heparan-sulfate-dependent interaction rather than a primary signalling receptor-ligand pair.

short_description: ECM glycoprotein-proteoglycan; structural matrix binding, not classical signalling
summary_description: Tenascin-XB (TNXB) is an extracellular matrix glycoprotein that can bind heparan sulfate proteoglycans like syndecan-1 (SDC1), mediating matrix organization and cell adhesion modulation rather than a dedicated signalling cascade. TNXB is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells/stroma, and SDC1 is expressed on plasma cells and epithelial/stromal cells, supporting extracellular matrix architecture in lymphoid tissue. This is a weakly characterized, largely structural matrix-binding interaction rather than a canonical signalling axis.

short_description: Sheddase-receptor; likely non-canonical, ADAM10 is a protease not classical ligand
summary_description: ADAM10 is a membrane metalloprotease best known for shedding substrates like Notch ligands and CD44 itself, not a secreted ligand for CD44; any reported ADAM10-CD44 'interaction' likely reflects ADAM10-mediated proteolytic processing of CD44 co-expressed on the same or neighboring cells (e.g., DCs, macrophages, lymphocytes) rather than a bona fide ligand-receptor signalling pair. This is best regarded as a database artefact arising from protease-substrate proximity rather than genuine paracrine signalling.

short_description: Matricellular protein-caveolin; non-canonical, CAV1 is intracellular scaffold protein
summary_description: CCN1 (CYR61) is a secreted matricellular protein that normally signals through integrins (e.g., αvβ3, α6β1) and heparan sulfate proteoglycans; caveolin-1 (CAV1) is predominantly an intracellular/membrane-scaffold protein organizing caveolae and is not a conventional cell-surface ligand-binding receptor. This pairing is likely a database artefact reflecting CAV1's role in modulating integrin signalling downstream rather than direct CCN1 receptor engagement; CCN1 is produced by stromal/endothelial cells while CAV1 is broadly expressed in endothelium and fibroblasts.

short_description: Collagen-receptor; endothelial adhesion/efferocytosis support in stromal vasculature
summary_description: Collagen I (COL1A2 chain) can engage CD93 (C1qR1), a receptor also implicated in complement C1q binding, cell adhesion and angiogenesis. COL1A2 is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells/stroma, while CD93 is expressed on endothelial cells and monocytes/macrophages, supporting vascular adhesion and stabilization within lymphoid stroma; evidence for this specific collagen-CD93 interaction is relatively limited compared to CD93's complement role.

short_description: Neuregulin-Fc receptor; likely spurious, FCAMR is an IgA/IgM Fc receptor
summary_description: Neuregulin-1 (NRG1) is an EGF-family growth factor that normally signals via ERBB3/ERBB4 receptor tyrosine kinases, not via Fc receptors; FCAMR (Fcα/μR) is an Ig Fc receptor binding IgA/IgM on B cells, mesangial cells and some epithelium. This NRG1-FCAMR pairing lacks established mechanistic basis and is best interpreted as a likely database/algorithmic artefact rather than genuine signalling.

short_description: Basement-membrane collagen-integrin; adhesion to vascular/stromal basement membrane
summary_description: Collagen IV (COL4A1) binds the integrin α9β1 (ITGA9_ITGB1), mediating cell adhesion to basement membrane and downstream integrin/FAK signalling influencing migration and survival. COL4A1 is produced by endothelial cells and stromal fibroblasts forming basement membranes (HEV, lymphatic, FDC networks), while ITGA9β1 is expressed on lymphatic endothelium, neutrophils and some lymphocytes, supporting cell attachment and trafficking through perivascular/basement membrane structures.

short_description: Ribosomal protein-complement receptor; damage-associated ligand triggers myeloid chemotaxis
summary_description: Extracellular/released ribosomal protein S19 (RPS19) can act as a damage/alarm signal binding C5aR1, triggering monocyte/macrophage chemotaxis, partly mimicking complement C5a signalling. RPS19 is released from apoptotic or activated cells (e.g., germinal centre B cells undergoing selection), while C5AR1 is expressed on macrophages, monocytes and granulocytes, supporting clearance of apoptotic debris in germinal centres. This is a non-canonical, less well-established ligand for C5AR1 compared to its principal ligand C5a.

short_description: Basement-membrane collagen-adhesion receptor; stromal/leukocyte matrix attachment
summary_description: Collagen IV (COL4A2) can engage CD44, a hyaluronan receptor with broader ECM-binding capacity, supporting cell adhesion and migration along basement membranes. COL4A2 is produced by endothelial/stromal cells forming vascular and reticular basement membranes, while CD44 is broadly expressed on lymphocytes, DCs and stromal cells, facilitating leukocyte retention and trafficking within lymphoid tissue; this collagen-CD44 link is less canonical than CD44's primary hyaluronan interaction.

short_description: Complement fragment-tetraspanin; weak/non-canonical co-receptor association, likely indirect
summary_description: C3 (as C3d) is a well-known co-stimulatory ligand for CR2/CD21-CD19-CD81 complex on B cells, but direct C3-CD81 binding is not a primary characterized interaction; CD81 mainly functions as a tetraspanin scaffolding partner for CD19/CR2 rather than a standalone C3 receptor. This pairing likely reflects the known C3d-CD21-CD19-CD81 B cell co-receptor complex context rather than direct independent C3-CD81 engagement, and should be considered indirect/non-canonical.

short_description: Transglutaminase-integrin; non-canonical cell adhesion/matrix crosslinking cofactor
summary_description: Transglutaminase 2 (TGM2) is an extracellular matrix-crosslinking enzyme that can also act as a non-enzymatic adhesion co-factor for integrins including α4 integrins (ITGA4, as in α4β1/α4β7), supporting cell adhesion to fibronectin-TGM2 complexes. TGM2 is expressed by stromal/endothelial cells and macrophages, while ITGA4-containing integrins are expressed on lymphocytes and monocytes, contributing to leukocyte adhesion and homing; this is a secondary, matrix-mediated interaction rather than classical ligand-receptor signalling.

short_description: Chemokine-receptor mismatch; non-canonical, CXCL2 is not an XCR1 ligand
summary_description: CXCL2 is a CXC chemokine that normally signals through CXCR2 on neutrophils, whereas XCR1 is a distinct receptor specific for the C-chemokine XCL1, expressed on cDC1 dendritic cells for cross-presentation. This CXCL2-XCR1 pairing crosses chemokine subfamilies and lacks known receptor specificity, so it is best regarded as a database artefact rather than a genuine signalling interaction.

short_description: Chemokine-decoy receptor; scavenging/transcytosis, not canonical signalling
summary_description: CCL5 binds ACKR1 (DARC), an atypical chemokine receptor that lacks G-protein coupling and functions as a scavenger/transcytosis decoy rather than a signalling receptor, modulating local chemokine bioavailability. CCL5 is secreted by T cells, platelets and macrophages, while ACKR1 is expressed on venular/HEV endothelium and erythrocytes, where it sequesters and transports chemokines across endothelium to support leukocyte adhesion gradients without direct intracellular signalling.

short_description: Trefoil factor-atypical chemokine receptor; likely scavenging/non-canonical pair
summary_description: TFF3 is a mucin-associated trefoil factor involved in epithelial repair, not a canonical ACKR3 (CXCR7) ligand; ACKR3 is a decoy/scavenger receptor for CXCL12/CXCL11 expressed on lymphatic endothelium, stromal and some B cells. This pairing is non-canonical/weakly supported and likely a database artefact rather than a validated signalling axis in lymphoid tissue.

short_description: Collagen IV-integrin α1β1; basement membrane adhesion signal
summary_description: COL4A1 is a basement-membrane collagen binding integrin α1β1 (VLA-1), activating FAK/Rho adhesion and survival signalling. COL4A1 is produced by stromal cells, FRCs and endothelium forming vascular/HEV basement membranes, while ITGA1_ITGB1 is expressed on memory T cells, monocytes and stromal cells, supporting adhesion and retention within perivascular/stromal niches.

short_description: von Willebrand factor-P-selectin; endothelial platelet/leukocyte adhesion
summary_description: VWF, stored with P-selectin in Weibel-Palade bodies, can co-present with SELP on activated endothelium to promote leukocyte and platelet tethering under shear stress. Both are expressed by HEV/venular endothelial cells; this axis supports leukocyte rolling/recruitment at high endothelial venules rather than being a direct high-affinity VWF-SELP signalling ligand-receptor pair, so functional relevance here is largely adhesive/co-localization based.

short_description: Ceruloplasmin-ferroportin; iron export/ferroxidase coupling, not a signalling receptor
summary_description: Ceruloplasmin (CP) is a ferroxidase that oxidizes Fe2+ exported via the ferroportin (SLC40A1) channel, enabling iron loading onto transferrin; this is a metabolic/transport coupling, not a classical ligand-receptor signalling event. Both are expressed by macrophages (including splenic red pulp/subcapsular sinus macrophages) regulating iron recycling; inclusion in ligand-receptor databases here reflects a functional but non-signalling interaction.

short_description: LPS coreceptor-TLR4; innate immune activation, NF-κB signalling
summary_description: CD14 presents LPS to the TLR4/MD2 complex, triggering MyD88/TRIF-dependent NF-κB and interferon signalling and pro-inflammatory cytokine production. CD14 is expressed on macrophages, monocytes and some DCs; TLR4 is on macrophages, DCs and stromal/endothelial cells, mediating innate sensing of bacterial components in subcapsular sinus and medullary macrophages of lymphoid organs.

short_description: Lipoprotein lipase-CD44; non-canonical lipid-binding interaction, weak support
summary_description: LPL is a secreted lipid-processing enzyme hydrolyzing triglycerides; its reported binding to CD44 is non-canonical, proposed to mediate LPL anchoring/presentation on endothelial or stromal cell surfaces rather than classical receptor signalling. CD44 is broadly expressed on leukocytes, FRCs and endothelium; this interaction is weakly supported and likely reflects incidental surface tethering rather than a dedicated signalling axis.

short_description: Heparin-binding EGF-CD44; growth factor presentation, proliferative signalling
summary_description: HB-EGF, a heparin-binding EGF-family ligand, can be presented by CD44 (a hyaluronan receptor) to EGFR on adjacent cells, promoting cell proliferation and tissue repair signalling. HB-EGF is produced by macrophages, stromal cells and endothelium; CD44 is ubiquitously expressed on leukocytes and FRCs, supporting growth factor localization in stromal niches rather than direct CD44 signalling.

short_description: CD23-integrin αXβ2; FDC-myeloid adhesion in germinal centre
summary_description: FCER2 (CD23), a low-affinity IgE receptor and FDC marker, can interact with integrin αXβ2 (CD11c/CD18) as an alternative ligand supporting adhesion rather than classical IgE signalling. CD23 is expressed on follicular dendritic cells and some B cells in germinal centres; ITGAX_ITGB2 is on dendritic cells/macrophages, suggesting a role in FDC-myeloid cell adhesion within the follicle/GC.

short_description: Perlecan-LRP1; basement membrane proteoglycan, endocytic/adhesion signalling
summary_description: HSPG2 (perlecan), a major basement-membrane heparan sulfate proteoglycan, binds LRP1, a multifunctional endocytic/signalling receptor mediating clearance and modulation of growth factor signalling. Perlecan is produced by stromal/endothelial cells forming vascular and stromal basement membranes; LRP1 is expressed on macrophages, stromal cells and endothelium, contributing to matrix remodeling and HEV/vascular integrity.

short_description: L-selectin-MAdCAM-1; lymphocyte homing to HEV, mucosal lymphoid tissue
summary_description: SELL (L-selectin) on naive lymphocytes binds MAdCAM-1 on high endothelial venules, mediating the initial rolling step of lymphocyte homing into mucosal-associated lymphoid tissue (e.g., Peyer's patches, mesenteric lymph nodes). This is a canonical, well-established adhesion interaction critical for lymphocyte trafficking and HEV-mediated entry into secondary lymphoid organs.

short_description: Tissue factor pathway inhibitor-LRP1; coagulation regulation, endocytic clearance
summary_description: TFPI inhibits the extrinsic coagulation pathway (factor Xa/VIIa-TF complex) and is cleared via LRP1-mediated endocytosis, representing a scavenging rather than classical signalling interaction. TFPI is produced by endothelial cells; LRP1 is broadly expressed on endothelium, macrophages and stromal cells, relevant to vascular/HEV homeostasis rather than lymphoid-specific immune signalling.

short_description: Collagen I-integrin α9β1; stromal matrix adhesion, weak/atypical pairing
summary_description: COL1A2 (collagen I chain) can engage integrin α9β1, though α9β1 more canonically binds tenascin-C, VCAM-1 and osteopontin, making this a weaker/atypical collagen-integrin pairing. COL1A2 is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells/stromal fibroblasts; ITGA9_ITGB1 is expressed on some leukocyte subsets and epithelium, supporting stromal adhesion and retention within FRC networks.

short_description: Collagen IV-integrin α1β1; basement membrane adhesion, same as COL4A1 axis
summary_description: COL4A2, a basement-membrane collagen IV chain, binds integrin α1β1 (VLA-1) to promote adhesion and FAK-mediated survival/migration signalling, analogous to the COL4A1_ITGA1_ITGB1 axis. COL4A2 is produced by stromal/endothelial cells building vascular basement membranes (including HEV), while α1β1 is on memory T cells and stromal cells, supporting perivascular retention.

short_description: Collagen IV-CD44; matrix adhesion, non-canonical ligand-receptor pairing
summary_description: COL4A1 is a basement-membrane collagen with no well-established direct high-affinity binding to CD44 (a hyaluronan receptor); this pairing is non-canonical and likely reflects a database-predicted interaction rather than validated signalling. COL4A1 is made by stromal/endothelial cells; CD44 is broadly expressed on leukocytes and stroma, so biological significance of direct engagement here is uncertain.

short_description: FAM3C-adhesion GPCR ADGRG5; poorly characterized, weak evidence in lymphoid tissue
summary_description: FAM3C (ILEI) is a secreted cytokine-like protein implicated in EMT/fibrosis signalling, and ADGRG5 (GPR114) is an adhesion GPCR with largely unknown ligands and function; their interaction is poorly characterized with minimal direct experimental support. Expression patterns in lymphoid stroma/epithelium are not well defined, so this pairing should be treated as weakly supported/putative rather than an established signalling axis.

short_description: Galectin-endoglin; modulates endothelial TGF-beta signalling, vascular adhesion
summary_description: LGALS3 (galectin-3) binds beta-galactoside glycans on ENG (endoglin/CD105), a TGF-beta co-receptor, modulating endothelial activation, angiogenesis and leukocyte adhesion rather than classical ligand-receptor signalling. In lymphoid tissue, LGALS3 is expressed by macrophages, dendritic cells and stromal cells, while ENG is expressed on blood vascular endothelium (including HEV). This pairing is weakly supported mechanistically and likely reflects a lectin-glycoprotein interaction captured as a database artefact rather than a defined signalling axis.

short_description: von Willebrand factor-osteoprotegerin; non-canonical, likely spurious vascular pairing
summary_description: VWF is an endothelial/platelet adhesion glycoprotein mediating platelet tethering under shear stress, while TNFRSF11B (osteoprotegerin/OPG) is a soluble TNF-receptor-superfamily decoy that normally binds RANKL and TRAIL. There is no established direct VWF-OPG signalling axis; both are secreted by vascular endothelium (HEV/blood vessels) in lymphoid tissue, so this pairing is likely a co-expression/database artefact rather than genuine receptor engagement.

short_description: Metalloprotease-integrin; ADAM28 binds alpha4 integrins for leukocyte adhesion
summary_description: ADAM28 is a disintegrin-metalloprotease that can act as a non-catalytic adhesion ligand for integrin alpha4beta1/alpha4beta7 (ITGA4), supporting lymphocyte binding and potentially proteolytic processing of ECM/adhesion molecules. ADAM28 is expressed by lymphocytes and some epithelial/stromal cells, while ITGA4 is expressed on T and B cells trafficking through HEV and lymphoid parenchyma. Evidence for this specific interaction in lymphoid tissue is limited and should be treated as weakly supported.

short_description: Perlecan-FGFR1; heparan sulfate proteoglycan co-receptor for FGF signalling
summary_description: HSPG2 (perlecan) is a basement-membrane heparan sulfate proteoglycan that acts as a co-receptor/reservoir presenting FGF ligands to FGFR1, promoting receptor tyrosine kinase signalling, proliferation and angiogenesis. Perlecan is produced by stromal fibroblastic reticular cells (FRC) and vascular basement membranes, while FGFR1 is expressed on endothelial cells and stromal progenitors, supporting lymphoid stromal/vascular remodeling. This is a plausible co-receptor-type interaction rather than direct high-affinity ligand binding.

short_description: Collagen I-integrin alpha1beta1; stromal matrix adhesion and FRC signalling
summary_description: COL1A2 (type I collagen chain) binds integrin alpha1beta1 (ITGA1_ITGB1) to mediate cell-matrix adhesion, mechanotransduction and regulation of collagen synthesis/turnover. Collagen I is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells (FRC) and other stromal fibroblasts, while ITGA1_ITGB1 is expressed on stromal cells, some memory T cells and endothelium, supporting FRC network integrity and T-zone structural organization. This is a well-established canonical ECM-integrin interaction.

short_description: Chemokine mismatch; CCL2 does not canonically signal via CCR10
summary_description: CCL2 (MCP-1) is a monocyte-chemoattractant chemokine whose canonical receptor is CCR2, not CCR10; CCR10 is the receptor for CCL27/CCL28 and mediates skin/mucosal-homing of IgA plasma cells and Tregs. CCL2 is produced by macrophages, stromal and endothelial cells, while CCR10 is expressed on plasma cells and skin-tropic lymphocytes. This pairing is non-canonical and likely a database/algorithmic artefact rather than a real signalling axis.

short_description: APP N-terminal fragment–DR6; death-receptor signalling, mainly neural evidence
summary_description: A shed N-terminal fragment of APP binds TNFRSF21 (DR6) and triggers caspase-dependent degeneration/pruning, a mechanism described mostly in neurons. Both genes are broadly expressed in lymphoid stroma and leukocytes, and DR6 is expressed on B cells and some T cells. The lymphoid relevance is weakly characterised, so read this pair as stroma-associated co-expression rather than a defined immune axis.

short_description: Complement regulators; CD55 and CR1 both inhibit complement, not ligand-receptor
summary_description: CD55 (DAF) and CR1 (CD35) are both complement-regulatory membrane proteins that accelerate decay of C3/C5 convertases and promote complement inactivation, respectively; they are not known to engage each other as a signalling ligand-receptor pair. Both are expressed on follicular dendritic cells (FDC), erythrocytes and various leukocytes within germinal centres and lymphoid stroma. This pairing is likely a database/functional co-annotation artefact rather than a true interaction.

short_description: MHC-I-inhibitory receptor; dampens myeloid/NK activation, immune tolerance
summary_description: HLA-C (MHC class I) engages LILRB2 (ILT4), an inhibitory immunoreceptor with ITIM motifs, delivering inhibitory signals that dampen myeloid cell and NK cell activation, promoting tolerance. HLA-C is broadly expressed on nucleated cells including antigen-presenting cells, while LILRB2 is expressed on monocytes/macrophages and dendritic cells in lymphoid tissue, contributing to regulation of myeloid activation states and immune homeostasis. This is a canonical, well-supported inhibitory checkpoint interaction.

short_description: Hyaluronan synthase-CD44; hyaluronic acid matrix binding, lymphocyte adhesion/migration
summary_description: HAS2 synthesizes hyaluronic acid, the principal ligand for CD44, promoting cell adhesion, migration and retention within hyaluronan-rich extracellular matrix. HAS2 is expressed by stromal fibroblasts/FRC and lymphatic endothelium, while CD44 is broadly expressed on lymphocytes, dendritic cells and stromal cells, supporting lymphocyte trafficking through T-zone reticular networks and lymphatic sinuses. This is a well-established canonical matrix-receptor interaction.

short_description: VEGFA-integrin beta1; non-canonical co-receptor engagement, angiogenic signalling support
summary_description: VEGFA primarily signals through VEGFR1/2, but can also engage beta1-integrins (ITGB1) as co-receptors to modulate endothelial adhesion and enhance angiogenic signalling. VEGFA is produced by stromal, myeloid and follicular dendritic cells, while ITGB1 is broadly expressed on endothelial cells, stromal cells and lymphocytes, supporting vascular remodeling in lymphoid tissue. This interaction is secondary/non-canonical relative to the primary VEGFR axis and should be interpreted cautiously.

short_description: Alpha1-antitrypsin-LRP1; scavenger receptor clearance, protease inhibitor endocytosis
summary_description: SERPINA1 (alpha1-antitrypsin), a serine protease inhibitor, is cleared via LRP1 (low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 1), a multifunctional endocytic scavenger receptor, mediating uptake and degradation of protease-inhibitor complexes rather than a classical signalling cascade. SERPINA1 is produced by hepatocytes and myeloid cells, while LRP1 is expressed on macrophages and stromal cells in lymphoid tissue, contributing to clearance/homeostatic functions rather than direct immune signalling.

short_description: Adhesion molecule-IL2 receptor alpha; non-canonical, likely database artefact
summary_description: ICAM1 is an adhesion molecule that canonically binds integrins (LFA-1/Mac-1), not IL2RA (CD25), which is the alpha subunit of the IL-2 receptor requiring IL-2 as its ligand; there is no established direct ICAM1-IL2RA signalling interaction. ICAM1 is expressed on activated endothelium, dendritic cells and stroma, while IL2RA is expressed on activated/regulatory T cells, so this pairing is non-canonical and likely a co-expression artefact.

short_description: Apolipoprotein E-LRP1; lipid uptake, immunomodulatory scavenger receptor signalling
summary_description: APOE binds LRP1, a scavenger/endocytic receptor, mediating lipoprotein uptake and also modulating macrophage/dendritic cell inflammatory signalling and efferocytosis. APOE is secreted by macrophages, stromal cells and follicular dendritic cells, while LRP1 is expressed on macrophages and stromal/endothelial cells in lymphoid tissue, supporting lipid metabolism and immune-regulatory crosstalk, particularly in germinal centre and macrophage-rich niches. This is a canonical, reasonably well-supported interaction.

short_description: Granzyme B-IGF2R; cytotoxic protease uptake via mannose-6-phosphate receptor
summary_description: GZMB (granzyme B), a cytotoxic T/NK cell serine protease, can be internalized via IGF2R (the cation-independent mannose-6-phosphate receptor) through mannose-6-phosphate tagging, facilitating entry into target cells to promote apoptosis independent of perforin pores. GZMB is produced by cytotoxic T cells and NK cells, while IGF2R is broadly expressed on target/stromal cells; this is a recognized but non-classical uptake mechanism rather than a signalling receptor interaction.

short_description: ECM collagen-CD44; stromal adhesion and cell migration signal
summary_description: COL6A1 is a microfibrillar collagen binding CD44, triggering adhesion/signalling that promotes cell spreading, survival and migration. In lymphoid tissue, collagen VI is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells (FRC) and other stromal cells, while CD44 is broadly expressed on lymphocytes, macrophages and FRCs, supporting leukocyte retention and stromal scaffolding in T-zone/medullary regions.

short_description: Protease-receptor; uPA/LRP1 drives ECM remodeling and endocytic clearance
summary_description: PLAU (urokinase plasminogen activator) binds LRP1, mediating clearance of uPA-plasminogen activator inhibitor complexes and modulating pericellular proteolysis, cell migration and signalling. In lymphoid organs this occurs mainly in stromal/fibroblastic cells and macrophages during tissue remodeling, wound healing-like responses, and extracellular matrix turnover rather than classical immune signalling.

short_description: Galectin-integrin; modulates T-cell adhesion and apoptosis signalling
summary_description: Galectin-1 (LGALS1) binds beta1-integrin glycans, affecting integrin clustering, adhesion to ECM, and can promote T-cell apoptosis/anergy. LGALS1 is secreted by stromal cells, FRCs and some T cells, while ITGB1 is widely expressed on T/B lymphocytes and stromal cells; this interaction contributes to immune homeostasis and T-zone stromal-lymphocyte crosstalk.

short_description: Basement-membrane nidogen-integrin; supports stromal/endothelial matrix adhesion
summary_description: Nidogen-1 (NID1) is a basement-membrane glycoprotein linking laminin and collagen networks, and binds ITGB1-containing integrins to mediate cell-matrix adhesion and basement membrane integrity. NID1 is produced by stromal/endothelial cells (e.g., HEV, FRC conduits), while ITGB1 is broadly expressed on lymphocytes and stromal cells, supporting structural organization of lymphoid niches.

short_description: Collagen VI-integrin α1β1; stromal adhesion and mechanosignalling
summary_description: COL6A2 engages the collagen-binding integrin ITGA1_ITGB1, activating adhesion and mechanotransduction pathways important for ECM organization and cell anchorage. Collagen VI is secreted by FRCs/stromal fibroblasts, and ITGA1_ITGB1 is expressed on stromal cells and some activated leukocytes, contributing to reticular network integrity in T-cell zones.

short_description: Tenascin-X ECM protein binding integrin α9β1; stromal adhesion
summary_description: Tenascin-X (TNXB) is an extracellular matrix glycoprotein that interacts with integrin α9β1 to modulate cell adhesion, ECM assembly and collagen fibrillogenesis. TNXB is produced by fibroblasts/stromal cells in connective tissue capsules and trabeculae of lymphoid organs, while ITGA9_ITGB1 is expressed on some leukocytes and endothelial/lymphatic cells, supporting structural tissue integrity rather than direct immune signalling.

short_description: TGF-beta family ligand-coreceptor; endothelial/stromal BMP signalling modulator
summary_description: BMP2 binds endoglin (ENG), a TGF-beta/BMP coreceptor that modulates BMP/TGF-beta signalling intensity, affecting angiogenesis and vascular remodeling. ENG is characteristically expressed on endothelial cells (including HEVs) and some stromal/perivascular cells, where BMP2-ENG signalling influences vascular development and homeostasis within lymphoid organ vasculature.

short_description: Matricellular protein-endoglin; vascular ECM remodeling association, weak support
summary_description: SPARC is a matricellular glycoprotein regulating collagen deposition and ECM turnover; its direct binding to ENG (endoglin) is not well characterized mechanistically and may represent a weaker/putative database-derived interaction. Both are associated with endothelial/stromal and perivascular compartments (e.g., HEVs) involved in vascular remodeling, but functional ligand-receptor signalling evidence is limited.

short_description: Collagen VI-integrin α1β1; stromal matrix adhesion signal
summary_description: COL6A3, like other collagen VI chains, binds integrin α1β1 to mediate cell-ECM adhesion and support mechanical signalling in connective tissue. Collagen VI is produced by FRCs/fibroblasts forming the reticular fiber network, and ITGA1_ITGB1 is expressed on stromal cells and subsets of leukocytes, contributing to lymphoid stromal scaffold integrity.

short_description: Laminin beta2-CD44; basement membrane adhesion and leukocyte retention
summary_description: Laminin β2 (LAMB2), a basement membrane component, binds CD44 to promote cell adhesion and can influence leukocyte migration along basement membranes. LAMB2 is expressed by endothelial/stromal basement membranes (e.g., HEV, lymphatics), while CD44 is broadly expressed on lymphocytes and macrophages, supporting cell anchorage and trafficking within lymphoid microenvironments.

short_description: von Willebrand factor-integrin α9; vascular adhesion, non-canonical pairing
summary_description: Von Willebrand factor (VWF) is classically an endothelial/platelet adhesion molecule binding GPIb and integrins like αIIbβ3; direct binding to integrin α9 alone (without β1 partner specified) is non-canonical and likely reflects a weakly supported or database-inferred interaction. VWF is produced by endothelial cells (HEV/blood vessels), while ITGA9 is found on lymphatic endothelium and some leukocytes, suggesting a possible vascular/lymphatic adhesion role requiring caution in interpretation.

short_description: Chemokine-receptor mismatch; CCL5 is non-canonical CXCR3 ligand
summary_description: CCL5 (RANTES) is a canonical ligand for CCR1/CCR3/CCR5, not CXCR3 (whose ligands are CXCL9/10/11); this pairing is non-canonical and likely a database/promiscuity artefact. CCL5 is produced by activated T cells, macrophages and stromal cells, while CXCR3 is expressed on activated/effector T cells and NK cells homing to inflamed or T-zone regions; genuine signalling via this specific pair is not well established.

short_description: CD99–CD81 (tetraspanin) cis/trans association; leukocyte adhesion and transmigration
summary_description: CD99 engages CD81 (a tetraspanin) in homophilic/heterophilic interactions implicated in leukocyte diapedesis, T-cell adhesion, and signalling microdomain organization. CD99 and CD81 are both broadly expressed on leukocytes, including T/B cells and germinal centre B cells, supporting transendothelial migration and immune synapse/tetraspanin web formation in lymphoid tissue.

short_description: Basement-membrane collagen IV-integrin α9β1; vascular/stromal adhesion
summary_description: Collagen IV (COL4A2), a core basement membrane collagen, binds integrin α9β1 to mediate cell adhesion and basement membrane interactions. COL4A2 is produced by endothelial cells and stromal/epithelial basement membranes (HEV, lymphatics), while ITGA9_ITGB1 is expressed on lymphatic endothelium and some leukocytes, supporting vascular and lymphatic structural integrity in lymphoid organs.

short_description: Protease inhibitor-CD44; ECM remodeling modulation, moderately supported pairing
summary_description: TIMP2, a matrix metalloproteinase inhibitor, has been reported to bind CD44 and modulate MMP activity and cell proliferation/migration signalling, though this interaction is less canonical than TIMP-MMP binding. TIMP2 is secreted by stromal fibroblasts/FRCs, while CD44 is widely expressed on lymphocytes and stromal cells, implicating this pair in ECM turnover regulation within lymphoid stroma.

short_description: Matrix proteoglycan-TLR; stromal DCN activates TLR4 innate signalling
summary_description: DCN (decorin), a small leucine-rich proteoglycan from fibroblastic reticular cells/stroma, can engage TLR4 to trigger NF-kB-dependent inflammatory signalling, acting as a damage-associated molecular pattern. In lymphoid tissue DCN is produced by FRCs/stromal fibroblasts while TLR4 is expressed on macrophages/DCs; this is a non-canonical, weakly supported interaction more characteristic of injury/fibrosis than steady-state lymphoid biology.

short_description: MHC-I component-NK inhibitory receptor; immune surveillance signal
summary_description: B2M (beta-2-microglobulin) pairs with MHC class I heavy chains and is recognized together with HLA-E by KLRD1 (CD94/NKG2 heterodimer), delivering inhibitory or activating signals to NK/NKT cells. B2M is ubiquitously expressed by nucleated cells presenting MHC-I, while KLRD1 marks NK cells and some CD8 T cells in lymphoid parenchyma/sinuses, contributing to tolerance surveillance. As annotated here B2M alone (without HLA-E) is a simplified/partial ligand-receptor proxy.

short_description: Alarmin-scavenger receptor; myeloid activation and debris clearance signal
summary_description: S100A9 (calprotectin component) is a DAMP released by neutrophils/monocytes that can bind CD68, a lysosomal/scavenger-type receptor on macrophages, promoting phagocytic/inflammatory activation. In lymphoid organs this reflects myeloid-myeloid crosstalk in medullary cords/sinuses and subcapsular macrophages during inflammation. The ligand-receptor link is weakly characterized functionally (CD68 is mainly an intracellular/lysosomal marker), so likely a database-inferred rather than well-validated signalling axis.

short_description: Angio/lymphangiogenic growth factor-coreceptor; vascular and lymphatic patterning
summary_description: VEGFA binds Neuropilin-2 (NRP2) as a coreceptor enhancing VEGFR signalling, promoting lymphangiogenesis and venous/lymphatic endothelial guidance. VEGFA is produced by stromal cells, macrophages and FRCs, while NRP2 is expressed on lymphatic endothelial cells (and some venous endothelium) lining lymphatic sinuses in lymph node/spleen. This supports lymphatic vessel maintenance and remodeling important for lymph flow and cell trafficking in SLOs.

short_description: Chemoattractant cytokine-CD4; T helper cell recruitment and activation
summary_description: IL16 (secreted after caspase-3 cleavage) binds CD4 directly, acting as a chemoattractant and costimulatory signal for CD4+ T cells, monocytes and DCs. IL16 is released by activated T cells, eosinophils and epithelium, while CD4 marks helper T cells and some myeloid cells in T-cell zones of lymph node/tonsil/spleen. This supports CD4+ T cell recruitment/retention during immune responses.

short_description: Urokinase plasminogen activator-integrin; proteolysis-linked adhesion/migration signal
summary_description: PLAU (uPA) binds its GPI-anchored receptor PLAUR typically, but can also interact with beta1 integrins (ITGB1) to modulate cell adhesion, ECM proteolysis and migration signalling. PLAU is produced by stromal/myeloid cells and endothelium; ITGB1 is broadly expressed on leukocytes, FRCs and endothelial cells, supporting tissue remodeling and cell trafficking. This ITGB1 pairing is non-canonical/indirect compared to the primary uPA-uPAR axis.

short_description: Homing chemokine-receptor pair; likely non-canonical cross-reactivity, not CCR7
summary_description: CCL21 is the canonical CCR7 ligand that guides naive T cells and DCs into T-cell zones via HEVs and lymphatics; CCR10 is instead the receptor for CCL27/CCL28, mediating skin/mucosal and IgA plasma cell homing. CCL21 producers are FRCs/lymphatic endothelium; CCR10 is on skin-homing T cells and plasmablasts. This CCL21-CCR10 pairing is non-canonical/likely a database cross-assignment rather than a validated signalling axis.

short_description: Lactoferrin-orphan receptor; weakly characterized, likely artefactual pairing
summary_description: LTF (lactoferrin) is an antimicrobial/iron-binding glycoprotein secreted by neutrophils and epithelial/secretory cells with known receptors (e.g., LRP1, intelectin), not IGDCC4, an immunoglobulin superfamily cell-adhesion molecule of uncertain ligand specificity. In lymphoid tissue LTF may arise from neutrophils/epithelium while IGDCC4 expression is poorly defined. This pairing lacks mechanistic support and likely reflects a database-predicted, non-canonical interaction.

short_description: Laminin-integrin; basement membrane adhesion for stromal/vascular cells
summary_description: Laminin gamma-1 (LAMC1), a basement membrane component, engages integrin alpha9beta1 to mediate cell adhesion, migration and lymphatic endothelial function. LAMC1 is produced by stromal/endothelial cells forming basement membranes of HEVs/lymphatics, while ITGA9_ITGB1 is expressed on lymphatic endothelium, neutrophils and some FRCs, supporting structural integrity and leukocyte trafficking across vascular/stromal interfaces in SLOs.

short_description: Treg/DC-attracting chemokine degraded by DPP4; regulatory homing axis
summary_description: CCL22 (via CCR4) recruits Tregs and activated T cells/DCs; DPP4 (CD26) is a peptidase that cleaves and inactivates many chemokines including CCL22, modulating gradient strength rather than acting as a classical signalling receptor. CCL22 is produced by DCs/macrophages in T zones; DPP4 is expressed on T cells, endothelium and epithelium. This is a ligand-processing enzyme interaction, not direct receptor signalling - interpret with caution.

short_description: Laminin-CD44; epithelial/stromal adhesion and migration signal
summary_description: Laminin gamma-2 (LAMC2), part of laminin-332, binds CD44 to promote cell adhesion, spreading and migration, typically in epithelial basement membranes. In lymphoid organs LAMC2 may be expressed by capsule/trabecular epithelial-like stroma, while CD44 is broadly expressed on lymphocytes, macrophages and FRCs, supporting leukocyte adhesion/migration along stromal scaffolds; this pairing is more established in epithelial than lymphoid contexts.

short_description: Matricellular protein-Notch receptor; vascular pericyte/stromal signalling, weak evidence
summary_description: Thrombospondin-2 (THBS2) is a matricellular glycoprotein mainly known to modulate angiogenesis/ECM, with limited direct evidence of NOTCH3 activation, which canonically responds to Jagged/Delta ligands. THBS2 is secreted by stromal fibroblasts/pericytes; NOTCH3 marks pericytes/vascular smooth muscle around high endothelial venules. This pairing is non-canonical and likely reflects predicted rather than validated receptor engagement.

short_description: Tenascin-C-vascular phosphatase; endothelial ECM sensing, poorly characterized
summary_description: Tenascin-C (TNC) is an ECM glycoprotein upregulated during stromal remodeling/inflammation; PTPRB (VE-PTP) is a receptor tyrosine phosphatase restricted to vascular/lymphatic endothelium regulating VE-cadherin and angiogenic signalling. TNC is produced by activated FRCs/fibroblasts; PTPRB marks HEV and sinusoidal endothelium. Direct TNC-PTPRB engagement is not well established mechanistically, so this is a weakly supported, likely database-inferred interaction.

short_description: Angiopoietin-like protein-integrin; endothelial/metabolic adhesion signalling
summary_description: ANGPTL4, a secreted factor regulating lipid metabolism and vascular permeability, can bind alpha5beta1 integrin to influence endothelial cell adhesion and vascular stability. ANGPTL4 is produced by stromal/adipose-like cells and hypoxic endothelium; ITGA5_ITGB1 is expressed on endothelial cells and fibroblasts within lymphoid stroma, supporting vascular remodeling and barrier regulation under metabolic/hypoxic stress.

short_description: APP–α2A-adrenergic receptor; non-canonical, likely database artefact
summary_description: APP (amyloid precursor protein) is a transmembrane protein processed into secreted fragments, without an established role as a secreted ligand for GPCRs; ADRA2A is an alpha-2 adrenergic receptor responding to catecholamines (norepinephrine), relevant to neuro-immune modulation of lymphoid stroma/vasculature. This pairing lacks direct mechanistic support and is a non-canonical, likely database-artefact interaction (ADRA2A chemokine-like link).

short_description: ECM-integrin; laminin binding supports stromal/vascular cell adhesion
summary_description: Laminin β2 chain binds the α7β1 integrin heterodimer, triggering FAK/ILK-mediated adhesion and cytoskeletal signalling rather than classical second-messenger signalling. In lymphoid tissue laminin-211/-221 is produced by stromal/vascular basement membrane cells (FRCs, endothelium, perivascular cells) while ITGA7_ITGB1 is mainly expressed on myocytes and some stromal/perivascular cells; this pair is more characteristic of vascular/perivascular basement membrane interactions than immune signalling, and support in SLO is relatively weak.

short_description: Non-canonical; secreted cytokine-like FAM3C paired with inhibitory PD-1
summary_description: FAM3C (ILEI) is a secreted cytokine-like protein with no established direct physical interaction with PD-1 (PDCD1), whose validated ligands are PD-L1/PD-L2; this pairing likely reflects a database/correlation artefact rather than a genuine ligand-receptor signalling axis. PDCD1 is expressed on activated/exhausted T cells in T zones and germinal centres (Tfh), while FAM3C is broadly expressed by epithelial/stromal cells; biological relevance of this specific interaction is not well supported.

short_description: MHC-I–ILT4 checkpoint; inhibits myeloid/NK and T cell activation
summary_description: Classical MHC class I (HLA-A) engages the inhibitory leukocyte immunoglobulin-like receptor LILRB2 (ILT4), delivering ITIM-mediated inhibitory signalling that dampens myeloid and lymphocyte activation. HLA-A is ubiquitously expressed on nucleated cells including stromal and antigen-presenting cells, while LILRB2 is expressed on monocytes/macrophages and dendritic cells in lymph node/spleen, contributing to immune tolerance and regulation of myeloid activation in these tissues.

short_description: PAI-1–LRP1 scavenger interaction; clearance and pro-survival signalling
summary_description: SERPINE1 (PAI-1) binds LRP1, mediating endocytic clearance of PAI-1/protease complexes and activating pro-survival/migratory signalling via LRP1's intracellular adaptor interactions. LRP1 is broadly expressed on macrophages, stromal fibroblasts, and endothelial cells, while PAI-1 is produced by stromal, endothelial and activated macrophages; this axis is mainly relevant to tissue remodeling/ECM turnover rather than lymphocyte-specific signalling in SLO.

short_description: Angiopoietin-like–Tie1; vascular remodeling, weak/orphan receptor interaction
summary_description: ANGPTL4 is an angiopoietin-like factor affecting vascular permeability and lipid metabolism; TIE1 is an orphan-like receptor tyrosine kinase that typically requires heterodimerization with TIE2 and lacks a well-defined direct ligand-binding mechanism for ANGPTL4, so this interaction is weakly supported. Both are expressed by lymphatic/blood endothelial cells in HEV and lymphatic sinuses, consistent with a vascular remodeling role, but direct ANGPTL4-TIE1 signalling is not firmly established.

short_description: Chemokine-integrin crosstalk; CXCL12 triggers VLA-4-mediated firm adhesion
summary_description: CXCL12 (SDF-1) is a canonical CXCR4 chemokine ligand; here it is paired with the integrin subunit ITGA4 (part of VLA-4/α4β1 or α4β7), reflecting chemokine-induced inside-out activation of integrin adhesion rather than direct high-affinity ligand binding to ITGA4 itself. CXCL12 is produced by FRCs/stromal cells and HEV, while ITGA4-bearing lymphocytes use this signal to arrest and transmigrate at HEV; the direct CXCL12-ITGA4 binding claim is non-canonical/likely inferred rather than a bona fide receptor interaction.

short_description: TRAIL–osteoprotegerin decoy; apoptosis-inhibiting decoy receptor interaction
summary_description: TNFSF10 (TRAIL) binds TNFRSF11B (osteoprotegerin, OPG), which acts as a soluble decoy receptor sequestering TRAIL and blocking its pro-apoptotic signalling through death receptors DR4/DR5. OPG is produced by stromal/follicular dendritic cells and osteoblast-lineage cells, while TRAIL is expressed by NK/T cells and myeloid cells; this interaction mainly serves as a regulatory decoy/neutralizing mechanism rather than direct apoptotic signalling.

short_description: Collagen VI-integrin; stromal ECM adhesion via α9β1
summary_description: Collagen VI (COL6A1) engages the α9β1 integrin heterodimer, mediating cell-ECM adhesion and migratory signalling through FAK/Rho pathways. Collagen VI is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells and stromal cells in lymph node/spleen capsule and trabeculae, while ITGA9_ITGB1 is expressed on some leukocytes, lymphatic endothelium and stromal cells, supporting structural scaffolding and cell trafficking within stromal niches.

short_description: Non-canonical; TRAIL paired with chemokine receptor CCR6
summary_description: TNFSF10 (TRAIL) is a TNF-family death ligand whose canonical receptors are DR4/DR5 (and decoy DcR1/DcR2/OPG); CCR6 is a chemokine receptor for CCL20 with no established direct binding to TRAIL, making this pairing non-canonical and likely a computational/database artefact. CCR6 is expressed on Th17 cells, Tregs, and subcapsular/follicular dendritic cells directing mucosal and follicular homing, unrelated to TRAIL's apoptotic signalling.

short_description: uPA-integrin; proteolysis-linked adhesion/migration signalling via α5β1
summary_description: PLAU (urokinase plasminogen activator) can interact with integrins including α5β1 (ITGA5 subunit) to promote cell adhesion, migration and pericellular proteolysis signalling, distinct from its canonical uPAR (PLAUR) receptor pathway. PLAU is produced by stromal, endothelial and myeloid cells, while ITGA5-bearing fibroblasts/endothelium use this interaction for ECM remodeling and migration during tissue remodeling/angiogenesis in lymphoid stroma.

short_description: Non-canonical; amyloid precursor protein paired with Notch2 receptor
summary_description: APP (amyloid precursor protein) is not a canonical Notch ligand (canonical ligands are Jagged/Delta-like family); this pairing is weakly supported and likely reflects a database artefact from proteomic/correlation-based inference rather than validated receptor engagement. NOTCH2 is expressed on marginal zone B cells and some stromal/endothelial cells, important for marginal zone B cell development, but its physiological ligand here is not APP.

short_description: Complement-regulatory; C3b/iC3b engages CD46 for complement regulation/T cell costimulation
summary_description: Complement component C3 (as C3b/iC3b) binds CD46 (membrane cofactor protein), promoting complement regulation (cofactor for factor I-mediated cleavage) and also acting as a costimulatory signal inducing regulatory T cell differentiation. CD46 is broadly expressed on nucleated cells including T cells and stromal/follicular dendritic cells, while C3 is produced locally by macrophages/FDCs and systemically, linking complement regulation to adaptive immune modulation in germinal centres.

short_description: Laminin-integrin; basement membrane adhesion via α9β1
summary_description: Laminin β2 chain binds the α9β1 integrin heterodimer, engaging basement-membrane adhesion and migratory signalling pathways (FAK/Rho). Laminin is produced by stromal/vascular basement membrane cells (FRCs, HEV, lymphatics) while ITGA9_ITGB1 is found on lymphatic endothelium and some leukocytes, supporting structural integrity and trafficking at vascular/lymphatic basement membranes in lymphoid tissue.

short_description: DAMP-TLR4 co-receptor; biglycan activates innate inflammatory signalling
summary_description: Biglycan (BGN), a soluble ECM proteoglycan acting as a danger-associated molecular pattern (DAMP), binds LY96 (MD-2), the co-receptor that partners with TLR4 to trigger NF-κB-driven pro-inflammatory signalling. BGN is released by stressed stromal/fibroblastic cells, while LY96/TLR4 complexes are expressed on macrophages and dendritic cells in lymphoid tissue, linking ECM damage/stress signals to innate immune activation.

short_description: Collagen-integrin; collagen XII binds α1β1 for stromal adhesion
summary_description: Collagen XII (COL12A1), a FACIT collagen associated with fibrillar collagen networks, engages the α1β1 integrin heterodimer mediating cell-matrix adhesion and FAK/Rho-dependent signalling. COL12A1 is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells and stromal fibroblasts, while ITGA1_ITGB1 is expressed on stromal cells, some memory T cells and endothelium, supporting structural organization of the FRC conduit network and stromal niches.

short_description: Adhesion ligand-integrin; endothelial VWF binds leukocyte/platelet integrin alpha4
summary_description: VWF is a multimeric adhesion glycoprotein secreted by endothelium that engages integrin alpha4beta1-containing receptors (here just ITGA4 subunit) to mediate leukocyte/platelet tethering and adhesion under flow. In lymphoid tissue, VWF is expressed by HEV/blood vessel endothelial cells while ITGA4 is on lymphocytes and myeloid cells, supporting adhesion at HEVs. ITGA4 alone (without ITGB1/ITGB7 partner) as receptor is a simplified/incomplete complex call, so interpret cautiously.

short_description: Laminin-integrin; basement membrane adhesion for stromal/immune cell migration
summary_description: LAMB1 is a laminin beta chain forming basement membrane laminins that bind integrin alpha9beta1, activating focal adhesion/migration signalling. Laminins are produced by stromal cells, FRCs and endothelium forming basement membranes/conduits, while ITGA9_ITGB1 is expressed on migrating leukocytes and lymphatic endothelium, supporting cell trafficking along reticular networks. This is a canonical ECM-integrin interaction, well supported.

short_description: Cytokine-receptor complex; MIF triggers CD74/CXCR4 survival and chemotaxis signalling
summary_description: MIF is a pro-inflammatory cytokine that binds the CD74/CXCR4 co-receptor complex, activating ERK/PI3K survival and chemotactic signalling independent of classical CXCL12-CXCR4 engagement. CD74 is broadly expressed on B cells, macrophages and DCs; CXCR4 is on B cells, plasma cells and migrating leukocytes, relevant to germinal centre and medullary cord retention. This is a well-documented non-canonical MIF receptor pairing, distinct from chemokine signalling.

short_description: Laminin-integrin; vascular/stromal basement membrane adhesion signal
summary_description: LAMA4 is a laminin alpha chain component of vascular basement membranes that engages integrin alpha6beta1 to promote cell-matrix adhesion and migration signalling. LAMA4 is produced by blood endothelial cells (including HEVs) and pericytes, while ITGA6_ITGB1 is expressed on endothelium, leukocytes and some stromal cells, supporting vascular integrity and leukocyte transmigration. This is a canonical, well-supported ECM-integrin interaction.

short_description: Matricellular protein-syndecan; modulates adhesion and growth factor signalling
summary_description: THBS2 (thrombospondin-2) is a matricellular glycoprotein that binds syndecan-1 (SDC1), a heparan sulfate proteoglycan co-receptor, modulating cell adhesion, matrix remodeling and growth factor presentation. THBS2 is secreted by stromal fibroblasts/FRCs, while SDC1 is highly expressed on plasma cells and some epithelial/stromal cells, relevant to medullary cord and plasma cell niches. This is a plausible but moderately supported stromal interaction.

short_description: Peptide hormone-GPCR accessory; adrenomedullin signals vasodilation via RAMP2/CLR
summary_description: ADM (adrenomedullin) is a vasoactive peptide that signals through the calcitonin receptor-like receptor (CLR) in complex with RAMP2, activating cAMP/PKA pathways to regulate vascular tone and permeability. ADM is produced by endothelial and stromal cells; RAMP2 is expressed on blood vascular endothelium including HEVs, supporting vascular homeostasis in lymphoid tissue. Note RAMP2 alone (without CALCRL) is an accessory subunit, partial complex representation.

short_description: Coagulation inhibitor-tissue factor; regulates clotting at vascular stroma
summary_description: TFPI (tissue factor pathway inhibitor) binds and inhibits tissue factor (F3)/factor VIIa complex, downregulating initiation of the extrinsic coagulation cascade. TFPI is expressed by endothelial cells, while F3 is expressed on perivascular stromal cells, pericytes and some DCs, relevant to hemostasis regulation at vascular interfaces in lymphoid stroma. This is a canonical coagulation-regulatory interaction, not a classical signalling ligand-receptor pair but biologically well supported.

short_description: Matricellular ECM-integrin; tenascin-X supports stromal adhesion signalling
summary_description: TNXB (tenascin-X) is an extracellular matrix glycoprotein that can engage integrin alpha8beta1 to modulate cell adhesion and matrix organization. TNXB is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells/stroma, while ITGA8_ITGB1 is expressed on mesenchymal/stromal and some smooth muscle-like cells, relevant to stromal network integrity. This is a weakly supported interaction with limited direct experimental validation in lymphoid tissue, likely database-inferred.

short_description: Intracellular enzyme-adaptor; likely database artefact, not surface signalling
summary_description: GSTP1 is a cytosolic glutathione S-transferase and TRAF2 is an intracellular TNF-receptor adaptor protein; neither is a secreted ligand nor a surface receptor, so this pairing has no plausible extracellular signalling role. This is almost certainly a database/algorithmic artefact arising from co-expression rather than a genuine ligand-receptor interaction, and should not be interpreted as functional intercellular communication in lymphoid tissue.

short_description: Growth factor-TNF receptor; progranulin modulates TNFR2 inflammatory signalling
summary_description: GRN (progranulin) can bind TNFRSF1B (TNFR2) and antagonize TNF-alpha signalling, dampening NF-kB-driven inflammation. GRN is secreted by macrophages and some stromal cells, while TNFRSF1B is expressed on Tregs, macrophages and endothelium, relevant to immune regulation and vascular homeostasis in lymphoid niches. This interaction is biologically supported but less canonical than classical TNF-TNFR signalling.

short_description: Chemokine-decoy receptor; CXCL3 scavenged by ACKR1, non-signalling
summary_description: CXCL3 is an ELR+ CXC chemokine typically signalling through CXCR2 on neutrophils, but here it is paired with ACKR1 (DARC), an atypical decoy/scavenger receptor lacking G-protein coupling that sequesters chemokines without downstream signalling. ACKR1 is expressed on venular/HEV endothelium and erythrocytes, functioning to shape chemokine gradients rather than transduce signals. This is a scavenger-receptor interaction, not canonical signalling.

short_description: Collagen-integrin; ECM adhesion supporting stromal/leukocyte interactions
summary_description: COL6A3 is a collagen VI chain forming microfibrillar ECM networks that bind integrin alpha9beta1 to support cell adhesion and migratory signalling. COL6A3 is secreted by fibroblastic reticular cells and stromal fibroblasts, while ITGA9_ITGB1 is on migrating leukocytes and lymphatic endothelium, relevant to conduit/stromal scaffold interactions. This is a plausible, moderately supported ECM-integrin interaction in lymphoid stroma.

short_description: Chemokine-receptor; monocyte/macrophage recruitment, non-canonical secondary receptor use
summary_description: CCL2 (MCP-1) is primarily a CCR2 ligand but can also engage CCR1 with lower affinity, activating Gi-coupled chemotaxis signalling in monocytes/macrophages. CCL2 is produced by macrophages, stromal cells and endothelium, while CCR1 is expressed on monocytes, some T cells and DCs, contributing to myeloid recruitment into lymphoid tissue. CCR1 engagement by CCL2 is a secondary, less canonical pairing compared to CCL2-CCR2.

short_description: Laminin-integrin; basement membrane adhesion, muscle/stromal specific integrin
summary_description: LAMC1 is a laminin gamma chain subunit of basement membrane laminins that binds integrin alpha7beta1, typically associated with adhesion in muscle and some stromal/vascular cells. LAMC1 is produced by endothelial and stromal cells forming basement membranes, while ITGA7_ITGB1 expression in lymphoid tissue is limited mainly to perivascular/mural cells, making this a less typical but structurally plausible ECM-integrin pairing.

short_description: Chemokine-adrenergic receptor; non-canonical, likely database artefact pairing
summary_description: CCL21 is the canonical CCR7 ligand driving T-cell/DC homing to the T-zone via FRC-derived gradients, but ADRA2A is an adrenergic GPCR for catecholamines (norepinephrine/epinephrine), not a chemokine receptor. This pairing has no established direct binding or signalling basis and likely reflects a database/algorithmic false positive rather than genuine CCL21 receptor engagement.

short_description: Lipoprotein lipase-syndecan; lipid metabolism/retention on stromal surfaces
summary_description: LPL binds the heparan sulfate proteoglycan SDC1, facilitating lipoprotein tethering and lipid uptake rather than a classical signalling cascade. SDC1 is expressed by plasma cells, stromal/epithelial cells and some macrophages in lymphoid tissue (e.g. medullary cords), while LPL is produced by stromal/adipose-associated cells; this pairing likely reflects a metabolic/adhesive interaction rather than immune signalling and may be a weakly supported database entry in this context.

short_description: Adhesion molecule-integrin; firm adhesion and immune synapse formation
summary_description: ICAM1 engages the LFA-1 integrin (ITGAL_ITGB2) to mediate firm adhesion, leukocyte arrest, transendothelial migration and immunological synapse stabilization. ICAM1 is expressed on HEV endothelium, FDCs, DCs and activated stromal cells, while ITGAL_ITGB2 is expressed on T cells, B cells, DCs and macrophages, supporting lymphocyte homing into lymph node/tonsil/spleen and antigen presentation at the T zone and germinal centre.

short_description: Mucosal addressin-integrin; gut-homing lymphocyte adhesion to HEV
summary_description: MAdCAM1 binds integrin alpha4beta7 (ITGA4_ITGB7) to mediate firm adhesion and rolling arrest of lymphocytes on specialized high endothelial venules, a classical mucosal homing axis. MAdCAM1 is expressed on HEV/mucosal endothelium (notably Peyer's patches, mesenteric nodes, spleen) while ITGA4_ITGB7 is expressed on gut-tropic T and B lymphocytes, directing their entry into mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue.

short_description: Intracellular G-protein subunit misannotated as ligand for C5aR1
summary_description: GNAI2 is an intracellular heterotrimeric G-protein alpha subunit that transduces signalling downstream of GPCRs like C5AR1; it is not a secreted/membrane ligand and cannot engage C5AR1 extracellularly. This pairing is a database/computational artefact arising from co-expression or pathway annotation rather than a genuine ligand-receptor interaction; true C5AR1 ligand is complement fragment C5a produced by macrophages/complement activation acting on myeloid cells.

short_description: Collagen-CD44; stromal matrix adhesion and cell retention signal
summary_description: Collagen VI (COL6A2) binds CD44, promoting cell-matrix adhesion and modulating leukocyte retention/migration within stromal niches rather than inducing a canonical signalling cascade. COL6A2 is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells/stromal fibroblasts, while CD44 is broadly expressed on T cells, B cells, macrophages and stromal cells, supporting lymphocyte positioning within the reticular network of lymph node/spleen/tonsil.

short_description: MHC-I–NK inhibitory receptor; self-recognition limiting NK cytotoxicity
summary_description: HLA-B (MHC class I) engages KLRD1 (CD94, pairs with NKG2 family) delivering inhibitory (or activating, depending on partner) signals that regulate NK and some CD8 T cell cytotoxicity, serving as a missing-self checkpoint. HLA-B is expressed broadly on nucleated cells including APCs/stromal cells, while KLRD1 is expressed on NK cells and subsets of CD8 T cells, relevant to immune surveillance within lymphoid tissue.

short_description: Collagen-syndecan; stromal matrix adhesion via heparan sulfate proteoglycan
summary_description: Collagen V (COL5A1) binds the heparan sulfate proteoglycan SDC3, mediating cell-matrix adhesion and potential co-receptor signalling modulation rather than direct receptor activation. COL5A1 is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells/stromal fibroblasts, while SDC3 is expressed on some myeloid cells, DCs and neuronal-associated cells; this interaction likely supports stromal scaffolding and leukocyte retention within lymphoid niches, though evidence is relatively limited.

short_description: Cytokine-receptor complex; pro-inflammatory survival/migration signalling via CD74
summary_description: MIF binds the CD74/CD44 receptor complex, triggering ERK/MAPK signalling that promotes cell survival, proliferation and migration, and sustains inflammatory responses. CD74 (with CD44 as co-receptor) is expressed on B cells, macrophages, DCs and germinal centre B cells, while MIF is broadly produced by stromal cells, macrophages and T cells, contributing to germinal centre B cell survival and macrophage activation.

short_description: Granzyme A-PAR1; pro-inflammatory protease signalling, non-canonical cytotoxic mechanism
summary_description: Granzyme A (GZMA) can cleave and activate protease-activated receptor 1 (F2R/PAR1), inducing pro-inflammatory cytokine release independent of its intracellular caspase-independent cell death function, a less canonical extracellular signalling role. GZMA is released by cytotoxic T cells and NK cells, while F2R is expressed on endothelial cells, fibroblasts and some immune cells; this pairing is plausible but less well-established than GZMA's classical intracellular cytotoxic role.

short_description: Basement membrane collagen-syndecan; stromal adhesion and basement membrane interaction
summary_description: Collagen IV (COL4A1), a basement membrane component, binds the heparan sulfate proteoglycan SDC1, mediating structural adhesion rather than classical signal transduction. COL4A1 is produced by endothelial cells, FRCs and basement membrane-associated stromal cells, while SDC1 is expressed on plasma cells, epithelial cells and some stromal cells, supporting plasma cell niche retention in medullary cords and vascular basement membrane integrity.

short_description: Chemokine mislinked to CD4; likely non-canonical/artefactual receptor pairing
summary_description: CXCL12 (SDF-1) is the canonical ligand for CXCR4 (and ACKR3), not CD4; CD4 is a co-receptor for MHC-II/TCR signalling and HIV entry, not a chemokine receptor. This pairing is non-canonical and likely a database artefact from co-expression in CD4+ T cells, which do express CXCR4 and respond to CXCL12 for T-zone positioning, but not via CD4 itself.

short_description: Semaphorin-plexin; vascular guidance and immune cell positioning signal
summary_description: SEMA3D binds Plexin-D1 (PLXND1), activating Rho-GTPase signalling that regulates cytoskeletal dynamics, cell repulsion/guidance, and vascular patterning. SEMA3D is produced by stromal/endothelial cells, while PLXND1 is expressed on endothelial cells and some lymphocyte subsets, contributing to vascular architecture and guidance cues within lymphoid organ niches such as HEV and marginal zone.

short_description: Decorin-TLR2; matrix-derived DAMP triggering innate inflammatory signalling
summary_description: Decorin (DCN), a small leucine-rich proteoglycan released from extracellular matrix, can act as a danger-associated molecular pattern engaging TLR2 to trigger NF-kB-mediated pro-inflammatory signalling. DCN is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells/stromal fibroblasts, while TLR2 is expressed on macrophages and DCs, linking stromal matrix remodeling to innate immune activation in lymphoid tissue; evidence for direct engagement is moderate.

short_description: Collagen-integrin; matrix adhesion signalling via alpha9beta1 integrin
summary_description: Collagen VI (COL6A2) engages integrin alpha9beta1 (ITGA9_ITGB1), mediating cell-matrix adhesion and modulating leukocyte migration/retention through focal adhesion signalling. COL6A2 is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells/stromal fibroblasts, while ITGA9_ITGB1 is expressed on neutrophils, some T cells and endothelial/lymphatic cells, supporting stromal scaffolding interactions and leukocyte trafficking within lymphoid tissue reticular networks.

short_description: Heme-binding protein mislinked to adrenergic receptor; likely artefact
summary_description: HEBP1 (heme-binding protein 1) is not a validated ligand for ADRA2A, an adrenergic GPCR whose physiological ligands are catecholamines (norepinephrine/epinephrine); this pairing is non-canonical and likely a database/computational artefact from co-expression rather than a genuine signalling interaction. ADRA2A is expressed on stromal/perivascular cells and platelets, regulating vascular tone, but HEBP1 engagement is not biologically established here.

short_description: ECM collagen-integrin; stromal adhesion and fibroblast anchorage
summary_description: Fibrillar collagen V binds integrin α1β1, activating FAK/ILK signalling for cell-matrix adhesion and stromal organization. Collagen V is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells and other stromal fibroblasts, while ITGA1_ITGB1 is expressed on FRCs, pericytes and some leukocytes; supports conduit/reticular network structure in T-zone and medulla.

short_description: Angiopoietin-Tie; vascular remodeling and endothelial destabilization
summary_description: ANGPT2 is a context-dependent TIE2 ligand/antagonist that modulates angiogenesis and vessel stability; TIE1 is an orphan co-receptor lacking direct high-affinity ligand binding, so this pairing is weakly supported and likely reflects database inference from the ANGPT2-TIE2 axis rather than direct ANGPT2-TIE1 signalling. Expressed by blood/lymphatic endothelial cells (HEV, lymphatics) regulating vascular remodeling in lymphoid stroma.

short_description: Sialoglycoprotein-selectin; leukocyte rolling and adhesion to endothelium
summary_description: CD24 is a sialylated GPI-anchored glycoprotein that can serve as a P-selectin ligand, mediating rolling adhesion under flow akin to PSGL-1. SELP (P-selectin) is expressed by activated endothelium (including HEV) and platelets, while CD24 is broad on leukocytes and some epithelial/tumour cells; supports lymphocyte/myeloid trafficking into lymphoid tissue.

short_description: Non-canonical; CSF1 is CSF1R ligand, not a SIRPA ligand
summary_description: CSF1 (M-CSF) canonically signals through CSF1R to drive macrophage/monocyte differentiation and survival; it is not a known ligand for SIRPA, so this pair is likely a database artefact from co-expression inference rather than direct binding. CSF1 is produced by stromal/FRC and macrophages; SIRPA is on myeloid cells regulating phagocytic checkpoint via CD47, an unrelated axis.

short_description: Non-canonical; ABCA1 is lipid transporter, not APOE surface receptor
summary_description: APOE is a lipid-transport apolipoprotein; ABCA1 is an ATP-binding cassette lipid efflux transporter involved in generating APOE/APOA1-containing HDL particles rather than acting as a classical signalling receptor for APOE, making this a likely indirect/metabolic pairing rather than true receptor-ligand signalling. Both are expressed by macrophages (including tingible body macrophages) and stromal cells involved in lipid handling and apoptotic cell clearance in germinal centres.

short_description: Growth factor-tetraspanin; EGFR co-receptor facilitating juxtacrine signalling
summary_description: Pro-HBEGF associates with tetraspanin CD9 to form a complex that enhances juxtacrine HBEGF-EGFR signalling and diphtheria toxin receptor presentation; CD9 itself is not a classical signalling receptor but a scaffolding partner. Expressed on stromal cells, macrophages and some epithelial/endothelial cells; relevant to tissue remodeling and local growth factor signalling in lymphoid stroma.

short_description: Artefact; intracellular calmodulin paired with intracellular HA receptor
summary_description: CALM1 (calmodulin) is a cytosolic calcium-sensor protein and HMMR (RHAMM) is predominantly an intracellular/mitotic spindle protein with some surface hyaluronan-binding function; neither is a conventional secreted ligand-cell surface receptor pair, so this is very likely a database/co-expression artefact rather than true extracellular signalling. Both can be expressed by proliferating stromal and immune cells (e.g., germinal centre cells) during mitosis.

short_description: Likely artefact; NRG1 ligand paired with MHC-II antigen-presentation molecule
summary_description: NRG1 is an EGF-family growth factor acting through ERBB3/ERBB4 receptor tyrosine kinases; HLA-DPB1 is an MHC class II antigen-presentation molecule unrelated to NRG1 signalling, so this pairing is not mechanistically supported and likely reflects spurious co-expression. HLA-DPB1 is expressed by professional antigen-presenting cells (DCs, B cells, macrophages) in T-zone and follicles; NRG1 may come from stromal/neural-associated cells.

short_description: Don't-eat-me checkpoint; inhibits macrophage phagocytosis of self cells
summary_description: CD47 binds SIRPα on phagocytes, triggering ITIM-mediated inhibitory signalling that suppresses phagocytosis ('don't eat me' signal). CD47 is broadly expressed on hematopoietic and stromal cells; SIRPA is expressed on macrophages and dendritic cells, important for regulating macrophage clearance activity in marginal zone, medulla, and germinal centre tingible body macrophages.

short_description: Reverse-oriented CD47-SIRPA checkpoint; same don't-eat-me axis
summary_description: This is the same CD47-SIRPα inhibitory phagocytic checkpoint axis listed in reverse ligand/receptor orientation; SIRPA on macrophages/DCs engages CD47 broadly expressed on hematopoietic and stromal cells to deliver an inhibitory 'don't eat me' signal. Functionally relevant to macrophage homeostasis in spleen (red/marginal zone) and lymph node medulla; duplicate orientation likely reflects bidirectional database annotation rather than distinct biology.

short_description: Scavenger receptor; efferocytosis of calreticulin-exposing apoptotic cells
summary_description: Cell-surface-exposed calreticulin (CALR) acts as an 'eat-me' signal recognized by the scavenger receptor SCARF1, promoting tethering and phagocytic clearance of apoptotic cells. SCARF1 is expressed on macrophages and dendritic cells; CALR exposure occurs on apoptotic/stressed cells, relevant to germinal centre tingible body macrophage clearance of apoptotic B cells.

short_description: Galectin-adhesion; promotes endothelial/pericyte adhesion and vascular integrity
summary_description: Galectin-3 (LGALS3) binds glycosylated MCAM (CD146), modulating cell-cell/cell-matrix adhesion and endothelial-pericyte interactions, with roles in angiogenesis and vascular stability. MCAM is expressed on endothelial cells, pericytes and some lymphocyte subsets; LGALS3 is secreted by macrophages and stromal cells, contributing to vascular and stromal remodeling in lymphoid tissue.

short_description: Angiogenesis inhibitor; TIMP3 blocks VEGFA-KDR signalling on endothelium
summary_description: TIMP3 binds VEGFR2 (KDR) and competitively blocks VEGFA binding, inhibiting VEGF-driven angiogenic signalling independent of its metalloproteinase-inhibitory activity. KDR is expressed on blood endothelial cells (including HEV); TIMP3 is produced by stromal fibroblasts/pericytes, regulating vascular quiescence and remodeling in lymphoid organ stroma.

short_description: Non-canonical; VEGFA engaging integrin α9β1 rather than VEGFR
summary_description: VEGFA can bind integrin α9β1 (ITGA9_ITGB1) as a non-canonical receptor distinct from its primary VEGFR1/2/NRP signalling, modulating endothelial/lymphatic cell adhesion and migration; this is a less-studied, weakly supported interaction relative to canonical VEGFR axis. ITGA9 is expressed on lymphatic endothelial cells and some myeloid cells, relevant to lymphangiogenesis in lymph node sinuses.

short_description: Collagen-scavenger receptor; modulates angiogenesis and cell adhesion signalling
summary_description: Collagen I (COL1A1) can engage CD36, a scavenger receptor that also binds thrombospondin-1, influencing anti-angiogenic signalling and cell adhesion/uptake pathways. CD36 is expressed on macrophages, endothelial cells (including microvascular), and some stromal cells; COL1A1 is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells, relevant to stromal-vascular remodeling and macrophage scavenging in lymphoid tissue.

short_description: Notch ligand-receptor; stromal cell fate and T/B zone niche signalling
summary_description: DLL1 is a transmembrane Delta-like Notch ligand that engages NOTCH2 to trigger juxtacrine proteolytic activation (gamma-secretase) and NICD-driven transcription. In lymphoid tissue, DLL1/DLL4 is expressed by stromal/endothelial cells (e.g., fibroblastic reticular cells, perivascular/lymphatic endothelium) signalling to NOTCH2 on marginal zone B cells, monocytes and some T/DC progenitors, supporting marginal-zone B-cell and monocyte/DC differentiation niches.

short_description: Apolipoprotein-proteoglycan binding; lipid handling, weak/non-canonical signalling pair
summary_description: APOE is a secreted lipid-binding apolipoprotein that can bind heparan sulfate chains of syndecan-2 (SDC2) via electrostatic interactions rather than a classical ligand-receptor signalling event. APOE is produced by macrophages/stromal cells and FDC-associated cells, while SDC2 is expressed on stromal/mesenchymal and some endothelial cells; this is a weakly supported interaction likely reflecting lipoprotein retention on proteoglycan matrix rather than dedicated signalling.

short_description: Coagulation factor-integrin; weak/non-canonical macrophage-matrix interaction
summary_description: F13A1 (coagulation Factor XIII-A) is an intracellular/secreted transglutaminase mainly produced by macrophages and is not a validated integrin ligand; ITGA9 (as ITGA9_ITGB1) normally binds ligands like tenascin-C, VCAM-1, and ADAMs. F13A1-high macrophages are perivascular/medullary lymph node macrophages, while ITGA9 appears on lymphatic endothelium and some leukocytes; this pairing is poorly supported and likely a database/correlation artefact rather than a defined receptor interaction.

short_description: Matricellular protein-TLR; innate activation of macrophages/stroma
summary_description: CCN1 (CYR61) is a secreted matricellular protein that can engage TLR2 (alongside integrins) to activate NF-κB-driven innate immune and inflammatory gene programs. CCN1 is produced by activated stromal fibroblasts/FRCs and endothelial cells under inflammatory stress, while TLR2 is expressed on macrophages, DCs and some stromal cells, contributing to innate sensing and tissue remodeling signals in lymphoid stroma.

short_description: Growth factor-RTK; pericyte/fibroblast recruitment and stromal proliferation
summary_description: PDGFA binds the receptor tyrosine kinase PDGFRB, driving dimerization and downstream PI3K/MAPK signalling that promotes mesenchymal cell proliferation and migration. PDGFA is produced by endothelial cells and some epithelial/stromal cells, while PDGFRB marks pericytes and fibroblastic reticular cell precursors, supporting perivascular stromal/FRC network development and maintenance in lymph node and spleen.

short_description: Macrophage growth factor complex-receptor; myeloid/macrophage survival and differentiation
summary_description: CSF1 and IL34 are alternative ligands for the receptor tyrosine kinase CSF1R, activating downstream ERK/PI3K signalling essential for monocyte/macrophage survival, proliferation and differentiation. CSF1 is produced broadly by stromal cells, fibroblasts and endothelium while IL34 is made by some epithelial/stromal niches; CSF1R is expressed on tissue-resident macrophages (including subcapsular sinus and medullary macrophages) and DCs, a canonical and well-supported macrophage maintenance axis.

short_description: Collagen-integrin; fibroblast/stromal adhesion to extracellular matrix
summary_description: Collagen VI (COL6A1) is an extracellular matrix protein that binds the integrin heterodimer ITGA1_ITGB1 (VLA-1), activating focal adhesion/FAK signalling for cell-matrix adhesion. COL6A1 is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells and other stromal fibroblasts, while ITGA1_ITGB1 is expressed on FRCs, some T cells and stromal cells, supporting reticular network integrity and leukocyte-stroma adhesion in T-cell zones.

short_description: Semaphorin-neuropilin; vascular/axon guidance and immune cell positioning
summary_description: SEMA3F is a secreted class 3 semaphorin that binds neuropilin-1 (NRP1), typically in complex with plexin-A receptors, to trigger cytoskeletal collapse signalling important for vascular and cellular guidance. SEMA3F is expressed by stromal/epithelial cells, while NRP1 is found on endothelial cells, some DCs and Treg populations, contributing to vascular patterning and immune cell positioning within lymphoid tissue microenvironments.

short_description: Laminin-integrin; stromal/muscle-type adhesion to basement membrane
summary_description: Laminin beta-1 (LAMB1) is a basement membrane glycoprotein that binds the ITGA7_ITGB1 integrin heterodimer, mediating cell-matrix adhesion via FAK/Rho signalling. LAMB1 is produced by stromal fibroblasts, FRCs and perivascular cells forming basement membranes, while ITGA7_ITGB1 is more classically a muscle/pericyte integrin; in lymphoid tissue this likely reflects perivascular/pericyte adhesion to reticular basement membranes rather than a major immune signalling axis.

short_description: Laminin-integrin subunit; incomplete receptor pairing, likely matrix adhesion
summary_description: LAMB1 binds integrin alpha chains typically as part of heterodimers (e.g., with ITGB1); ITGA1 alone is not a functional receptor without its beta partner, so this listing likely represents a partial/simplified annotation of the LAMB1-ITGA1_ITGB1 adhesion axis. Biologically, LAMB1 from stromal/basement membrane cells would engage ITGA1-containing integrins on FRCs or pericytes to support reticular fiber and basement membrane adhesion.

short_description: MHC-I-inhibitory receptor; immune checkpoint on myeloid cells
summary_description: HLA-B (MHC class I) engages the inhibitory receptor LILRB2 (ILT4) on myeloid cells, delivering ITIM-mediated inhibitory signalling that dampens antigen presentation and innate activation. HLA-B is expressed broadly on nucleated cells including stromal and immune cells, while LILRB2 is expressed on macrophages, monocytes and DCs, contributing to immune tolerance checkpoints in lymphoid tissue, e.g., modulating myeloid activation near germinal centres.

short_description: Fibronectin-syndecan; stromal matrix adhesion and co-receptor signalling
