summary_description: Fibronectin (FN1) binds the heparan sulfate proteoglycan syndecan-2 (SDC2) as a co-receptor alongside integrins, promoting focal adhesion assembly and cytoskeletal signalling. FN1 is abundantly produced by fibroblastic reticular cells and stromal fibroblasts forming the conduit/reticular network, while SDC2 is expressed on stromal and some endothelial cells, supporting structural organization of the FRC conduit system in T-cell zones.

short_description: TWEAK-DR3; T cell costimulation/apoptosis signalling, moderately supported pair
summary_description: TNFSF12 (TWEAK) classically signals through FN14 (TNFRSF12A); pairing with TNFRSF25 (DR3) is a less canonical cross-reactivity, though DR3 more typically binds TL1A (TNFSF15), so this interaction is weakly supported. TWEAK is produced by monocytes/DCs and some stromal cells, while TNFRSF25 is expressed on activated T cells, potentially modulating T-cell costimulation/survival or apoptotic signalling, but should be interpreted cautiously as a possible database cross-assignment.

short_description: Apolipoprotein-LDL receptor; lipid uptake, canonical metabolic signalling
summary_description: APOE is a secreted apolipoprotein that binds the LDL receptor (LDLR) to mediate endocytic clearance of lipoprotein particles via clathrin-coated pits, a canonical lipid metabolism interaction rather than immune signalling per se. APOE is produced by macrophages, FDCs and stromal cells, while LDLR is broadly expressed on macrophages, stromal and endothelial cells, supporting local lipid homeostasis and macrophage lipid handling in lymphoid tissue.

short_description: Lipid transfer protein-transporter; macrophage cholesterol efflux, non-canonical receptor pair
summary_description: PLTP (phospholipid transfer protein) is a secreted lipid transfer protein, and ABCA1 is a membrane cholesterol/phospholipid efflux transporter rather than a classical signalling receptor, so this is a non-canonical ligand-receptor pairing reflecting a functional lipid-handling association rather than direct receptor engagement. PLTP is secreted by macrophages/stromal cells, and ABCA1 is expressed on macrophages and FDCs, both relevant to cholesterol efflux and foam-cell regulation in lymphoid tissue, but the interaction is likely a database-inferred functional link rather than a bona fide ligand-receptor signalling event.

short_description: Likely artefact; PTPN6 is intracellular phosphatase, not a ligand
summary_description: PTPN6 (SHP-1) is a cytoplasmic protein tyrosine phosphatase involved in intracellular inhibitory signalling downstream of immune receptors; it is not a secreted or membrane ligand for EGFR. EGFR is expressed on epithelial/stromal cells. This pairing is a database artefact arising from co-expression, not a genuine ligand-receptor signalling axis.

short_description: B-cell inhibitory lectin; non-canonical receptor pairing with CD45
summary_description: CD22 (Siglec-2) is a sialic-acid-binding lectin on B cells that normally engages sialylated glycans (often in cis on CD45/PTPRC or other glycoproteins) to dampen BCR signalling, rather than acting through a classical ligand-receptor signalling cascade. Both CD22 and PTPRC(CD45) are expressed on B cells in follicles; this is a weakly supported, glycan-mediated cis-interaction rather than a true trans ligand-receptor pair.

short_description: Laminin-integrin adhesion; basement membrane anchoring of stromal/vascular cells
summary_description: Laminin gamma-1 (LAMC1), a basement membrane ECM component, engages integrin alpha1 (pairing with beta1) to mediate cell-matrix adhesion and outside-in signalling supporting cell survival/migration. LAMC1 is produced by stromal/endothelial cells in basement membranes (HEV, lymphatics, FRC networks) while ITGA1 is expressed on stromal cells, pericytes and some leukocytes anchoring them to vascular/stromal basement membranes.

short_description: Weak/non-canonical; versican is not a validated P-selectin ligand
summary_description: Versican (VCAN) is a large ECM proteoglycan produced by stromal fibroblasts/FRCs, while SELP (P-selectin) is expressed on activated endothelium and platelets and canonically binds PSGL-1/sialyl-Lewis glycans on leukocytes. A direct VCAN-SELP interaction is not well characterized mechanistically and likely reflects a database-predicted rather than established signalling pair.

short_description: Collagen-syndecan adhesion; weakly supported in lymphoid stroma
summary_description: Collagen IX alpha-3 (COL9A3) is a minor fibril-associated collagen that can bind cell-surface heparan sulfate proteoglycans like syndecan-1 (SDC1/CD138) mediating matrix adhesion. SDC1 is expressed on plasma cells and some stromal/epithelial cells in lymphoid tissue; COL9A3 is typically cartilage-associated, so this pairing in lymphoid organs is weakly supported and likely reflects low-level ECM-proteoglycan tethering rather than a dedicated signalling axis.

short_description: Fibronectin-integrin adhesion; stromal ECM engagement of alpha8beta1
summary_description: Fibronectin (FN1), an ECM glycoprotein produced by fibroblastic reticular cells and stromal cells, binds integrin alpha8beta1 (ITGA8_ITGB1) via RGD motifs to mediate adhesion, migration and mechanotransduction. ITGA8_ITGB1 is expressed on stromal/mesenchymal and some smooth muscle/pericyte populations, supporting stromal network integrity and cell positioning within T-zone/FRC conduits.

short_description: Notch ligand-receptor; endothelial signalling for vascular identity
summary_description: JAG1 is a transmembrane Notch ligand that engages NOTCH4 receptor to trigger proteolytic release of NICD and canonical Notch transcriptional signalling. Both JAG1 and NOTCH4 are predominantly expressed on endothelial cells (including HEVs and lymphatic/blood vasculature), where this axis regulates vascular development, arterial-venous specification and angiogenic remodeling in lymphoid tissue.

short_description: RANKL-RANK; osteoclastogenesis and lymphoid tissue organogenesis signal
summary_description: TNFSF11 (RANKL) binds TNFRSF11A (RANK) to activate NF-kB/NFATc1 signalling, a canonical TNF-superfamily ligand-receptor pair. In lymphoid organs RANKL is expressed by stromal organizer cells, lymphoid tissue inducer cells and some T cells, while RANK is on dendritic cells, M cells and osteoclast precursors, supporting lymphoid tissue development, DC survival and M-cell differentiation in mucosal/lymphoid stroma.

short_description: Disintegrin-integrin adhesion; ADAM15 engages alpha5 integrin non-proteolytically
summary_description: ADAM15 is a transmembrane disintegrin-metalloprotease whose disintegrin domain can directly bind integrin alpha5beta1 (ITGA5) mediating cell-cell adhesion independent of its protease activity. ADAM15 is expressed on endothelium, leukocytes and some epithelial cells; ITGA5 is broadly expressed on stromal, endothelial and immune cells, supporting leukocyte-endothelial adhesion and transmigration.

short_description: Non-canonical; dysferlin is not an established ANXA1 receptor
summary_description: Annexin A1 (ANXA1) is typically a secreted/membrane-associated anti-inflammatory mediator that signals through formyl peptide receptors (FPR1/2), not dysferlin (DYSF), a membrane-repair protein in myocytes and some leukocytes. This pairing lacks established receptor pharmacology and likely reflects a database co-expression artefact rather than genuine ligand-receptor signalling.

short_description: Weak/non-canonical; MAdCAM-1 canonically binds integrin alpha4beta7, not CD44
summary_description: MAdCAM-1 is an HEV-restricted adhesion molecule whose well-established receptor is integrin alpha4beta7 (and L-selectin), mediating gut/lymphoid homing of lymphocytes; a direct MAdCAM1-CD44 interaction is not a canonical, well-validated signalling axis. CD44 is broadly expressed on leukocytes and stromal cells and normally binds hyaluronan, so this pairing likely represents weak or incidental binding rather than a primary homing mechanism.

short_description: Collagen-integrin adhesion; basement membrane anchoring via alpha1beta1
summary_description: Collagen XV (COL15A1), a basement membrane-associated collagen, binds integrin alpha1beta1 (ITGA1_ITGB1) to mediate stromal/endothelial cell adhesion to basement membranes and modulate matrix organization. COL15A1 is produced by stromal fibroblasts and perivascular cells, while ITGA1_ITGB1 is on stromal, endothelial and pericyte populations, supporting structural integrity of vascular and stromal niches in lymphoid tissue.

short_description: Prosaposin-LRP1; trophic/scavenger signalling supporting cell survival
summary_description: Prosaposin (PSAP) is a secreted glycoprotein that can act as a ligand for LRP1, a multifunctional scavenger/endocytic receptor, triggering pro-survival and anti-apoptotic signalling (e.g., via MAPK/PI3K pathways). PSAP is broadly secreted by stromal and myeloid cells, while LRP1 is expressed on macrophages, stromal cells and some endothelium, supporting tissue homeostasis and efferocytosis-related clearance in lymphoid stroma.

short_description: Lymphangiogenic growth factor; weak/atypical binding to lymphatic scavenger receptor
summary_description: VEGFC is the principal lymphangiogenic growth factor signalling canonically through VEGFR3 (FLT4) on lymphatic endothelium; LYVE1 is a hyaluronan receptor on lymphatic endothelial cells and some macrophages and is not VEGFC's primary signalling receptor, though some binding/sequestration has been reported. This pairing is weakly supported mechanistically compared to the VEGFC-VEGFR3 axis and may reflect co-expression on lymphatic endothelial cells rather than direct productive signalling.

short_description: Costimulatory ligand-checkpoint receptor; inhibits T-cell activation
summary_description: CD86 is a B7-family costimulatory ligand on antigen-presenting cells that binds CTLA4 on T cells with high affinity, delivering an inhibitory signal that dampens T-cell activation and promotes peripheral tolerance (competing with CD28 for CD86/CD80). CD86 is expressed on dendritic cells, macrophages and B cells in T-cell zones/germinal centres, while CTLA4 is upregulated on activated and regulatory T cells, central to immune checkpoint regulation.

short_description: ECM-receptor; laminin engages CD44 for adhesion/migration
summary_description: LAMA4 (laminin alpha4, basement membrane ECM glycoprotein) binds CD44, a transmembrane hyaluronan/ECM receptor, promoting cell adhesion, spreading and migration signalling. LAMA4 is produced by stromal cells/pericytes/HEV-associated basement membranes while CD44 is broadly expressed on lymphocytes, DCs and stromal cells; this interaction supports leukocyte trafficking and stromal scaffolding in lymphoid tissue.

short_description: Collagen-integrin; fibrillar collagen binding supports stromal adhesion
summary_description: COL5A1 is a fibrillar collagen component of the ECM that binds the collagen-binding integrin ITGA1_ITGB1 (alpha1beta1), triggering integrin-mediated adhesion and outside-in signalling. COL5A1 is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells and other stromal fibroblasts, while ITGA1_ITGB1 is expressed on stromal cells, some T cells and endothelium, supporting FRC network/conduit integrity and stromal-immune cell adhesion.

short_description: Disintegrin-metalloprotease; ADAM15 disintegrin domain ligates integrin beta1
summary_description: ADAM15 is a membrane-anchored metalloprotease-disintegrin whose disintegrin domain binds integrin ITGB1 (as part of various alpha/beta1 heterodimers), mediating cell-cell adhesion and potential proteolytic ECM remodeling signals. ADAM15 is expressed on endothelium, leukocytes and some epithelial/stromal cells; ITGB1 is broad on lymphocytes and stroma, so this pair likely reflects leukocyte-endothelial or leukocyte-stromal adhesion in lymphoid tissue.

short_description: Likely artefact; intracellular coatomer protein COPA as ligand
summary_description: COPA is a core component of the COPI coatomer complex involved in intracellular Golgi-to-ER retrograde vesicle trafficking, not a secreted/membrane ligand, while CD74 (invariant chain) is a genuine MHC-II chaperone receptor for MIF on antigen-presenting cells (DCs, B cells, macrophages). This pairing is very likely a database/algorithmic artefact arising from co-expression rather than a true extracellular ligand-receptor interaction.

short_description: Semaphorin-neuropilin; guidance cue regulating lymphatic/immune cell positioning
summary_description: SEMA3A is a secreted class-3 semaphorin that binds neuropilin-2 (NRP2), typically with plexin-A co-receptors, to transduce repulsive guidance and cytoskeletal signalling. SEMA3A is produced by stromal/neuronal and some epithelial cells while NRP2 is expressed on lymphatic endothelial cells, DCs and some T cells, contributing to lymphatic vessel patterning and immune cell positioning within lymphoid tissue.

short_description: Likely artefact; TNF-family ligand paired with MHC-II chain
summary_description: TNFSF9 (4-1BBL) is a genuine costimulatory TNF-superfamily ligand whose true receptor is TNFRSF9 (4-1BB) on activated T/NK cells, not HLA-DPA1, an MHC class II alpha chain that presents peptides to CD4 T cells via the TCR, not TNFSF9. This pairing is not a known biological signalling axis and most likely reflects a database/co-expression artefact rather than direct ligand-receptor engagement.

short_description: Likely non-canonical; collagen ligand paired with lymphatic VEGFR3
summary_description: COL1A2 is a fibrillar collagen ECM component typically engaging integrins/DDR receptors, whereas FLT4 (VEGFR3) is the receptor for VEGF-C/D on lymphatic endothelial cells controlling lymphangiogenesis. Direct COL1A2-FLT4 binding is not well established mechanistically; this likely reflects co-expression of stromal collagen with lymphatic endothelium in lymph node sinuses rather than a validated direct interaction.

short_description: Growth factor-proteoglycan; midkine binds syndecan-4 for adhesion/signalling
summary_description: MDK (midkine), a heparin-binding growth factor, binds syndecan-4 (SDC4), a cell-surface heparan sulfate proteoglycan, activating PI3K/PKC signalling that promotes cell migration, survival and adhesion. MDK is secreted by stromal cells, activated endothelium and some immune cells, while SDC4 is broadly expressed on lymphocytes, stromal/reticular cells and endothelium, supporting tissue remodeling and leukocyte adhesion in lymphoid niches.

short_description: Notch ligand-receptor; vascular DLL4 drives Notch2 signalling in immune cells
summary_description: DLL4 is a Notch-family ligand expressed on endothelial cells (including HEV) that engages NOTCH2 receptors via juxtacrine contact, inducing proteolytic Notch intracellular domain release and transcriptional programs. DLL4 is classically endothelial/HEV-derived while NOTCH2 is expressed on marginal zone B cells and some DCs/monocytes, supporting marginal zone B cell differentiation and myeloid/DC development in spleen and lymph node.

short_description: Sialomucin-selectin; HEV CD34 ligand engages L-selectin for lymphocyte homing
summary_description: CD34 is a sialomucin expressed on high endothelial venules that, when appropriately glycosylated/sulfated (as PNAd), serves as a ligand for SELL (L-selectin) on naive lymphocytes, mediating initial tethering/rolling during lymphocyte homing. This is a canonical HEV-lymphocyte homing interaction central to naive T and B cell entry into lymph node and tonsil.

short_description: Platelet GPIbα engages leukocyte Mac-1 integrin, adhesion bridge
summary_description: GP1BA is the platelet glycoprotein Ib-alpha subunit that can bind ITGAM_ITGB2 (Mac-1/CR3) on myeloid cells, mediating platelet-leukocyte adhesion and supporting leukocyte recruitment at sites of vascular/inflammatory activation. GP1BA is platelet-restricted while ITGAM_ITGB2 is expressed on macrophages, neutrophils and some DCs; in lymphoid tissue this likely reflects platelet-myeloid interactions at vascular/sinus interfaces rather than a lymphoid-intrinsic signal.

short_description: Cytokine-receptor; oncostatin M signals via gp130/LIFR complex
summary_description: OSM (oncostatin M), an IL-6 family cytokine, binds the heterodimeric receptor IL6ST (gp130) and LIFR, activating JAK/STAT3 signalling that promotes stromal remodeling and inflammatory responses. OSM is produced by activated macrophages, DCs and T cells, while IL6ST_LIFR is expressed on stromal fibroblastic reticular cells and endothelium, supporting stromal reorganization and cytokine networks in reactive lymphoid tissue.

short_description: Laminin-integrin; basement membrane ligand supports leukocyte/stromal adhesion
summary_description: LAMA4 (laminin alpha4) engages integrin ITGA9_ITGB1 (alpha9beta1), a laminin/ECM-binding integrin, triggering adhesion and migratory signalling. LAMA4 is produced by stromal and vascular basement membrane cells while ITGA9_ITGB1 is expressed on some lymphocytes, neutrophils and lymphatic endothelium, contributing to leukocyte trafficking across basement membranes and lymphatic vessel-associated adhesion in lymphoid organs.

short_description: Protease-scavenger receptor; MMP9 cleared/signals via LRP1 endocytic receptor
summary_description: MMP9 is a secreted matrix metalloproteinase that degrades ECM components and can also act as a ligand for LRP1, a multifunctional endocytic scavenger receptor mediating clearance and some intracellular signalling. MMP9 is produced by macrophages, neutrophils and activated stromal cells, while LRP1 is expressed on macrophages, DCs and stromal/fibroblastic cells, linking ECM remodeling to receptor-mediated clearance in lymphoid tissue remodeling.

short_description: Likely artefact; IL-6 cytokine paired with tissue factor receptor
summary_description: IL6 is a cytokine that normally signals through IL6R/IL6ST (gp130), not F3 (tissue factor), which is the receptor/cofactor for coagulation factor VIIa initiating the extrinsic clotting cascade. There is no established direct IL6-F3 ligand-receptor signalling axis; this pairing likely reflects co-expression of IL6 with tissue-factor-bearing stromal/endothelial cells rather than a genuine interaction, and should be treated as a probable database artefact.

short_description: Protease-tetraspanin; TSPAN14 regulates ADAM10 trafficking/sheddase activity
summary_description: ADAM10 is a membrane metalloprotease and TSPAN14 is a tetraspanin regulator that controls its surface expression, maturation and substrate access (e.g. Notch, cadherins); this is a regulatory/chaperone-like interaction rather than classical ligand-receptor signalling. Both are broadly expressed (epithelium, stromal and immune cells including FRCs, endothelium) with no lymphoid-zone restriction. Likely a database artefact of pairing a protease with its co-factor as 'ligand-receptor'.

short_description: DAMP-TLR4; stress protein activates innate inflammatory signalling
summary_description: HSPA1A (HSP70) released from stressed/dying cells acts as a danger-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) engaging TLR4 to trigger NF-κB-driven pro-inflammatory cytokine production. In lymphoid tissue, HSP70 can be released by stressed stromal, dendritic or dying germinal centre cells, while TLR4 is expressed on macrophages, DCs and some stromal cells, contributing to innate activation during inflammation/damage. HSP70 as a secreted TLR4 ligand is non-canonical/weakly supported and may reflect contamination or non-specific release rather than a dedicated signalling axis.

short_description: Chemokine-receptor; monocyte/myeloid chemoattraction, constitutive homeostatic chemokine
summary_description: CCL14 is a CC-chemokine that binds CCR1 (Gi-coupled GPCR) to drive chemotaxis of monocytes, macrophages and some granulocytes. In lymphoid organs, CCL14 can be produced by stromal/endothelial cells (HEV-associated) while CCR1 is expressed on monocytes/macrophages and some DCs, supporting myeloid recruitment into medullary/red pulp or sinus regions. CCL14 can also be processed to more potent forms; CCR1 binding is physiologically relevant but relatively minor compared to CCR1's main ligands (CCL3/CCL5).

short_description: ECM-adhesion receptor; laminin engages CD44 for stromal adhesion/migration
summary_description: LAMB1 (laminin beta-1 chain, part of basement membrane laminins) can bind CD44, a broadly expressed adhesion/hyaluronan receptor, promoting cell-matrix adhesion and migration signalling. Laminins are produced by stromal cells (FRCs, follicular dendritic cells, lymphatic/HEV basement membranes), while CD44 is expressed on nearly all leukocytes and stromal cells, supporting lymphocyte trafficking along reticular/basement-membrane scaffolds. This is a moderately supported but non-primary CD44 ligand interaction (hyaluronan is the canonical ligand).

short_description: Sialomucin-lectin; CD43 engages sialoadhesin on macrophages
summary_description: SPN (CD43, a sialomucin) carries sialylated glycans recognized by SIGLEC1 (CD169/sialoadhesin), a lectin receptor mediating cell-cell adhesion and antigen capture rather than classical signalling. SPN is broadly expressed on T cells, DCs and leukocytes, while SIGLEC1 is a marker of subcapsular sinus and medullary macrophages in lymph node/spleen, important for capturing antigen/virus and presenting to B cells. Biologically plausible, supporting macrophage-mediated antigen capture in the SCS.

short_description: Enzyme-aGPCR; transglutaminase2 engages adhesion GPCR GPR56
summary_description: TGM2 (transglutaminase 2) is a secreted/cell-surface crosslinking enzyme that can act as a ligand for ADGRG1 (GPR56), an adhesion GPCR, modulating cell adhesion and RhoA signalling. TGM2 is expressed by stromal/endothelial and myeloid cells and ECM-associated; ADGRG1 is found on some lymphocyte subsets (e.g., NK, CD8 T cells) and oligodendrocytes outside lymphoid tissue. This pairing is relatively non-canonical in lymphoid organs and weakly characterized compared to GPR56's main ligand collagen III.

short_description: Peptide hormone-orphan GPCR; adrenomedullin scavenged by endothelial GPR182
summary_description: ADM (adrenomedullin) is a vasoactive peptide that can bind GPR182, an orphan/atypical GPCR now recognized as a scavenger receptor for adrenomedullin, limiting its vasodilatory/lymphangiogenic signalling rather than transducing classical downstream signalling. GPR182 is highly expressed on lymphatic and blood vascular endothelium (including HEVs) in lymphoid organs, while ADM is produced by stromal/endothelial cells, regulating vascular tone and lymphatic remodeling. GPR182 acts mainly as a decoy/clearance receptor, so this should be flagged as non-signalling/scavenging rather than canonical activation.

short_description: ECM glycoprotein-integrin; spondin2 engages alpha5 integrin for adhesion
summary_description: SPON2 (M-spondin/mindin) is an extracellular matrix glycoprotein that binds integrins including ITGA5 (as part of α5β1), promoting leukocyte adhesion and migration, and also has roles in innate immune opsonization. SPON2 is produced by stromal cells and macrophages; ITGA5 is expressed on monocytes, DCs and some lymphocytes, supporting myeloid adhesion/trafficking within lymphoid stroma. Reasonably supported interaction, though ITGA5 pairing partner (ITGB1) is often implied but not listed here.

short_description: Laminin-integrin; basement-membrane adhesion via α7β1 integrin
summary_description: LAMA4 (laminin alpha-4) is a basement-membrane ECM component engaging the ITGA7_ITGB1 integrin heterodimer to mediate cell-matrix adhesion and migration signalling. LAMA4 is produced by stromal/endothelial cells (including HEV and lymphatic basement membranes), while ITGA7_ITGB1 is mainly described on muscle and some stromal/mesenchymal cells; expression on lymphoid leukocytes is limited, making this a plausible but less classically immune-specific adhesion axis.

short_description: Chaperone-receptor; RAP regulates LRP1 endocytic receptor folding/ligand binding
summary_description: LRPAP1 (RAP) is an intracellular/ER chaperone for LRP1 that also acts as a competitive ligand regulating LRP1's endocytic and signalling functions (e.g., lipoprotein, protease clearance) rather than a classical secreted signalling ligand. LRP1 is broadly expressed on macrophages, stromal cells and some DCs, involved in efferocytosis and lipid handling. This interaction is largely a chaperone/regulatory relationship and should be considered non-canonical as a bona fide intercellular ligand-receptor signalling pair.

short_description: DAMP-TLR2; annexin A2 triggers innate inflammatory activation
summary_description: ANXA2 (annexin A2), normally intracellular/membrane-associated, can be externalized and act as a DAMP engaging TLR2 to activate NF-κB-driven innate immune signalling. ANXA2 can be released by stressed epithelial, endothelial or immune cells, while TLR2 is expressed on macrophages, DCs and some B cells in lymphoid tissue, contributing to innate sensing during tissue stress/infection. Given ANXA2's primarily intracellular localization, this pairing is weakly supported and may reflect non-specific or artefactual extracellular detection.

short_description: Co-inhibitory checkpoint; BTLA-HVEM dampens T cell activation
summary_description: BTLA engages TNFRSF14 (HVEM), delivering inhibitory signalling that attenuates T cell receptor activation, functioning as an immune checkpoint. BTLA is expressed on T cells, B cells and some DCs, while HVEM (TNFRSF14) is broadly expressed on T cells, stromal and epithelial cells, with this interaction prominent in germinal centre and T zone regulation of lymphocyte activation thresholds. This is a well-established canonical co-inhibitory checkpoint pair.

short_description: Adhesion molecule-caveolin; ICAM1 clustering links to caveolar signalling/transcytosis
summary_description: ICAM1 is a surface adhesion molecule for leukocyte integrins (LFA-1), and its clustering can recruit intracellular CAV1 (caveolin-1) to organize caveolae for transendothelial migration/signalling; CAV1 is not a conventional cell-surface receptor. ICAM1 is expressed on endothelium (HEVs), FRCs and activated APCs, while CAV1 is an intracellular/membrane-scaffold protein in endothelial cells. This pairing is non-canonical as a ligand-receptor axis since CAV1 is intracellular, likely reflecting a downstream adaptor rather than direct receptor engagement.

short_description: Anti-inflammatory peptide-GPCR; annexin A1 resolves inflammation via FPR1
summary_description: ANXA1 (annexin A1), often cleaved to active peptides, binds FPR1 (a Gi-coupled formyl peptide receptor) to promote resolution of inflammation and modulate neutrophil/macrophage function. ANXA1 is produced by neutrophils, macrophages and epithelial/stromal cells, while FPR1 is expressed on neutrophils, monocytes and macrophages, relevant in medullary/sinus macrophage regulation and inflammation resolution in lymphoid tissue. This is a reasonably well-supported anti-inflammatory signalling axis.

short_description: ECM proteoglycan-adhesion receptor; versican engages CD44 for stromal retention
summary_description: VCAN (versican), a large ECM chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan, binds CD44 (also a hyaluronan receptor) to promote cell adhesion, retention and modulation of immune cell migration within stroma. VCAN is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells and other stromal cells, while CD44 is broadly expressed on lymphocytes, DCs and macrophages, supporting lymphocyte positioning/retention in T-zone/stromal niches. This is a biologically plausible ECM-adhesion interaction, complementary to CD44's canonical ligand hyaluronan.

short_description: Homophilic-like adhesion ligand; CD99 engages inhibitory receptor PILRB
summary_description: CD99 is a transmembrane glycoprotein engaging PILRB, a paired immunoglobulin-like receptor, triggering ITIM-mediated inhibitory signalling; also implicated in leukocyte transendothelial migration and T-cell adhesion. CD99 is broadly expressed on thymocytes, T cells, and endothelium (HEV), while PILRB is expressed on myeloid cells/DCs; relevant to leukocyte trafficking across HEV in lymphoid tissue. Evidence for this specific pairing in spatial lymphoid data is relatively weak/non-canonical compared to CD99-CD99 homotypic interactions.

short_description: ECM laminin-integrin adhesion; supports basement membrane attachment and migration
summary_description: Laminin gamma1 chain (LAMC1), part of laminin heterotrimers in basement membranes, binds integrin alpha6beta1, activating FAK/ILK signalling for cell adhesion and migration. Stromal/fibroblastic reticular cells and endothelium (including HEV) produce laminins, while integrin alpha6beta1 is expressed on lymphocytes, DCs, and epithelial cells, supporting basement membrane anchoring and transmigration in lymphoid stroma and HEV zones.

short_description: Laminin-CD44 adhesion; supports stromal adhesion and leukocyte migration
summary_description: LAMC1 (laminin gamma1) binds CD44, a hyaladherin receptor, promoting adhesion to extracellular matrix and modulating cytoskeletal signalling and migration. Laminin is produced by stromal/FRC and basement membrane cells, while CD44 is broadly expressed on lymphocytes, macrophages, and DCs; this interaction supports lymphocyte retention/migration within stromal niches of lymph node and spleen.

short_description: Collagen-syndecan adhesion; ECM binding supporting plasma cell niches
summary_description: Collagen VI alpha3 chain binds syndecan-1 (CD138) heparan sulfate proteoglycan, mediating cell-matrix adhesion and potentially modulating growth factor presentation. COL6A3 is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells/stroma, while SDC1 is highly expressed on plasma cells and some epithelial/stromal cells; relevant to plasma cell survival niches in medullary cords and red pulp.

short_description: Adhesion molecule-tetraspanin complex; supports cell adhesion and migration
summary_description: L1CAM, an Ig-superfamily adhesion molecule, associates with tetraspanin CD9 at the membrane to modulate integrin clustering and promote cell motility/adhesion signalling. L1CAM is expressed on neurons, some endothelium and immune subsets, while CD9 is broadly expressed on leukocytes, platelets, and stromal cells; functional relevance in lymphoid tissue is less well characterized and this pairing is relatively non-canonical/weakly supported.

short_description: Non-classical MHC-I inhibitory receptor; immune checkpoint signalling
summary_description: HLA-F, a non-classical MHC class I molecule, engages LILRB2 (ILT4), an inhibitory receptor with ITIMs, dampening myeloid and NK/T cell activation. HLA-F is expressed on activated lymphocytes/endothelium while LILRB2 is expressed on myeloid cells, monocytes, and DCs; this axis contributes to immune checkpoint regulation and tolerance within lymphoid tissue myeloid compartments.

short_description: Amyloid precursor-tetraspanin; likely database artefact, non-immune function
summary_description: Amyloid precursor protein (APP) is a transmembrane protein with roles in neuronal signalling and proteolytic processing; TSPAN12 is a tetraspanin involved in Norrin/FZD4 signalling for vascular development. Both are broadly expressed (APP ubiquitous, TSPAN12 on endothelium); this pairing lacks established immunological signalling relevance and is likely a database artefact rather than a biologically meaningful lymphoid interaction.

short_description: Annexin-adrenergic receptor; non-canonical, ADRA2A not a true chemokine/annexin receptor
summary_description: Annexin A1 (ANXA1) normally signals through FPR2 (ALX/FPR2) to promote resolution of inflammation and leukocyte migration; ADRA2A is an adrenergic GPCR for catecholamines, not a validated ANXA1 receptor. ANXA1 is expressed by macrophages, neutrophils, and epithelium; ADRA2A is expressed on neurons/platelets/some stromal cells. This pairing is non-canonical and likely a database artefact rather than a direct functional interaction.

short_description: Complement regulator-adhesion GPCR; modulates leukocyte adhesion/signalling
summary_description: CD55 (DAF), a complement decay-accelerating factor, binds ADGRE2 (EMR2), an adhesion GPCR, triggering mechanosensitive signalling in myeloid cells. CD55 is broadly expressed on stromal and hematopoietic cells including endothelium, while ADGRE2 is expressed on monocytes/macrophages and granulocytes; relevant to myeloid cell adhesion/activation in marginal zone and medullary sinus macrophage populations.

short_description: Matricellular protein-syndecan; modulates stromal adhesion and signalling
summary_description: Tenascin-C (TNC), a matricellular ECM glycoprotein, binds syndecan-4, activating PKCα and focal adhesion signalling, modulating cell adhesion and migration. TNC is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells and activated stroma, while SDC4 is expressed broadly on stromal cells, endothelium, and some leukocytes; implicated in stromal remodeling within T-zone/FRC network during immune responses.

short_description: Protease-pseudoprotease complex; controls ADAM17 maturation and ectodomain shedding
summary_description: ADAM17 (TACE) is a sheddase requiring RHBDF2 (iRhom2) as an obligate cofactor for trafficking/maturation, enabling cleavage of TNF, TGFα, and other substrates—this is an intracellular/membrane-trafficking partnership rather than a classical ligand-receptor signal. Both are expressed broadly in myeloid cells and epithelium; in lymphoid tissue relevant to macrophage/DC cytokine shedding. Receptor-ligand framing here is somewhat atypical since this is a biogenesis complex, not surface signalling.

short_description: Growth factor-nucleolin; promotes proliferation and survival signalling
summary_description: Midkine (MDK), a heparin-binding growth factor, binds cell-surface nucleolin (NCL) to activate PI3K/Akt and ERK pathways promoting proliferation, survival, and migration. MDK is produced by stromal/epithelial cells and some immune cells, while NCL (canonically nuclear/nucleolar) can also localize to cell surface on proliferating lymphocytes and endothelium; surface NCL as receptor is less canonical and should be interpreted cautiously.

short_description: Intracellular G-protein subunit; not a true secreted ligand, artefact
summary_description: GNAI2 is an intracellular heterotrimeric G-protein alpha subunit that couples to GPCRs including CNR1 (cannabinoid receptor 1) downstream of ligand binding—it is not a secreted/membrane ligand itself. CNR1 is expressed on neurons and some immune cells; this pairing represents a database artefact arising from misannotating an intracellular signalling component as a ligand rather than a genuine cell-cell interaction.

short_description: Chaperone/antagonist-LDL receptor; regulates lipoprotein receptor trafficking, non-canonical signalling
summary_description: LRPAP1 (RAP) is an intracellular/ER chaperone that binds LDLR family members to prevent premature ligand binding during receptor trafficking, rather than acting as a genuine extracellular signalling ligand. LDLR is broadly expressed on hepatocytes and various cells including some immune/stromal cells for lipid uptake; this interaction is largely a chaperone-receptor biogenesis relationship and a likely database artefact in a cell-cell communication context.

short_description: Basement membrane collagen-syndecan; supports stromal/plasma cell adhesion niches
summary_description: Collagen IV alpha2 chain, a basement membrane structural collagen, binds syndecan-1 heparan sulfate proteoglycan mediating cell-matrix adhesion and potential growth factor co-receptor function. COL4A2 is produced by endothelial/basement membrane and stromal cells (HEV, FRC), while SDC1 is prominently expressed on plasma cells and epithelium; relevant to plasma cell niche adhesion in medullary cords and perivascular regions.

short_description: Adhesion; endothelial VWF engages myeloid SIRPA, platelet/myeloid interaction
summary_description: VWF is an endothelial/platelet adhesion glycoprotein that can bind SIRPA, a myeloid inhibitory immunoreceptor (canonical SIRPA ligand is CD47); downstream this is thought to modulate leukocyte-endothelial adhesion rather than classic SIRPA signalling. In lymphoid tissue VWF is expressed by HEV/vascular endothelium and megakaryocytes/platelets, while SIRPA is on macrophages/myeloid and dendritic cells, relevant to vascular-myeloid crosstalk at HEV. This pairing is weakly supported/non-canonical compared to the well-established CD47-SIRPA axis and may reflect a database-predicted interaction rather than a validated signalling pair.

short_description: Chemokine-receptor; recruits activated T cells, NK cells, pDCs
summary_description: CXCL11 is a chemokine that binds and activates CXCR3, a Gi-coupled GPCR, triggering chemotaxis and integrin activation. In lymphoid organs CXCL11 is produced by stromal cells, FRCs, endothelium and IFN-activated macrophages/DCs in the T zone, while CXCR3 is expressed on activated/effector CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, Th1 cells, NK cells and plasmacytoid DCs, guiding their migration into T-zone and inflamed areas. This is a canonical, well-supported chemokine-receptor interaction.

short_description: Non-canonical; CXCL11 with adrenergic receptor, likely database artefact
summary_description: CXCL11 is a CXCR3-ligand chemokine; ADRA2A is a Gi-coupled alpha2-adrenergic receptor for catecholamines (norepinephrine/epinephrine), not a chemokine receptor. Any signalling outcome predicted from this pairing is not biologically established. This interaction is non-canonical and almost certainly a database/algorithmic artefact arising from promiscuous ligand-receptor resource annotations rather than a true CXCL11-ADRA2A signalling axis.

short_description: Death ligand-receptor; TRAIL induces apoptosis via DR5
summary_description: TNFSF10 (TRAIL) binds TNFRSF10B (DR5), a death-domain-containing receptor, triggering caspase-8-dependent apoptosis in target cells. In lymphoid tissue TRAIL is expressed by NK cells, activated T cells, macrophages and some DCs, while DR5 is broadly expressed on stressed, infected, or malignant lymphocytes and stromal cells, contributing to immune surveillance and germinal centre B-cell/activated lymphocyte homeostasis. This is a canonical, well-validated apoptotic signalling pair.

short_description: Peptide hormone-receptor; adrenomedullin acts on endothelium, vascular tone
summary_description: ADM (adrenomedullin) signals through CALCRL complexed with RAMP2/3 (CLR/RAMP) to activate cAMP/PKA, promoting vasodilation, endothelial barrier stabilization and lymphangiogenesis. In lymphoid organs ADM is produced by stromal/endothelial cells and macrophages, while CALCRL is expressed on blood and lymphatic endothelium (HEV, lymphatics), supporting vascular integrity and fluid/lymphocyte trafficking. This is a canonical endothelial signalling axis, though RAMP co-receptor usage is often omitted in these analyses.

short_description: Decoy receptor; TRAIL binds non-signalling DcR2, dampens apoptosis
summary_description: TNFSF10 (TRAIL) can bind TNFRSF10D (DcR2), a decoy receptor lacking a functional death domain, which competitively inhibits TRAIL-induced apoptosis rather than transmitting death signals. DcR2 is expressed on various stromal and hematopoietic cells including some lymphocytes and epithelial/stromal cells in lymphoid tissue, serving a protective, apoptosis-dampening role. This interaction, while real, is a decoy/non-signalling receptor pairing and should not be interpreted as pro-apoptotic.

short_description: Cytokine-receptor; oncostatin M drives stromal remodeling, inflammation
summary_description: OSM (oncostatin M) binds the heterodimeric receptor complex IL6ST (gp130)/OSMR (type II receptor), activating JAK/STAT3 signalling to promote stromal remodeling, fibrosis-like changes and inflammatory gene induction. In lymphoid tissue OSM is produced by activated macrophages, neutrophils and T cells, while IL6ST/OSMR is expressed on fibroblastic reticular cells (FRCs), stromal cells and endothelium, driving stromal activation and extracellular matrix remodeling in inflamed lymphoid niches. This is a canonical, well-supported cytokine signalling complex.

short_description: Galectin-lectin; Galectin-9 engages mannose receptor, likely weak/non-canonical
summary_description: LGALS9 (Galectin-9) is a beta-galactoside-binding lectin best known for signalling through TIM-3/CD44/PD-1, with glycan-dependent interactions; MRC2 (Endo180/uPARAP) is a mannose-family receptor mediating collagen endocytosis on fibroblasts/macrophages. A direct LGALS9-MRC2 signalling interaction is not well characterized in the literature. In lymphoid tissue Galectin-9 is expressed by macrophages, DCs, FDCs and endothelium, while MRC2 marks stromal fibroblasts/FRCs; this pairing is weakly supported and likely reflects glycan-mediated lectin binding rather than a validated signalling axis.

short_description: Disintegrin-integrin; ADAM15 engages ITGA9 subunit, adhesion/migration
summary_description: ADAM15 is a disintegrin-metalloprotease that can engage integrins (including ITGA9, typically paired with ITGB1) via its disintegrin domain, supporting cell-cell adhesion and potentially migration independent of its protease activity. ADAM15 is expressed on endothelium, leukocytes and some stromal cells, while ITGA9 is found on lymphatic endothelium, smooth muscle and some fibroblasts; in lymphoid tissue this may support leukocyte-endothelial or stromal adhesion. This is a less-common, moderately supported integrin-ligand interaction compared to classical chemokine/adhesion pairs.

short_description: DAMP-PRR; biglycan activates innate immune TLR4 signalling
summary_description: BGN (biglycan), a soluble extracellular matrix proteoglycan released upon tissue damage, acts as a danger-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) that engages TLR4 (often with TLR2/CD14) to activate NF-kB and pro-inflammatory cytokine production. In lymphoid tissue BGN is produced by stromal/fibroblastic cells and ECM, while TLR4 is expressed on macrophages, DCs and some stromal cells, contributing to innate immune activation during tissue remodeling/inflammation. This is a biologically supported DAMP-PRR interaction, distinct from classical ligand-receptor signalling.

short_description: Notch ligand-receptor; vascular DLL4 signals to NOTCH3 on mural cells
summary_description: DLL4 is a Notch ligand that engages NOTCH3 via juxtacrine contact, triggering gamma-secretase-mediated release of the NOTCH3 intracellular domain to regulate transcription, classically governing arterial specification and vascular mural cell differentiation. DLL4 is expressed on arterial/HEV endothelium, while NOTCH3 is expressed on pericytes, vascular smooth muscle and some stromal cells, supporting vascular stabilization and HEV maturation in lymphoid organs. This is a canonical, well-established vascular signalling pair.

short_description: Endothelial adhesion; multimerin-2 and endosialin, vascular/stromal crosstalk
summary_description: MMRN2 (multimerin-2) is an endothelial-specific extracellular matrix glycoprotein that can interact with CD248 (endosialin/TEM1), a pericyte/fibroblast surface glycoprotein implicated in angiogenesis and stromal remodeling; their interaction is thought to modulate vascular-stromal adhesion and angiogenic signalling. In lymphoid tissue MMRN2 marks blood vascular endothelium (including HEV) while CD248 marks perivascular fibroblasts/pericytes and activated stromal cells, relevant to vascular niche organization. This is a moderately supported, less widely characterized endothelial-stromal interaction.

short_description: Chemokine-protease; DPP4 cleaves/inactivates CCL5, regulatory not signalling
summary_description: CCL5 (RANTES) is a chemokine that signals through CCR1/CCR3/CCR5, but DPP4 (CD26) is a cell-surface protease that cleaves and inactivates CCL5 rather than acting as its signalling receptor, altering its receptor selectivity. CCL5 is produced by T cells, platelets and stromal cells, while DPP4 is expressed on activated T cells, epithelium and endothelium; in lymphoid tissue this represents a proteolytic regulatory interaction, not classical chemokine signalling, and should be interpreted as such.

short_description: Growth factor-receptor; IGF1 cross-activates insulin receptor, survival signalling
summary_description: IGF1 primarily signals through IGF1R but can cross-react with INSR (and IGF1R/INSR hybrid receptors) to activate PI3K/AKT and MAPK pathways, promoting cell growth, survival and metabolism. In lymphoid tissue IGF1 is produced by stromal cells and macrophages, while INSR is broadly expressed on lymphocytes, stromal and endothelial cells, supporting metabolic fitness and survival of immune cells. This cross-reactive pairing is real but secondary to the canonical IGF1-IGF1R axis.

short_description: Lipase-receptor; lipoprotein lipase bridges lipoproteins to LRP1 endocytosis
summary_description: LPL (lipoprotein lipase) can act as a bridging ligand for LRP1, a multifunctional endocytic/scavenger receptor, facilitating lipoprotein particle uptake and clearance rather than classical signal transduction. LPL is produced by macrophages, adipocytes and stromal cells, while LRP1 is broadly expressed on macrophages, endothelium, fibroblasts and some stromal cells in lymphoid tissue, supporting lipid handling and efferocytosis-related clearance functions. This is a scavenger/endocytic interaction rather than a canonical signalling ligand-receptor pair.

short_description: Chemokine-protease; CXCL10 truncation by DPP4 limits CXCR3 signalling
summary_description: CXCL10 is a CXCR3-binding chemokine; DPP4 (CD26) is a cell-surface serine protease that cleaves CXCL10 N-terminally, reducing its chemotactic potency rather than acting as a classical signalling receptor. CXCL10 is made by stromal cells/macrophages/DCs in T zones; DPP4 is expressed on activated T cells, endothelium and stroma. This is a non-canonical, enzymatic (not signalling) ligand-receptor pair likely reflecting chemokine processing rather than true receptor engagement.

short_description: Osteopontin-CD44; promotes macrophage/T-cell adhesion, survival, migration
summary_description: SPP1 (osteopontin) binds CD44 (and integrins) activating adhesion, PI3K/Akt survival and migration signalling. SPP1 is produced by macrophages, DCs and stromal/fibroblastic cells; CD44 is broadly expressed on T/B lymphocytes, macrophages and FRCs. This interaction supports leukocyte retention/migration within lymphoid stroma and is a well-established, canonical pair in immune niches including germinal centres and T zones.

short_description: Lymphotoxin-alpha; non-canonical, RIPK1 is intracellular adaptor not receptor
summary_description: LTA (lymphotoxin-alpha) normally signals via TNFR1/TNFR2 or LTβR (as LTα1β2 heterotrimer) to drive NF-κB signalling essential for lymphoid organogenesis (HEV, FDC networks, follicle formation). RIPK1 is an intracellular kinase/adaptor downstream of TNFR signalling, not a surface receptor, so this pairing is a likely database artefact reflecting pathway proximity rather than a genuine ligand-receptor interaction.

short_description: Midkine-SORL1; growth factor signalling, stromal/vascular trophic support
summary_description: Midkine (MDK) is a heparin-binding growth factor that can engage SORL1 (sortilin-related receptor) involved in intracellular trafficking/endocytosis and modulation of growth factor signalling. MDK is expressed by stromal, endothelial and some immune cells; SORL1 is expressed on macrophages, neurons and stromal cells. This is a less well-characterized, moderately supported interaction relevant to tissue remodeling/vascular niches rather than classical lymphocyte signalling.

short_description: Angiopoietin-like4-VE-cadherin; destabilizes endothelial junctions, modulates HEV permeability
summary_description: ANGPTL4 disrupts VE-cadherin (CDH5) junctional integrity, increasing vascular permeability, rather than acting as a canonical agonist ligand for a dedicated receptor. ANGPTL4 is secreted by stromal/hypoxic or metabolic cells; CDH5 is specific to vascular/high endothelial venule endothelial cells. Biologically relevant to HEV permeability and lymphocyte extravasation, though mechanistically indirect (disruption of adhesion complex) rather than classical receptor activation.

short_description: Presenilin1-Notch3; intracellular protease, not a secreted ligand
summary_description: PSEN1 is the catalytic subunit of γ-secretase that cleaves NOTCH3 intracellularly to release NICD for nuclear signalling; it is not a secreted/membrane ligand engaging NOTCH3 extracellularly. NOTCH3 is expressed on pericytes/vascular smooth muscle and some stromal cells. This pairing is a database artefact arising from pathway membership (intramembrane proteolysis) rather than a bona fide ligand-receptor interaction.

short_description: Chemokine-syndecan; heparan sulfate co-receptor presents CXCL10 for haptotaxis
summary_description: CXCL10 binds glycosaminoglycans on syndecan-4 (SDC4), facilitating chemokine immobilization/presentation on stromal and endothelial surfaces that supports haptotactic gradients rather than direct GPCR signalling. CXCL10 is produced by stromal cells, macrophages and IFN-stimulated cells; SDC4 is broadly expressed on stromal, endothelial and some immune cells. This is a supportive, non-canonical co-receptor interaction complementing CXCR3-mediated T-cell recruitment to T zones.

short_description: SDF-1-protease; DPP4 truncates CXCL12, limiting CXCR4 chemotaxis
summary_description: CXCL12 (SDF-1) normally signals via CXCR4/ACKR3; DPP4 cleaves its N-terminal dipeptide, inactivating CXCR4 agonism and altering CXCR3-binding specificity of the truncated form. CXCL12 is produced by stromal/reticular cells (e.g., FRCs, perivascular cells) supporting HSC/lymphocyte homing; DPP4 is on endothelium and activated lymphocytes. This is an enzymatic processing interaction, not a classical receptor-signalling pair.

short_description: Coagulation factor-integrin; macrophage/fibroblast adhesion and matrix crosslinking
summary_description: F13A1 (coagulation factor XIII-A) can bind integrin β1 (ITGB1) on cell surfaces influencing adhesion and extracellular matrix crosslinking, relevant to tissue remodeling. F13A1 is a classic marker of macrophages (especially perivascular/subcapsular sinus macrophages) in lymphoid tissue; ITGB1 is broadly expressed on stromal cells, lymphocytes and macrophages. This is a plausible but moderately supported adhesion-related interaction rather than a canonical signalling axis.

short_description: Chemokine-adrenergic receptor mismatch; likely database artefact, no known binding
summary_description: CXCL9 is a canonical CXCR3 ligand recruiting Th1 cells/NK cells in T zones and inflamed germinal centres; ADRA2A is an alpha-2 adrenergic GPCR for catecholamines with no established chemokine-binding activity. This pairing is a non-canonical, likely spurious database artefact resulting from promiscuous ligand-receptor inference algorithms rather than genuine CXCL9 engagement of an adrenergic receptor.

short_description: Matrix metalloproteinase-integrin; macrophage/neutrophil adhesion and matrix remodeling
summary_description: MMP9 can bind integrin αM (ITGAM/CD11b, part of Mac-1) on myeloid cells, localizing proteolytic activity to the cell surface for matrix remodeling and migration, distinct from its catalytic ECM-degrading function. MMP9 is secreted by neutrophils/macrophages; ITGAM is expressed on macrophages, neutrophils and some DCs. Biologically relevant to myeloid trafficking in medullary/sinus regions, a moderately supported non-classical ligand-receptor pair.

short_description: Coagulation factor VIII-LDLR; clearance receptor, not immune signalling
summary_description: F8 (coagulation Factor VIII) is cleared from circulation via LDLR-family receptors (including LDLR/LRP1), representing a scavenging/clearance interaction rather than an immune signalling event. F8 is produced by endothelial cells; LDLR is broadly expressed on hepatocytes, endothelium and some stromal/immune cells. This pair is largely irrelevant to lymphoid immune crosstalk and likely reflects a database artefact from generic receptor-ligand databases.

short_description: Adhesion molecule-common gamma chain; non-canonical, mismatched receptor pairing
summary_description: ICAM1 is an adhesion ligand for integrins LFA-1/Mac-1 mediating firm adhesion at HEVs and immune synapses; IL2RG (common gamma chain) is a cytokine receptor subunit for IL-2/4/7/9/15/21 with no known ICAM1-binding activity. This is a non-canonical, likely spurious pairing arising from co-expression-based inference rather than true direct molecular interaction.

short_description: Laminin-integrin α6β1; basement membrane adhesion for stromal/vascular cells
summary_description: LAMB2 (laminin subunit beta-2) engages integrin α6β1 (ITGA6_ITGB1) mediating cell-basement membrane adhesion and signalling for cell polarity/migration. LAMB2 is produced by endothelial, epithelial and stromal (FRC) cells forming basement membranes; ITGA6_ITGB1 is expressed on endothelial, epithelial and some leukocyte subsets. This is a canonical, well-supported structural adhesion interaction important for HEV and stromal scaffold integrity.

short_description: Secretin-RAMP2; unconventional pairing, RAMP2 normally partners CALCRL
summary_description: SCT (secretin) canonically signals through the secretin receptor (SCTR), a class B GPCR; RAMP2 is an accessory protein that typically modulates CALCRL (calcitonin receptor-like receptor) for adrenomedullin/CGRP signalling, not secretin. This pairing is non-canonical and weakly supported, likely reflecting database inference of RAMP-GPCR promiscuity rather than confirmed direct SCT-RAMP2 interaction; neither is a typical lymphoid-tissue signalling axis.

short_description: Notch ligand-receptor; induces lateral/arterial and T-cell fate signalling
summary_description: DLL1 is a transmembrane Notch ligand that engages NOTCH3, triggering gamma-secretase-mediated release of NICD3 and canonical Notch transcriptional signalling. In lymphoid tissue DLL1 is expressed by stromal/endothelial cells (e.g. HEV, perivascular/pericyte-like fibroblasts) while NOTCH3 marks mural cells/pericytes and some stromal subsets, supporting vascular stabilisation and stromal niche maintenance; also relevant to T-cell lineage decisions in thymus-adjacent contexts.

short_description: Lymphangiogenic growth factor-coreceptor; promotes lymphatic vessel growth
summary_description: VEGFC binds the co-receptor NRP2 (alongside VEGFR3/FLT4) to enhance VEGFR3 signalling, driving lymphatic endothelial proliferation and sprouting. VEGFC is produced by stromal/fibroblastic reticular cells and macrophages, while NRP2 is expressed on lymphatic endothelial cells, underpinning lymphangiogenesis and lymph node remodeling during immune responses.

short_description: Canonical TGF-beta signalling; immune suppression and stromal fibrosis
summary_description: TGFB1 binds the TGFBR1_TGFBR2 heterodimeric receptor complex, activating SMAD2/3 signalling that drives immunosuppression, Treg induction, and fibroblast/ECM remodeling. Ligand is produced broadly by Tregs, macrophages and stromal cells, while the receptor complex is expressed on T cells, fibroblastic reticular cells and endothelium, key to T-zone tolerance and capsule/stromal fibrosis.

short_description: Non-canonical; BAFF paired with transferrin receptor, likely artefact
summary_description: TNFSF13B (BAFF) is a TNF-family ligand whose canonical receptors are TNFRSF13B/TACI, TNFRSF13C/BAFFR and TNFRSF17/BCMA; TFRC (transferrin receptor/CD71) is an iron-uptake receptor unrelated to TNF signalling. This pairing is not a known biological receptor-ligand interaction and likely reflects a database co-expression artefact rather than true signalling, despite both being upregulated in germinal centre B cells/myeloid cells.

short_description: ECM-syndecan adhesion; collagen anchoring of plasma cells/stroma
summary_description: COL1A1 (fibrillar collagen I) binds the heparan sulfate proteoglycan SDC1 (CD138), mediating cell-matrix adhesion and modulating growth factor presentation. Collagen is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells/capsule fibroblasts, while SDC1 is highly expressed on plasma cells and marginal zone/medullary stromal cells, supporting plasma cell niche retention and stromal scaffold organisation.

short_description: Laminin-integrin adhesion; basement membrane attachment for migrating cells
summary_description: LAMA5, a basement-membrane laminin subunit, engages the ITGA9_ITGB1 integrin heterodimer to mediate cell adhesion and migration along basement membranes. Laminin is produced by stromal/endothelial basement membranes (HEV, lymphatics, FRC conduits) while ITGA9_ITGB1 is expressed on migrating leukocytes and some stromal cells, supporting trafficking through reticular/vascular structures.

short_description: Non-canonical; intracellular protease listed as ligand for CD44, artefact
summary_description: PSEN1 (presenilin-1) is the catalytic subunit of the intracellular gamma-secretase complex, not a secreted or membrane-displayed ligand; CD44 is a cell-surface adhesion/hyaluronan receptor. While PSEN1 can proteolytically cleave CD44's intracellular domain, this is an intracrine proteolytic event, not a ligand-receptor signalling interaction, so this pairing is best regarded as a database artefact from co-expression/processing annotation rather than genuine paracrine signalling.

short_description: TAM receptor tyrosine kinase; efferocytosis and immune dampening
summary_description: GAS6 binds the receptor tyrosine kinase MERTK, triggering phagocytic clearance of apoptotic cells and dampening inflammatory signalling. GAS6 is produced by macrophages, dendritic cells and stromal cells, while MERTK is expressed on tingible-body macrophages and DCs, central to clearance of apoptotic germinal centre B cells and maintenance of tolerance.

short_description: Weakly supported; neurotensin paired with low-affinity neurotrophin receptor
summary_description: NTS (neurotensin) is a neuropeptide that canonically signals through NTSR1/NTSR2/SORT1 GPCRs/receptors, not NGFR (p75NTR), which is a TNFR-superfamily neurotrophin receptor for NGF/proNGF and other neurotrophins. This pairing lacks established direct binding evidence and likely reflects database inference from co-expression in perivascular/neuronal-associated stromal cells rather than a validated ligand-receptor interaction.

short_description: LIGHT-HVEM; lymphoid stroma crosstalk promoting lymphoid organogenesis
summary_description: TNFSF14 (LIGHT) binds TNFRSF14 (HVEM), activating NF-kB signalling that supports lymphoid tissue organisation and T-cell costimulation. LIGHT is expressed by activated T cells, NK cells and DCs, while HVEM is broadly expressed on stromal cells, FRCs and lymphocytes, contributing to secondary lymphoid organ stromal development and immune activation.

short_description: Weak/atypical; CTGF-mannose-6-phosphate receptor matrix sequestration interaction
summary_description: CCN2 (CTGF) is a matricellular protein that can bind IGF2R (cation-independent mannose-6-phosphate receptor) primarily for clearance/sequestration of CTGF and modulation of TGF-beta/IGF availability, rather than direct receptor signal transduction. CCN2 is produced by fibroblasts/stromal cells, IGF2R is broadly expressed; this interaction is non-canonical as a signalling axis and mainly reflects ligand scavenging.

short_description: Non-canonical; metalloprotease paired with GPNMB, likely artefact
summary_description: ADAM10 is a membrane-anchored sheddase (processing Notch, CD23, and other substrates), not a conventional secreted ligand, while GPNMB is a type I transmembrane glycoprotein expressed on macrophages/dendritic cells with roles in adhesion and immune regulation. There is no established direct ligand-receptor binding between these two; this pairing likely reflects a database inference from co-expression or protease-substrate proximity rather than genuine signalling.

short_description: Non-canonical; low-affinity IgE receptor paired with complement integrin
summary_description: FCER2 (CD23) is the low-affinity IgE Fc receptor/C-type lectin found on B cells and FDCs, while ITGAM_ITGB2 (Mac-1/CR3) is a complement/ICAM receptor on myeloid cells. CD23 can engage integrins including ITGAM_ITGB2 in some reports to modulate inflammatory mediator release, but this is a weakly characterised, non-canonical interaction relative to CD23's main IgE/CD21 functions in germinal centre B cell-FDC interactions.

short_description: Secretin-RAMP accessory subunit; atypical GPCR modulatory interaction
summary_description: SCT (secretin) classically signals through the secretin receptor (SCTR), a class B GPCR; RAMP3 is an accessory subunit that typically partners with calcitonin receptor-like receptor (CALCRL) to form adrenomedullin/CGRP receptors, not secretin receptors directly. This pairing is atypical/non-canonical, likely reflecting database inference of RAMP3 co-expression with GPCR ligands rather than a confirmed SCT-RAMP3 binding event in lymphoid stroma/perivascular cells.

short_description: Chaperone-transporter complex; lactate transport supporting metabolically active cells
summary_description: BSG (CD147/Basigin) acts as an obligate chaperone for monocarboxylate transporter SLC16A1 (MCT1), facilitating its plasma membrane trafficking and lactate/pyruvate transport rather than classical ligand-receptor signalling. Both are broadly expressed on proliferating lymphocytes, germinal centre B cells and plasmablasts, supporting glycolytic metabolism; interaction is a chaperone-transporter complex rather than a signalling receptor pair.

short_description: Growth factor-proteoglycan; PTN signals via SDC1 promoting adhesion/proliferation
summary_description: PTN (pleiotrophin) binds the heparan sulfate proteoglycan SDC1, triggering SDC1 clustering and downstream signalling (e.g. via PTPRZ1 co-receptor pathways) that modulates adhesion, migration and proliferation. In lymphoid tissue, PTN is produced by stromal/follicular cells while SDC1 (CD138) marks plasma cells and some stromal/epithelial cells, so this axis is relevant to plasma cell niches in medullary cords and bone marrow-like microenvironments. The interaction is plausible but relatively weakly characterized in secondary lymphoid organs compared to classic cytokine axes.

short_description: Chemokine-receptor; recruits activated T cells/NK cells to inflamed sites
summary_description: CXCL10 (IP-10) is a canonical CXCR3 ligand; binding activates Gi-coupled signalling driving chemotaxis. CXCL10 is secreted by stromal cells, macrophages and dendritic cells (often IFN-γ induced), while CXCR3 is expressed on activated Th1 cells, CD8 T cells and NK cells, guiding their recruitment into T-cell zones and inflamed germinal centres. This is a well-supported, canonical signalling pair.

short_description: Notch ligand-receptor; drives T-cell lineage commitment and differentiation
summary_description: DLL1 is a transmembrane Notch ligand that engages NOTCH1 via juxtacrine contact, triggering gamma-secretase cleavage and nuclear translocation of NICD to activate transcription. In lymphoid tissue DLL1 is expressed by stromal/endothelial cells (e.g. thymic/marginal reticular cells) while NOTCH1 is on T-lineage progenitors and some B cells, supporting T-cell development and marginal zone B-cell differentiation. This is a canonical, well-supported juxtacrine interaction.

short_description: Adhesion ligand-integrin; retains intraepithelial/resident lymphocytes in epithelium
summary_description: E-cadherin (CDH1) on epithelial cells binds the integrin αEβ7 (ITGAE_ITGB7, CD103/β7) expressed on intraepithelial lymphocytes, tissue-resident memory T cells and some dendritic cells, mediating retention and adhesion. In lymphoid organs this is most relevant at epithelial interfaces (e.g. tonsillar crypt epithelium, gut-associated lymphoid tissue) rather than core follicular/T-zone stroma. This is a well-established, canonical adhesion axis for tissue residency.

short_description: Intracellular phosphatase misannotated as ligand; likely database artefact
summary_description: PTPN11 (SHP2) is a cytoplasmic protein tyrosine phosphatase with no secreted or membrane-ligand form, so it cannot act as an extracellular ligand for FCRL4, a surface Fc receptor-like protein on memory/marginal-zone and mucosal B cells. This pairing is very likely a database/annotation artefact arising from co-expression or interaction-database mining rather than a genuine ligand-receptor signalling event, and should be treated with caution.

short_description: Neuropeptide-adrenergic receptor; likely cross-reactive/non-canonical pairing, weak support
summary_description: ADCYAP1 (PACAP) is a neuropeptide that normally signals through its cognate receptors PAC1R/VIPR1/VIPR2, not the adrenergic receptor ADRB2, which is the receptor for catecholamines (adrenaline/noradrenaline). Any detected spatial correlation likely reflects co-expression of neuro-immune modulatory genes (e.g. sympathetic nerve fibres near stroma/HEV) rather than direct receptor engagement; this pair is non-canonical and weakly supported mechanistically.

short_description: Mismatched cytokine-receptor; CSF1 does not bind CSF2RA, likely artefact
summary_description: CSF1 (M-CSF) canonically signals through CSF1R, not CSF2RA, which is the alpha subunit of the GM-CSF (CSF2) receptor; there is no established direct binding between CSF1 and CSF2RA. CSF1 is produced by stromal/macrophage lineages and CSF2RA is on myeloid progenitors/macrophages/DCs, so co-expression in myeloid niches may explain a spurious spatial correlation rather than genuine signalling; this pairing is non-canonical/likely a database artefact.

short_description: Laminin-integrin; basement membrane adhesion, muscle/stromal context mainly
summary_description: Laminin α5 (LAMA5) is a basement membrane component that can bind α7β1 integrin (ITGA7_ITGB1), classically mediating adhesion in muscle and some stromal/vascular basement membranes, supporting cell attachment and tissue architecture. In lymphoid organs, LAMA5 is produced by stromal/endothelial basement membranes (e.g. HEV, reticular fibres) while ITGA7 expression is largely restricted to myocytes/pericytes, making this a plausible but low-abundance, non-canonical interaction for lymphoid immune cells specifically.

short_description: Osteopontin-integrin; promotes leukocyte adhesion and migration in stroma
summary_description: SPP1 (osteopontin) binds α9β1 integrin (ITGA9_ITGB1), activating adhesion and migratory signalling important for leukocyte trafficking and tissue remodelling. SPP1 is secreted by macrophages, dendritic cells and stromal/reticular cells in lymphoid tissue, while ITGA9β1 is expressed on neutrophils and some lymphocytes/endothelium, supporting cell recruitment within medullary and perivascular niches. This is a reasonably well-supported, moderately canonical adhesion axis.

short_description: Secreted glycoprotein-integrin subunit; weak/non-canonical stromal adhesion signal
summary_description: CLEC11A (osteolectin) is a secreted C-type lectin domain factor mainly characterized as a growth factor for mesenchymal/osteogenic progenitors; a direct, well-validated interaction with the integrin subunit ITGB1 alone (not a specific α/β heterodimer) is not firmly established. ITGB1 is broadly expressed across stromal, endothelial and immune cells, so this pairing likely reflects a promiscuous/generic integrin-subunit database entry rather than a validated, specific ligand-receptor signalling event.

short_description: Intracellular protease, not surface ligand, for NOTCH1; database artefact
summary_description: PSEN1 (presenilin-1) is the catalytic component of the gamma-secretase complex that cleaves NOTCH1 intracellularly after ligand (e.g. DLL/JAG) engagement; it is not itself a secreted or membrane-bound ligand for NOTCH1. This pairing represents a mechanistic/pathway component mislabelled as a ligand-receptor pair and should be flagged as a likely database/annotation artefact rather than genuine intercellular signalling.

short_description: R-spondin-syndecan; modulates Wnt signalling in stromal niches
summary_description: RSPO3 potentiates canonical Wnt/β-catenin signalling and can engage syndecan-4 (SDC4) as a co-receptor alongside LGR4/5, enhancing Wnt pathway activity in stromal niche maintenance. In lymphoid organs, RSPO3 is produced by niche fibroblastic reticular/stromal cells and SDC4 is broadly expressed on stromal and some immune cells, supporting stromal self-renewal and tissue architecture; this is a plausible but less-canonical RSPO co-receptor interaction compared to LGR4/5 binding.

short_description: Adhesion molecule-CD43 axis; weak/alternative ligand for leukocyte adhesion
summary_description: ICAM1 is the canonical ligand for integrin LFA-1 (ITGAL_ITGB2); SPN (CD43, sialophorin) is a heavily glycosylated anti-adhesive mucin on leukocytes that has been reported to bind ICAM1 in some contexts but is far less established than the LFA-1 axis and CD43 is more often anti-adhesive. ICAM1 is expressed on HEV/stromal/APCs and SPN broadly on leukocytes/T cells; this pairing is non-canonical/weakly supported relative to the primary ICAM1-integrin interaction.

short_description: Matrix protein-ecto-enzyme; indirect/non-canonical, NT5E is adenosine-generating enzyme
summary_description: Fibronectin (FN1) is an ECM glycoprotein that signals mainly through integrins, not NT5E (CD73), which is a GPI-anchored ecto-5'-nucleotidase generating immunosuppressive adenosine from AMP; there is no established direct ligand-receptor binding between FN1 and NT5E. FN1 is made by stromal/fibroblastic reticular cells and CD73 marks stromal cells, Tregs and some endothelium, so co-expression in stromal niches likely drives a spurious database-derived spatial correlation rather than true signalling.

short_description: Lymphangiogenic VEGFC–integrin β1; non-canonical, weakly validated
summary_description: VEGFC signals mainly through VEGFR3 (FLT4), with VEGFR2 and the co-receptor NRP2; direct functional binding to the generic ITGB1 subunit is weakly validated (integrin α9β1 binds VEGFC/D). VEGFC comes from stromal/perivascular cells near lymphatic sinuses, and ITGB1 is ubiquitous. Interpret as a lymphatic-niche co-localisation signal, not a definitive receptor event.

short_description: Chemokine-receptor; recruits monocytes/macrophages, memory T cells
summary_description: CCL5 (RANTES) binds the GPCR CCR1, triggering Gi-mediated chemotaxis. In lymphoid tissue CCL5 is produced by T cells, macrophages, FRCs and platelets, while CCR1 is expressed on monocytes/macrophages, DCs, and some memory T/NK cells; the axis helps recruit myeloid and memory lymphocyte populations into inflamed or perivascular areas.

short_description: Non-canonical; intracellular/secreted peptidase pairing is a database artefact
summary_description: NUCB2 (nesfatin-1 precursor) is a secreted/Golgi protein and ERAP1 is an ER-resident aminopeptidase that trims peptides for MHC-I loading; neither functions as a bona fide ligand-receptor signalling pair. This is almost certainly a database artefact arising from co-expression/correlation rather than a true receptor interaction, and has no established role in lymphoid organ architecture.

short_description: Growth factor-receptor; lymphangiogenesis/angiogenesis signalling via VEGFR1
summary_description: VEGFC can bind FLT1 (VEGFR1) with lower affinity than its primary receptors FLT4/KDR, activating tyrosine kinase signalling for angiogenesis and monocyte chemotaxis. VEGFC is produced by stromal/FRC and lymphatic endothelial cells, while FLT1 is expressed on blood vascular endothelium and monocytes/macrophages, supporting vascular remodeling near lymphoid stroma. This pairing is weaker/secondary compared to VEGFC-FLT4 signalling.

short_description: ECM glycoprotein-integrin; mediates leukocyte adhesion and migration
summary_description: SPON2 (mindin) is an ECM/extracellular matrix glycoprotein that engages integrin alpha4 (as part of ITGA4_ITGB1 or ITGA4_ITGB7 heterodimers), promoting leukocyte adhesion and migration. SPON2 is produced by stromal/endothelial cells, while ITGA4-containing integrins are expressed on lymphocytes and myeloid cells, supporting trafficking into lymphoid tissue parenchyma and across HEVs.

short_description: Ephrin-Eph; contact-dependent cell adhesion/repulsion signalling
summary_description: EFNA1 (GPI-anchored ephrin-A ligand) binds EPHB6, a kinase-dead Eph receptor that signals via adaptor recruitment rather than catalytic activity, mediating cell-cell contact-dependent adhesion/repulsion and migration guidance. EFNA1 is expressed on stromal/endothelial cells and EPHB6 on T cells and dendritic cells, potentially contributing to lymphocyte positioning, though this cross-subclass pairing (ephrin-A/EphB) is atypical and less well characterized functionally.

short_description: Non-canonical; intracellular G-protein subunit miscast as ligand
summary_description: GNAI2 is an intracellular heterotrimeric G-protein alpha subunit that transduces signals downstream of GPCRs like F2R (PAR1, a thrombin receptor); it is not a secreted/surface ligand and cannot bind F2R extracellularly. This pairing is a database/algorithmic artefact reflecting intracellular signalling co-association rather than a genuine ligand-receptor interaction.

short_description: Growth factor-receptor; weak cross-reactivity, canonical receptor is ERBB3/4
summary_description: NRG1 (neuregulin-1) primarily signals through ERBB3/ERBB4 and heterodimers with EGFR/ERBB2, with direct EGFR binding being weak/indirect; signalling activates RTK/MAPK-PI3K pathways. In lymphoid tissue, NRG1 can be produced by stromal cells, with EGFR expressed on epithelial and some stromal/myeloid cells; this specific NRG1-EGFR pairing is non-canonical and likely reflects heterodimer-context association rather than direct high-affinity binding.

short_description: Non-canonical; POMC-derived peptides don't directly ligate RAMP3
summary_description: POMC is a precursor cleaved into peptides (ACTH, MSH, beta-endorphin) that signal through melanocortin receptors (MC1R-MC5R), not RAMPs; RAMP3 is an accessory subunit that modulates calcitonin-receptor-like receptor (CLR) responses to adrenomedullin/CGRP. This pairing is likely a database artefact without direct evidence of POMC peptides binding RAMP3 in lymphoid tissue.

short_description: Non-canonical; PSEN1 is intracellular gamma-secretase, not a ligand
summary_description: PSEN1 is the catalytic component of the gamma-secretase complex that cleaves NOTCH2 intracellularly after ligand (e.g., DLL/JAG) engagement, releasing NICD for nuclear signalling; it is not a secreted ligand itself. This is a mechanistic/pathway association misclassified as ligand-receptor, reflecting PSEN1's role in processing NOTCH2 rather than direct extracellular binding - a database artefact.

short_description: Growth factor-receptor complex; drives lymphangiogenesis in lymphatic endothelium
summary_description: VEGFC binds the FLT4 (VEGFR3)/KDR (VEGFR2) heterodimer, its primary high-affinity receptor complex, activating lymphangiogenic signalling. VEGFC is secreted by FRCs, DCs, and macrophages, while FLT4_KDR is expressed on lymphatic endothelial cells lining sinuses and lymphatics, driving lymphatic vessel growth/maintenance critical for fluid drainage and lymphocyte egress from lymph nodes.

short_description: Non-canonical; intracellular G-protein subunit miscast as ligand for EGFR
summary_description: GNAI2 is an intracellular heterotrimeric G-protein alpha subunit involved in downstream GPCR signal transduction and is not a secreted or membrane ligand capable of engaging the receptor tyrosine kinase EGFR. This pairing is a database/algorithmic artefact arising from intracellular signalling co-expression rather than genuine extracellular ligand-receptor engagement.

short_description: Non-canonical; CCL19's canonical receptor is CCR7, not CCR10
summary_description: CCL19 is a CCR7 ligand driving T cell/DC homing to T zones via HEVs and stromal/FRC conduits; CCR10 is the receptor for CCL27/CCL28, mediating skin/mucosal and IgA plasmablast homing. This CCL19-CCR10 pairing is non-canonical/weakly supported and likely reflects promiscuous low-affinity binding or a database artefact rather than a physiologically dominant axis.

short_description: Non-canonical; complement C3 ligates complement receptors, not CD19 directly
summary_description: Complement C3 fragments (e.g., C3d) are recognized by CR2 (CD21), which forms a co-receptor complex with CD19 on B cells to lower the BCR activation threshold; C3 does not bind CD19 directly. This pairing likely reflects the CD19-CD21 co-receptor complex context in germinal centre/follicular B cells rather than a direct C3-CD19 interaction - a database simplification.

short_description: Non-canonical; TRAF2 is an intracellular adaptor, not a receptor
summary_description: TNF signals through surface receptors TNFR1/TNFR2, which recruit the intracellular adaptor TRAF2 to activate downstream NF-kB/MAPK signalling; TRAF2 itself is cytoplasmic and cannot bind extracellular TNF directly. This is a pathway-adjacent association rather than a true ligand-receptor pair, reflecting a database artefact from intracellular signalling co-involvement.

short_description: Non-canonical; PTPN6 (SHP-1) is an intracellular phosphatase, not a ligand
summary_description: PTPN6 (SHP-1) is a cytoplasmic protein tyrosine phosphatase recruited to the ITIM motifs of inhibitory receptors like CD300LF (an inhibitory receptor on myeloid cells binding phosphatidylserine/ceramide) to dampen signalling; it is not a secreted/surface ligand. This pairing is a database artefact reflecting intracellular downstream signalling association rather than genuine extracellular ligand-receptor binding.

short_description: Intracellular GTPase-effector; likely database artefact, not true LR pair
summary_description: ARF6 is a cytosolic small GTPase that activates PLD1 at membranes to regulate vesicular trafficking and lipid signalling, not a secreted/surface ligand-receptor event. Neither protein is a canonical extracellular signalling pair in lymphoid stroma or immune cells. This listing is best interpreted as a database artefact from intracellular PPI data misclassified as ligand-receptor.

short_description: Matrix metalloproteinase-growth factor receptor; ECM remodeling, stromal signalling
summary_description: MMP2 is a secreted/matrix-associated protease that can proteolytically release or modulate ECM-bound FGF ligands and may directly engage FGFR1, contributing to stromal remodeling and angiogenic signalling rather than classical ligand-receptor activation. In lymphoid tissue, MMP2 is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells (FRC), endothelium and macrophages, while FGFR1 is expressed on stromal/endothelial cells supporting vascular and stromal niche remodeling. This interaction is weakly supported mechanistically and likely reflects indirect ECM-mediated crosstalk rather than direct high-affinity binding.

short_description: Complement regulator-adhesion GPCR; leukocyte-stromal adhesion and activation
summary_description: CD55 (DAF) is a GPI-anchored complement decay-accelerating factor that also serves as a ligand for the adhesion GPCR ADGRE5 (CD97), triggering adhesion and costimulatory signalling upon binding. CD55 is broadly expressed on stromal, epithelial and hematopoietic cells including FRCs and FDCs, while ADGRE5/CD97 is expressed on myeloid cells, activated T/B lymphocytes and granulocytes, mediating leukocyte-stromal and leukocyte-leukocyte adhesion important for immune cell positioning and activation in lymphoid tissue.

short_description: VEGF-receptor complex; drives angiogenesis and HEV/vascular remodeling
summary_description: VEGFA binds the FLT1 (VEGFR1)/KDR (VEGFR2) receptor complex to activate receptor tyrosine kinase signalling, promoting endothelial proliferation, permeability and angiogenesis. Ligand is produced by stromal cells, macrophages and some lymphocytes, while receptors are expressed on blood endothelium including high endothelial venules (HEV) and lymphatic endothelium, supporting vascular remodeling and lymphocyte trafficking into lymphoid organs. This is a canonical, well-supported angiogenic signalling axis.

short_description: Matrix proteoglycan-TLR2; damage-associated innate immune activation
summary_description: Versican (VCAN), a large ECM proteoglycan, can act as a damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) engaging TLR2 to trigger NF-kB-driven innate inflammatory signalling rather than a classical high-affinity ligand-receptor pair. VCAN is produced by fibroblastic reticular cells and other stromal fibroblasts in lymphoid tissue, while TLR2 is expressed on macrophages, dendritic cells and some B cells, contributing to innate sensing of stromal matrix remodeling/damage. Evidence for direct, specific VCAN-TLR2 engagement is moderate and context-dependent, so this pairing should be treated cautiously.

short_description: Angiopoietin-like-syndecan; vascular/stromal adhesion and lipid metabolism signalling
summary_description: ANGPTL4 is a secreted angiopoietin-like protein that binds heparan sulfate proteoglycans like syndecan-2 (SDC2), modulating endothelial permeability, lipid metabolism and integrin-mediated adhesion rather than classical kinase receptor activation. In lymphoid tissue, ANGPTL4 can be produced by stromal/endothelial cells and macrophages under hypoxic or metabolic stress, while SDC2 is expressed on stromal fibroblasts and some endothelium, supporting ECM organization and vascular barrier function. This is a moderately supported, non-classical proteoglycan-based interaction.
